authors.institution: The Catholic University of Korea Bucheon St. Mary's Hospital

papers.title: Neural networks and games
papers.abstract: Hopfield neural networks and noncooperative games provide seemingly different approaches to understanding how collective outcomes emerge from local interactions. In a neural network, individual units adjust their states according to local signals; in a game, players choose actions to maximise individual payoffs. I establish an exact equivalence between symmetric binary Hopfield networks and binary-action games that admit a quadratic potential. The equivalence identifies stable network configurations with pure-strategy Nash equilibria, and asynchronous neural updating with best-response dynamics. More broadly, the storage and retrieval of memories in neural networks correspond, respectively, to the design and selection of equilibria in games.

papers.title: ModelBlaster: Closing the Performance Gap through Learning-Augmented Agents Across Models, Kernels and Hardware Backends
papers.abstract:
Optimizing accelerator code across hardware architectures is difficult. ML compilers search predefined spaces of schedules and micro-kernels, while LLM-guided optimization can explore alternative algorithms, operator decompositions, and hardware-specific techniques. However, existing LLM agents typically target a single programming interface, toolchain, or accelerator family, focus on kernel-level optimization without model-level transforms, and offer limited reuse of experience across hardware targets.
  We present ModelBlaster, a Memory-Augmented In-Context Reinforcement Learning (MAIC-RL) framework for optimizing data-parallel kernels and whole models across heterogeneous SIMD and SIMT accelerators. Its mutable policy is a persistent knowledge base updated at inference time by Actor-Critic Textual Gradient Descent (AC-TGD). The knowledge base maps performance states to actions, outcomes, and constraints, enabling experience reuse across kernels, models, and hardware targets. A model-level optimizer uses kernel-level knowledge to inform whole-model decisions. The same optimization loop and knowledge schema support CUDA on NVIDIA GPUs, OpenCL on Qualcomm GPUs, and RVV intrinsics on RISC-V vector cores, with only lowering and measurement layers specific to each target.
  Compared with PyTorch, ModelBlaster achieves geometric-mean speedups of 1.85x, 5.58x, and 5.18x on KernelBench Levels 1, 2, and 3, and 1.69x on SOL-ExecBench Levels 1 and 2 on a B200 GPU. On Qualcomm Adreno GPUs, it achieves 5.8x over the vendor SDK and 1.7x over Apache TVM; on RISC-V vector cores, it achieves 2.7x over ExecuTorch with XNNPACK across 70 KernelBench problems.

papers.title: Positional Encoding is All You Need for Scalable Equivariance Constraint Relaxation
papers.abstract: Equivariant neural networks incorporate known symmetries of the data, such as permutations, rotations, or translations, directly into their architecture, often improving sample efficiency and generalization. However, strict equivariance can make optimization difficult, for example, when the data only approximately satisfy the assumed symmetry, or when the equivariance constraints induce a challenging loss landscape. Recent studies have shown that relaxing equivariance during training by introducing non-equivariant dense linear layers can ease optimization in such cases and improve the performance of the resulting strictly equivariant model, after removing the relaxation layers at test time. While effective, this approach incurs a significant computational overhead, limiting its applicability in scalable architectures. In this work, we propose a more efficient constraint-relaxation method based on positional encoding (PE). Our framework injects a positional encoding with learnable scale that breaks the model's original symmetry. This positional signal is gradually annealed to zero, recovering the original equivariant model by the end of training. Empirically, we demonstrate significant improvements for translational and rotational equivariant models with only marginal compute and memory overhead.

papers.title: ELA: End-to-End Latent Action Policy Learning from Video Demonstrations
papers.abstract: Robot imitation learning is limited by the scarcity of action-labeled data, while action-free demonstrations such as videos are abundant. Recent latent-action methods learn action-relevant representations from observation transitions, but they do not optimize latent actions for downstream control, leading to latent representations that are difficult for policies to model and difficult to accurately decode into continuous robot actions. This paper introduces ELA, an end-to-end framework for learning from video demonstrations via latent actions jointly optimized for policy learning and action decoding. ELA jointly trains a latent action model, latent action policy, and action decoder, enabling policies to leverage abundant video data with only a handful of action-labeled robot demonstrations. Experiments on simulated and real-world manipulation tasks show that ELA consistently outperforms prior latent action baselines. Moreover, it integrates seamlessly with existing imitation learning methods through lightweight 4M-parameter action decoders, requiring no changes to policy architectures or training objectives. Additional materials can be found on: https://end2end-latent-action.github.io/

papers.title: NanoKV: High-Ratio KV Cache Compression for Autoregressive Video Generation
papers.abstract: Autoregressive video models rely on historical key-value (KV) caches to preserve scene consistency over extended rollouts, making KV storage and repeated attention over history a growing memory and computational bottleneck. Aggressive compression can degrade generation quality, while reconstructing full-dimensional KV leaves attention computation largely unchanged. We introduce NanoKV, a frozen-backbone framework for generation-aware high-ratio KV compression. NanoKV exploits redundancy across tokens and attention heads by storing shared content in cluster centers and encoding joint head-channel residuals into low-bit coefficients. Crucially, NanoKV uses different fitting objectives for Keys and Values according to their distinct roles in attention: Key decoders are optimized to preserve downstream block outputs, whereas Value encoders and decoders are fitted for faithful reconstruction through the deployed quantization path. Building on the same compressed representation, the optional NanoKV-Fast variant reuses the stored coefficients for mixed-dimensional attention, reducing computation without modifying the video backbone. Across three autoregressive video backbones, NanoKV consistently improves the quality-storage trade-off. On HY-WorldPlay, NanoKV achieves $26.09\times$ effective KV compression, nearly twice that of KVTC, while improving PSNR by 1.0 dB. NanoKV-Fast retains $20.53\times$ effective compression and achieves an approximately $1.15\times$ end-to-end speedup over KVTC.

authors.name: Haoyi Zhu
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: cuRoboV2-Fast: Fast Torque-Limited Collision-Free Motion Planning
papers.abstract: We present cuRoboV2-Fast, a GPU-accelerated planner that reduces both planning latency and execution time for collision-free, payload-aware, torque-limited motions. B-spline trajectory optimization reduces the required iterations, while accelerated robot computations and differentiable inverse dynamics reduce refinement cost and accommodate changing payloads. TimeOpt optimizes traversal speed along the fixed path under sampled velocity, acceleration, jerk, and torque constraints, exploiting local spline support to solve banded Newton systems efficiently on the GPU. With a 3,kg payload, cuRoboV2-Fast achieves 4.4 ms mean planning time on RTX 5090, 14.7x faster than cuRoboV2. Our method on Jetson AGX Orin plans faster than cuRoboV1 + TOPPRA on RTX 5090. A stereo-camera-based deployment on YAM achieves 5.93 s mean completed pick-and-drop cycles, 34.6% shorter than cuRoboV2. Code (Apache 2.0): www.github.com/NVlabs/curobo , Project Page: www.research.nvidia.com/labs/lpr/curobov2-fast .

papers.title: A Hybrid Approach for Automated Security Pattern Recovery
papers.abstract: Security-by-design emphasises integrating security into software design and development. Security pattern catalogues operationalise this principle by prescribing reusable architectural solutions to recurring security problems. However, recovering their implementations from source code remains challenging because security patterns are abstract, span multiple components, and admit many valid implementations. We present SecPatRec, a hybrid approach for automated security pattern recovery from source code repositories. We treat a security pattern as a reference architecture and frame its recovery as a deductive task: determining which prescribed roles are present, grounding them in code entities, and recovering their interaction sequences. SecPatRec pairs a ReAct-style LLM agent equipped with semantic and lexical code search for role detection and grounding with static code property graph analysis for interaction recovery. We curate a human-validated ground-truth dataset of 100 pattern instances covering five security patterns across 93 open-source Java and Python repositories, and introduce a three-level evaluation framework measuring recovery correctness against this ground truth. We evaluate SecPatRec using four LLMs, including proprietary and open-source models. Averaged over all models and pattern instances, SecPatRec achieves role-detection accuracy of 0.84, role-grounding similarity of 0.84, and an interaction-recovery score of 0.66. Compared to a one-shot end-to-end LLM baseline, SecPatRec achieves higher aggregate recovery scores and lower estimated LLM API costs per run, while processing repositories that exceed the baseline's configured input limit. The recovered role mappings and statically derived interaction sequences provide structural and behavioural evidence that can support inspection of security-pattern implementations.

authors.name: Tuan Dat Tran
authors.institution: Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City

papers.title: From Continuum-Kinematics-Inspired Peridynamics to Simplicial Hyperelasticity
papers.abstract:
We develop a variational and functional-analytic framework for continuum-kinematics-inspired peridynamics with simultaneous nonlocal interactions among multiple points. We encode the finite-difference data of each interacting simplex in a simplicial deformation gradient. For nondegenerate simplices in three dimensions, the gradient, its cofactor, and its determinant encode the associated continuum-kinematics-inspired peridynamic line, area, and volume changes, respectively. This unified representation leads to a class of simplicial hyperelastic energies with general, possibly nonadditive, constitutive dependence on the affine deformation of an interacting simplex, thereby extending the original continuum-kinematics-inspired peridynamic framework.
  To describe interactions occurring at different scales and over different simplex geometries, we introduce radial- and shape-weighted nonlocal spaces. Their multipoint seminorms control two-point energies induced by the edge marginals of the interaction measure. This comparison yields nonlocal Poincar\'e inequalities and fractional Sobolev embeddings.
  We establish existence of equilibrium configurations by two complementary mechanisms. Particle-wise averaged convexity yields weak lower semicontinuity of the associated energy functionals. Under stronger assumptions on the edge marginals, fractional compactness gives existence for nonconvex energy densities. These results provide a mathematical foundation for simplicial and continuum-kinematics-inspired peridynamic models.

papers.title: Risk-Sensitive Stochastic Optimal Control on Positive Cones
papers.abstract: We consider stochastic optimal control problems in which the state is constrained to a proper cone. Specifically, we consider risk-neutral, risk-averse, and risk-seeking formulations within a single entropic-risk framework. We investigate classes of problems whose Bellman operator preserves affine functions and characterize their optimal value functions and feedback policies for both finite-horizon and time-average infinite-horizon problems. Additionally, we establish convergence and state-bound results under finite-step cost observability. Moreover, we demonstrate an exact connection between entropic-risk optimal control on proper cones and deterministic infsup control for systems whose dynamics and stage costs are affine in the disturbances. In addition, we provide examples of classes of systems for which explicit solutions can be obtained.

papers.title: DualCast: Dual-Image Conditioned Diffusion Transformers for Digital Human E-Commerce Video Generation
papers.abstract: Digital human e-commerce video generation requires preserving product appearance, human identity, and overall video style during dynamic demonstrations. Although recent models support multiple reference images, their general conditioning schemes do not explicitly distinguish the asymmetric roles of "what is presented" and "who presents it." Consequently, generated videos may favor a single reference, resulting in product distortion, identity drift, or single-reference collapse. To address this issue, we propose DualCast, a role-addressed dual-image conditioning framework for video generation. By explicitly modeling the distinct roles of product and human conditions, DualCast reduces role ambiguity and feature competition between references. First, a dual-spatiotemporal slot injection mechanism VAE-encodes the product and human images separately and places their latent features at the front and rear boundaries of the DiT sequence, enabling sequence-level condition separation and directed injection. Second, a mask-guided region-weighted loss strengthens supervision over product, face, and product-face overlap regions, improving generation fidelity in critical areas. Third, image condition dropout enables a single model to support dual-image, product-only, and human-only generation. In addition, we construct a curated dataset of 10K e-commerce videos for model training. Experimental results demonstrate the strong performance of DualCast.

papers.title: iGC: Antibody Optimization via Reinforcement Learning over a Learned Somatic Hypermutation Prior
papers.abstract:
Antibody affinity maturation is a natural optimization process in which B cells acquire mutations through somatic hypermutation (SHM), undergo selection for improved antigen binding, and iteratively evolve toward higher affinity. Computationally modeling this process requires capturing both biologically plausible mutations and antigen-specific selection. However, existing mutation models do not directly optimize binding, while affinity optimization often neglects realistic mutation trajectories.
  We introduce iGC (in silico Germinal Centers), a two-stage reinforcement learning (RL) framework for antigen-specific antibody optimization. Stage 1 learns an SHM mutation prior from parent-child pairs in B-cell lineage trees and adapts it to a target affinity-maturation dataset. Stage 2 initializes an RL policy from this prior and optimizes antigen binding with Kullback-Leibler (KL) regularization toward the frozen prior. To prevent reward exploitation, including repetitive high-reward substitutions and structurally tolerated framework mutations, we introduce a Reward-Tax Meta-Gradient objective. RewardNet smooths the affinity landscape, while TaxNet penalizes reward overexploitation, jointly defining a learned meta-reward for policy optimization.
  We evaluate iGC on mutation prediction, SHM consistency, affinity optimization, and mutation diversity. The mutation prior more than doubles the strongest baseline in mutation-site prediction. Following RL optimization, iGC maintains SHM sequence structure. It also achieves a strong exploration-exploitation balance, yielding competitive reward-diversity products across candidate-selection cutoffs. These results demonstrate that iGC integrates biologically plausible mutation generation with antigen-specific affinity selection, providing an in silico framework for iterative antibody affinity maturation.

authors.name: Andrew Leaver-Fay
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: Agnostic Learning by Imitating
papers.abstract: Given a class of machine learning models and sample access to a data distribution with binary labels, which computational task is harder: training a discriminative model that distinguishes positive and negative labels as well as the best member of the class, or training a generative model whose outputs are indistinguishable from real data by all members of the class? We prove that these two fundamental tasks in computational learning theory are not just closely related, but actually equivalent to each other in complexity. One direction of this equivalence was previously known. Indeed, the powerful regularity lemma in complexity theory gives an efficient oracle reduction from the indistinguishability task (a.k.a. multiaccuracy) to the distinguishing task (a.k.a. agnostic learning) in the style of boosting algorithms. Our main contribution is an efficient oracle reduction in the other direction. Taking this idea further, we show that a multiaccuracy oracle is a remarkably powerful primitive, achieving not just agnostic learning but also a wide range of seemingly more demanding learning objectives via similarly efficient and direct constructions. Our results crucially use the power of making adaptive queries to the oracle, and stand in stark contrast to prior work, which showed that post-processing a single multiaccurate predictor is insufficient for even weak forms of learning. On a technical level, we draw a connection between our (offline) problem and a version of no-regret learning in the online setting, which allows us to use follow-the-leader type algorithms to modify the label distribution and aggregate the predictions of the multiaccuracy oracle.

papers.title: Scheduling Data to Compute: Hierarchical Data Pipelining for LLM Training on AMD GPUs
papers.abstract:
Large language models (LLM) have been the key focus of recent machine learning breakthroughs. As the model size grows exponentially, the computation needed for training is astronomical. A GPU can do a huge amount of arithmetic. However, the data its compute units need is not always available when they are ready. This data may still be in slow memory or on another GPU. While the chip waits, expensive compute sits idle, and at scale even a small drop in utilization translates into substantial cost. In this paper, we treat this waiting time as the primary bottleneck. We focus on hardware features designed for explicit data movement. These features load data from off-chip memory onto the chip, rearrange it into the layout the computation requires as it is loaded, and transfer it between GPUs. By orchestrating them, we keep a steady pipeline of data flowing to the compute units so that they remain busy.
  We present kernel and framework implementations that address this bottleneck using three key data-movement instructions and hardware features. The Tensor Data Mover (TDM) moves tensor data from high-bandwidth memory (HBM) into on-chip memory. Transpose-load instructions transpose tensor data into the layout that LLM computations require as it is loaded on-chip. Finally, System DMA (SDMA) and Remote DMA (RDMA) move data between GPUs over the scale-up and scale-out networks, respectively. Our results show that TDM and transpose-load provide on average 1.88x and 1.19x speedup at the kernel level, respectively. The SDMA and RDMA lead to on average 1.16x and 1.33x speedup for computation overlapped with communication. This is the first AMD LLM training system to utilize all the GPU data pipelining features. Our implementation has been integrated into open source framework and library for AMD GPUs. https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus-Turbo https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Primus

papers.title: Shifts in Rossby wave regimes via the change of group velocity with zonal jets
papers.abstract: Evidences show it is questionable to use the trends in Rossby wave phase speed (Cpx) to interpret the relation between the changes of extreme events and westerly jets. We propose, by using 70 years (1954-2023) of ERA5 reanalysis, that the trends in extremes are associated with the shifts of Rossby wave regimes, via the westerly-induced changes in Rossby wave group velocity (Cgx), which are two to three times larger than those in Cpx. We find significant deceleration in the subtropics and polar regions, alongside a salient midlatitude acceleration, of Rossby wave Cgx, especially over the East Asia-Pacific-North America and North Atlantic-Europe sectors. These changes induce robust shifts in spatiotemporal regimes of Rossby waves, from the transient synoptic-scale regime toward the quasi-stationary planetary-scale wave regime where Cgx decelerates, and vice versa. The CESM2 Large Ensemble confirms that the observed pattern over the Eurasia-Pacific-North America sector is a forced response to external forcing, while uncertainties remain over the polar regions and the North Atlantic. We suggest that westerly trends may reshape the regimes of extratropical Rossby wave activity and extreme weather events through the changes in group velocity rather than phase speed of Rossby waves.

authors.name: Zhixiang Li
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: TestBED: An Open-Source Toolkit for Bayesian Experimental Design
papers.abstract: Bayesian experimental design (BED) is a principled framework for intelligent data acquisition with applications across a wide range of scientific and industrial domains. However, the development and adoption of BED remains hindered by a lack of standardised software and benchmarks. Existing methods are typically implemented in bespoke codebases and evaluated on a small subset of tasks, making methods difficult to apply, compare, or extend. To address this, we present TestBED, a general-purpose, open-source toolkit for Bayesian experimental design. TestBED decomposes the BED process into modular, reusable components spanning tasks, objectives, training mechanisms, policy architectures, and evaluation procedures, together with scalable implementations of core primitives such as expected information gain estimators. We provide a wide range of these components, which can be freely composed, allowing existing methods to be reproduced within a common framework, while also enabling previously unexplored configurations and new methodologies to be easily implemented and evaluated. Using TestBED, we further conduct a large-scale benchmark of contemporary BED methods, including controlled studies of under-appreciated but surprisingly critical methodological choices, such as the importance of time embeddings in design policy architectures. By providing a modular, extensible software foundation and a reproducible benchmarking suite, we hope that TestBED will accelerate methodological research in BED and lower the barrier to its real-world application.

papers.title: ALTO: African and Levantine Tech-Facilitated Gender-Based Violence Corpus
papers.abstract: Tech-facilitated gender based violence (TFGBV) is a pervasive online harm affecting women and gender minority groups through its many direct and covert forms. Current models and annotated datasets for gendered harm detection are dominated by data from, and models trained in, Global North languages. In collaboration with civil society organizations (CSOs) from Jordan, Francophone West Africa, and Kenya, we developed a community-led approach to crowdsource culturally and linguistically relevant instances of TFGBV in Levantine Arabic, African French, and Swahili. We annotated the crowdsourced data using active learning to develop a small but performant dataset (N=3022) called ALTO to improve TFGBV detection in the three languages. Through benchmarking and fine-tuning experiments, we show that existing harmful content detection models show poor TFGBV recall within ALTO and improve with fine-tuning. We found that models often miss covert harms across all languages, while error rates are markedly higher in Swahili. We report the experimental results and release the annotation taxonomy, dataset, and trained models.

papers.title: Matching Random Point Sets with Minimum Distortion
papers.abstract:
How well can two independent random samples from a metric measure space be matched while preserving pairwise distances? Concretely, given two independent copies, each of $n$ points sampled from the space, what is their typical metric distortion as finite $n$-point metric spaces? We prove that the space $[0,1]$ equipped with the uniform measure already exhibits a rich behavior. We show that with high probability the distortion of the two independent samples is $n^{2/3}$ up to polylogarithmic factors.
  The lower bound reflects two competing obstructions. A bijection that maps points close to their original positions or their reflections in $[0,1]$ must expand the smallest gaps, in both directions. On the other hand, we show that large displacement from both the identity and reflection itself forces large distortion. Balancing these obstructions yields the lower-bound exponent $2/3$. For the upper bound, we construct a partial matching of the points that maps each gap between consecutive points of length $d\lesssim n^{-4/3}$ to a pair at distance $\widetilde{O}(dn^{1/3})$, with analogous control in the reverse direction. We then use a delicate multiscale oscillation construction to extend this partial matching to a low-distortion bijection.

papers.title: Within-Family EfficientNet Scaling under Fixed-Resolution Transfer Learning for Spectral-Domain Optical Coherence Tomography Retinal Disease Classification
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: CNNs perform well in retinal disease classification from spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT), but whether EfficientNet's natural-image scaling hierarchy transfers to medical-image transfer learning at fixed resolution remains unclear. This study evaluates EfficientNet-B0-B7 for four-class SD-OCT classification and accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. Methods: Eight ImageNet-pretrained variants (4.05-64.10M instantiated backbone parameters) were evaluated at 224x224 on the Kermany dataset. Grayscale images were replicated to RGB and processed using model-embedded preprocessing and augmentation. Training comprised frozen-backbone head training followed by partial fine-tuning. Metrics covered classification, discrimination, efficiency, and visual analyses. Results: Test accuracy varied non-monotonically from 95.93% (B0) to 96.95% (B1); B7 achieved 96.73%. B1 had the highest accuracy and Drusen F1 (0.8780), while B7 had Drusen F1 of 0.8720 and the highest Drusen recall (0.9177). Drusen had the lowest F1 across all variants and contributed 82.2% of the summed squared deviation in class-specific F1; class ranking remained Normal > CNV > DME > Drusen. The OCT accuracy ranking differed from the reported ImageNet hierarchy, where B7 ranked first. The accuracy-to-parameter ratio fell from 19.82 to 1.48 percentage points per million total parameters. The final train-test gap had a weak, non-significant association with test accuracy (r = 0.26, p = 0.53). Conclusions: Larger EfficientNet variants did not consistently improve SD-OCT classification. B1 achieved the highest accuracy and Drusen F1, whereas B7 showed a secondary accuracy recovery at greater model size and CPU latency, indicating task and protocol dependent scaling effects. As cross-partition duplicates have not been independently audited, results are conditional on the supplied split.

papers.title: MCP-Eco: A Linked Dataset of MCP Servers, Consumers, and Development Activity
papers.abstract: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) enables LLM agents to access external tools and data. Studying its software ecosystem requires connecting server interfaces, the projects that configure these servers, and their development activity. However, this information is scattered across directories, package registries, configuration files, and repository histories. We present MCP-Eco, a relational dataset that integrates these sources and links consumer configuration declarations to candidate server projects. Its frozen release contains 16,880,899 records across 19 Parquet tables, covering 78,302 candidate server projects, 16,165 candidate consuming repositories, and 9,200 configuration declarations. Of these declarations, 5,975 resolve to 5,138 distinct repository-server pairs. The dataset also includes tool, resource, and prompt descriptions, declared dependencies, and associated development records, including pull requests, reviews, issues, and commits. Provenance fields distinguish directory-reported capabilities from those observed through live probing and document discovery sources and declaration-matching methods. These connections support research on MCP interface design, configuration practices, and repository maintenance, while enabling practitioners to inspect tool schemas and existing integration configurations. The dataset and accompanying analysis scripts are publicly available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/mcp-research-alliance/mcp-ecosystem Demo video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N7TqnNneSfU

authors.name: Yutaro Kashiwa
authors.institution: Nara Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Uniqueness of Ricci flows from singular initial data
papers.abstract: We establish uniqueness of Ricci flows with non-negative sectional curvatures and scaling invariant curvature bounds, assuming that the induced distance functions converge to the same initial distance function up to isometry. In the compact case, restricting the size of the initial singular set, we also establish uniqueness under suitable weaker conditions.

papers.title: Existence of Lagrangian Mean Curvature Flow Singularities with Bounded Mean Curvature
papers.abstract: In every dimension $n \ge 3$, we show there exist Lagrangian mean curvature flows that develop neck pinch singularities such that the mean curvature remains uniformly bounded. This follows from a related result that, under a structural assumption on the singularity formation, the mean curvature at small scales near the singularity can be bounded by the Lagrangian angle at outer scales with suitable weights. Applying this result to a subset of the finite-time Lagrangian mean curvature flow singularities constructed in the companion paper [arXiv:2607.03152] and the infinite-time Lagrangian mean curvature flow singularities constructed by Tsai, Wood, and the second-named author [arXiv:2401.02228] then gives examples of both finite-time and infinite-time singularity formation with uniformly bounded mean curvature.

papers.title: Law-Dependent Poisson-Refresh Randomised Feedback Control for Stochastic Systems
papers.abstract: This paper studies a continuous-time probabilistic control problem for stochastic systems in which the feedback law assigns a probability distribution over control inputs. The control is modelled as a law-dependent Poisson-refresh process: it is held constant between refresh times and resampled at Poisson times from a feedback rule depending on the current state and state law. The closed-loop system is therefore formulated as a jump--diffusion for the joint state--control process. The objective is to design the sampling rule by comparing the realised closed-loop system with a prescribed reference description. The cost separates two local terms: a relative-entropy penalty for the instantaneous refresh kernel and a state-side drift-mismatch cost. The state-side term is evaluated at the realised control value and is motivated by a frozen-control Girsanov identity. Under global Lipschitz, moment, and uniform ellipticity assumptions, we prove well-posedness of the closed loop and a dynamic programming principle on the joint state--control law space. For linear data and admissible mean-dependent affine-Gaussian refresh rules, the full joint law need not remain Gaussian, but the first and second moments of the joint state--control process close exactly. This yields a deterministic reduced control problem on moment space, with an explicit running cost, a reduced Hamiltonian, and a verification theorem.

papers.title: Energy-Accumulate-Then-Act Backscatter Communications With Retransmission Under Imperfect Feedback Detection
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a threshold-triggered energy-accumulate-then-act backscatter communication system with retransmission under imperfect feedback detection. Under this system, harvested energy is accumulated across transmission blocks, and the backscatter device switches among different operation modes, including energy harvesting, initial transmission, and retransmission, according to its stored energy and decoded feedback. To characterize the resulting dynamics, the joint evolution of the packet-buffer and stored-energy states is modeled, based on which an embedded Markov chain is constructed to derive the steady-state energy distribution at the beginning of each update cycle. Subsequently, the average age of information (AAoI) is derived from the statistics of the inter-update interval and its correlation with the preceding packet system time, while the packet loss rate (PLR) caused by imperfect feedback detection is also obtained. Simulation results validate the analytical results and reveal that retransmission reduces PLR but may either improve or degrade AAoI, depending on packet-generation energy, data transmission rate, and feedback power. Moreover, lower feedback power shrinks the AAoI-favorable region of retransmission at low transmission rate, whereas the opposite trend emerges at higher rate.

papers.title: Aggregating treatment effects across multiple outcomes
papers.abstract: Researchers often aggregate outcomes to estimate treatment effects on abstract concepts, such as "crime" or "wealth." First, I document that principal component analysis (PCA), inverse variance matrix (IVM) weighting, and standardized averaging (SA) are commonly used but have unexpected shortcomings. PCA can assign negative weights, need not maximize precision, depends on an arbitrary sign normalization, and can have nonstandard asymptotics. Unlike SA, IVM can assign negative weights, but neither necessarily maximizes precision. Second, I develop a statistical decision-theoretic approach that uses mean-squared error to choose nonnegative weights while accounting for outcome quality. I revisit a study on social distancing.

papers.title: The full Kolakoski shift is topologically transitive
papers.abstract: We prove that the full Kolakoski shift---namely, the subshift of all smooth sequences over the alphabet $\{1,2\}$---is topologically transitive. Consequently, we demonstrate the existence of a smooth sequence whose factors are invariant under both reversal and bitwise complementation. As a further application, we prove the existence of arbitrarily long smooth words containing an equal number of occurrences of the symbols $1$ and $2$, providing evidence in support of Keane's conjecture. Our approach leverages the hierarchical structure of the full Kolakoski shift to reimagine the shift action in terms of a self-similar semigroup, which allows techniques from group theory and combinatorics to be applied.

papers.title: Quartic polynomial differential systems with three disjoint invariant circles
papers.abstract: We determine the normal forms of real planar polynomial differential systems of degree at most four with three prescribed pairwise disjoint invariant circles, covering all configurations of their centers. None of the prescribed circles is a limit cycle in the concentric case or in the coaxial case with three distinct centers, where the pairwise radical axes coincide. When exactly two centers coincide, or when the three centers are distinct and collinear and the circles are non-coaxial, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for all three circles to be algebraic limit cycles, which are necessarily hyperbolic. For non-collinear centers, we give explicit necessary and sufficient conditions for all three circles to be periodic orbits and for all three to be hyperbolic algebraic limit cycles. Each of the four configurations with non-collinear centers is realized by a coprime quartic polynomial differential system with three hyperbolic circular limit cycles.

papers.title: Analytic two-body density-matrix spectrum of the Fermionic Tonks-Girardeau gas
papers.abstract: The two-body density matrix (TBDM) of a quantum many-body system provides information about particle correlations, e.g., pairing. In this work, we derive the complete spectrum of the TBDM of the fermionic Tonks-Girardeau gas using its exact ground-state wavefunction in second quantization. We obtain analytical expressions for all eigenvalues and eigenvectors for an arbitrary number of particles and identify two different types of eigenstates: collective states, formed by superpositions of paired momentum modes, and single-determinant states. We provide a physical interpretation of this structure, explaining the origin of the different eigenstates and their degeneracies. We further derive an asymptotic expansion for the largest eigenvalue, improving on previous estimates and analytically confirming its linear scaling with the particle number, thereby indicating off-diagonal long-range order. For the high-index collective states, we obtain simpler expressions for the eigenvalues and eigenvectors, showing that the eigenvalues decay as $n^{-4}$ and that the eigenvectors become independent of the number of particles. Finally, we discuss the connection between the collective states and an effective description in terms of composite bosons, whose spectral properties suggest a behavior consistent with Tan's contact for interacting bosonic systems.

authors.name: Francesc Sabater

papers.title: SynMOE: A Syntax-Aware MOE-Guided Approach for PEFT-Based Code Intelligence Learning
papers.abstract: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) has emerged as an important approach for adapting Language Models (LMs) in downstream tasks. However, in the domain of code intelligence, the performance of most PEFT methods relatively drops compared to Full fine-Tuning (FT), hindering their broader applicability. One of the main reasons is that current PEFT methods are generally based on assumptions about the low-rank nature or sparsity of parameter updates, lacking explicit modeling of code-related information. To tackle this limitation, we propose SynMOE, a syntax-aware MOE-guided approach for PEFT on code intelligence learning. Specifically, SynMOE contains two stages: syntactic information extraction and syntax-aware MOE-guided adaptation. It first obtains the syntactic labels of source code from Abstract Syntax Trees (ASTs), and then aligns the labels with the input tokens of code LMs. In the second stage, syntactic labels are integrated into the MOE module, participating in the routing decision of MOE for a more powerful syntactic-aware token representation. We evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed approach by applying it to two typical PEFT methods, LoRA and $(IA)^3$, across three diverse code intelligence tasks. Experimental results show that SynMOE achieves consistent and significant improvements. Even compared to FT, SynMOE achieves comparable or superior performance while being more computationally efficient. In addition, we also conduct ablation studies, hyperparameter analysis, and evaluation in the low-resource scenario to provide a comprehensive investigation of the proposed approach.

papers.title: Towards Automatic Heart Murmur Characterization from Multi-spot Phonocardiograms
papers.abstract: Cardiac auscultation traditionally detects the presence of a heart murmur, but clinicians further characterize it by timing, shape, pitch, quality, and grade. Most automatic phonocardiogram analysis systems stop at binary detection and do not estimate this richer description. In this work, we formulate automatic murmur characterization as five patient-level classification tasks and compare three multi-spot strategies on recordings from the aortic, pulmonary, mitral, and tricuspid auscultation locations. First, classical and deep-learning classifiers are trained independently at each location, and predictions are combined via a maximum-severity late-fusion rule. Second, a synchronous multi-input CNN jointly processes one representative segment per location for a single task. Third, a unified multi-input, multi-output CNN predicts all five attributes from one shared multi-spot representation. Using 735 patients from the CirCor DigiScope dataset with complete four-spot recordings, the best late-fusion configurations reach an unweighted mean sensitivity between 85.56% and 93.81% across the five tasks, with class-specific recalls between 80.00% and 100.00% for every relevant category. The multi-input CNN trails late fusion by 7-16 points depending on the task, while the multi-output model reaches values between 72.59% and 79.40%, estimating all five attributes from one shared representation. We further show that naively balancing training data by adding all minority-class segments degrades patient-level performance under the maximum-severity rule, since it introduces non-representative, noisy segments not filtered by the clustering-based segment selection used for evaluation. These results indicate multi-spot murmur characterization is feasible with both fusion-based and jointly learned architectures, outlining a path toward automatic, structured murmur reports complementing binary screening.

papers.title: Empirical approximation of $L^p$ norms for $p\in (1, 2)$
papers.abstract: For $p\in[1,2]$, we prove uniform moment estimates for weighted sums \[ \sum_{j=1}^m\zeta_jw_j|\langle{\bf v}_j,y\rangle|^p \] of independent subgaussian random variables $\zeta_j$, where the unit vectors $\{{\bf v}_j\}_{j=1}^m$ and nonnegative weights $\{w_j\}_{j=1}^m$ form an isotropic frame. This allows us to obtain optimal sampling discretization of $L_p$ norms for each fixed $p\in[1,2]$. Namely, for an $N$-dimensional space $X_N$ of bounded functions satisfying $\|f\|_\infty\le\sqrt {KN}\,\|f\|_{L_2}$ for every $f\in X_N$, we show that $m\ge C\varepsilon^{-2}KN\log(2N)$ independent samples $\xi^1,\ldots,\xi^m$ provide the discretization \[ (1-\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p}^p \le\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m|f(\xi^j)|^p \le(1+\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p}^p \quad\forall f\in X_N \] with probability at least $1-\exp(-c\frac{m\varepsilon^2}{KN})$. This implies a corresponding weighted discretization result that, for $1<p<2$, improves Talagrand's bound on the dimension $m$ needed to embed $N$-dimensional subspaces of $L_p$ into $\ell_p^m$ with distortion at most $1+\varepsilon$, giving $m\le C\varepsilon^{-2}N\log(2N)$.

papers.title: Vision-Aided Near-Field Channel Estimation for XL-MIMO
papers.abstract: In wideband extremely large-scale MIMO (XLMIMO) systems, the transmitter (TX) is often in the near field of the base station array. The resulting spherical wavefront makes the line-of-sight channel depend on both the TX angle and distance. Existing polar-domain estimators sample both parameters across the entire coverage region, requiring many candidate positions and pilots. This paper proposes a vision aided framework that uses the object carrying the TX, as seen in a camera image, to restrict the candidate positions to a small grid on that object. An on-grid vision-aided coarse localization (V-CL) algorithm obtains a coarse estimate from the grid points that best fit the received pilots, and an off-grid vision-aided Nelder-Mead refinement (V-NMR) algorithm refines it over continuous angle and distance, from which the channel is reconstructed. Simulations show that the proposed algorithms achieve higher accuracy than both wideband and narrowband polar-domain estimators while requiring far fewer pilots and candidate positions.

papers.title: RAGAM-AI: A Hybrid Reinforcement Learning based Agentic approach powered by Generative AI for Edge Resource Management
papers.abstract: Resource management for distributed edge networks hosting different services has been handled efficiently using Reinforcement learning (RL). Reward generalization in complex workflows is still an open issue within the RL realm. Therefore, this work proposes RAGAM-AI, a hybrid framework that combines the capabilities of RL algorithms and Generative-AI (Gen-AI) for powering an Agentic AI workflow that optimizes resource allocation at the Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC) units. This framework further resolves the reward generalization issue by utilizing Large Language Model (LLM) for feedback. A Multi- Agent Soft-Actor Critic (MASAC) using Math{\Sigma}tral as a reward oracle is implemented for managing resource allocations at the MEC. RAGAM-AI interprets system state information and evaluates multi-objective trade-offs guiding the resource orchestration loop over distributed edge server agents. The complexity of the framework is further brought down by incorporating surrogate reward model. The overall performance is evaluated against the single agent SAC, REINFORCE and random policies for benchmarking. On using RAGAM-AI, lower allocation deviations for CPU, memory and bandwidth resources are reported while minimizing the latency and data rate costs. A scalable AI as a feedback (AIAF) solution optimizing network resources with significant performance improvement is thus presented.

papers.title: How Rich is the Rich-Club? Super Rich-Club Organization in Complex Networks
papers.abstract: The rich-club coefficient is used in complex networks to quantify the tendency of progressively higher-degree nodes to be more densely connected than expected by chance. However, it does not capture whether high degree nodes towards the core are actually more interconnected than the original network. Here, we jointly analyze the rich-club coefficient and an enrichment coefficient, which quantifies whether the internal average degree of progressively higher-degree subgraphs is greater than that of the original network, despite the decreasing number of nodes. We apply this framework to real and synthetic networks. Our results reveal three distinct regimes of core organization: rich-club organization without enrichment, enrichment without rich-club organization, and a combination of both, which we call Super Rich-Club organization. In the latter regime, high-degree nodes form cohesive and unusually dense cores that support efficient communication. Our results show that characterizing core organization across structural scales requires considering both relative density and internal connectivity, revealing a stronger form of core organization in real systems with implications for network structure, spectral properties that govern dynamical processes, and communicability.

papers.title: Optimal Marginal Mixing for Transvection-Based Trapdoored Matrices over Large Fields
papers.abstract:
\emph{Trapdoored matrices} are pseudorandom matrices admitting a fast matrix-vector multiplication algorithm given the secret key. We study a candidate family of such matrices: matrices generated by short random \emph{transvection walks} on \(\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)\), whose steps are given by adding a random multiple of a random row of the current state to another.
  We show that the worst-case time for any nonempty set \(\mathcal{S}\subseteq [n]\times[n]\) of matrix entries to come within TV distance \(\varepsilon\leq \frac{1}{4}\) of its stationary marginal under this walk is \(\Theta(|\mathcal{S}|+n\log(n/\varepsilon))\), uniformly over all \(\mathcal{S}\) and \(q\geq Q_\mathrm{all}(n)\). This is asymptotically optimal, and resolves open questions about the mixing times of transvection walks. We derive concrete upper and lower bounds for \(n\geq 256\). Surprisingly, our bounds also hold conditioned on the row-pair structure of the walk, except on a fraction at most \(\varepsilon\) of such structures. This implies that these walks may be pseudorandom even after conditioning on the row-pair structure, and therefore that trapdoored matrices built with these walks may be universal.
  Assuming the conjectured structure-conditioned pseudorandomness of short walks, we exhibit highly efficient, highly parallelizable, and universal trapdoored matrices over \(\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)\), \(\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)\), and \(\mathbb{F}_q^{n\times n}\). The families over \(\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)\) and \(\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)\) admit equally efficient trapdoors for their inverses, making them the first to do so for finite-field trapdoored matrices. We discuss attacks, analyzing one in detail, and lay out directions for further investigation.

papers.title: Beyond the principle-practice gap: Responsible AI as situated epistemic and ethical practice
papers.abstract: Responsible AI scholarship has found that ethical principles are frequently not reflected in AI design and development. Conceptualised as a `gap' between principle and practice, this is framed as a problem of implementation, awareness or compliance, and by implication, a deficit of systems or individual behaviour. This paper sets out an alternative explanation. Drawing on fourteen semi-structured interviews with actors designing and governing AI-enabled anti-trafficking systems across law enforcement, commercial, research, and survivor-support contexts, it argues that such apparent gaps emerge from the varied and complex institutional and professional conditions through which actors come to recognise some issues, but not others, as ethical problems requiring action. We show that epistemic choices are intertwined with ethical judgements, and trace four interconnected moments---perception, judgement, situated action and socio-technical materialisation---through which concerns become intelligible, are weighed and acted upon, and are embedded in technical artefacts and governance arrangements. Actors often hold genuine ethical commitments, but these commitments are shaped by institutional logics and professional moral economies: some concerns are materialised, while others are narrowed, deferred or left unrealised. We show that ethical agency is exercised within and between competing constraints of profession, role, prior experience, and institutional settings. The paper argues that responsible AI governance requires purposeful and well-developed epistemic infrastructures that can cut across these constraints to establish institutional conditions through which the knowledge of affected communities and potential harms becomes receivable and actionable in design.

papers.title: Computer-Use Agents Gain Little Benefit from a World Model When Conditioned on Tutorials
papers.abstract: Recent work has improved computer-use agents (CUAs) by combining retrieved task-relevant tutorials and look-ahead planning using world models with MLLM judges. However, the contribution of each component -- tutorials, the judge, and the world model -- to overall improvement has not been evaluated in isolation. To fill this gap, we first construct OSWorld-Tutorial and ScienceBoard-Tutorial: two datasets for CUAs with curated multimodal tutorials, covering everyday and scientific domains. We then propose RAG-PolicyJudge (RAG-PJ), a policy-judge framework for CUAs conditioned on task-specific tutorials: the policy proposes candidate actions, and the judge selects among them. To isolate the effect of world models given tutorials, we compare RAG-PJ with and without common world models: using either zero-shot text-based descriptions of next states or an oracle that returns ground-truth visual observations. We find that RAG-PJ gains little benefit from these rollouts when tutorials are present, even with perfect visual futures. This suggests prior world-model gains in tutorial-conditioned methods come mainly from tutorial understanding and the judge's ability to select the proposed actions, rather than from predicted rollouts. Error analysis reveals that the bottleneck is not rollout fidelity, but the judge's ability to reason over future states and recognize task completion. This highlights the need to improve not just next-state prediction in world models, but also reasoning over their predicted rollouts. Datasets and code are available at https://github.com/realjoenguyen/RAGPJ-official.

papers.title: Spontaneous Enhancement of Inward Impurity Pinch during Massive Impurity Injection in Tokamak Plasmas
papers.abstract: A spontaneous enhancement of inward impurity pinch is identified prior to the fast quench under massive impurity injection on the EAST tokamak. The transition is marked by a rapid shift of the magnetic-island rotation frequency toward the electron diamagnetic direction within a few hundred microseconds. An extended KDG model shows that the impurity-induced increase in bulk ion collisionality can drive a transition across banana regime, nonlinearly modifying the parallel viscosity and producing a radial electric field excursion of approximately -10 kV/m, consistent with experiment. The associated self-organized response of the plasma flow and electrostatic potential can modify the parallel friction and further strengthen the neoclassical inward impurity pinch. Projections for ITER disruption mitigation suggest that this mechanism is expected to enhance impurity penetration, thereby improving the overall effectiveness of mitigation.

papers.title: A coupled lattice Boltzmann model for pore-scale mushy-layer dynamics with application to sea ice
papers.abstract: A pore-scale lattice Boltzmann model is developed for reactive transport in phase-changing porous media, coupling solute transport in the liquid with conjugate heat transfer across the solid and liquid phases. Two methodological developments are introduced: a novel link-based Volume-of-Pixel formulation for direction-dependent interface motion, and a generalized Robin boundary treatment for solute redistribution at moving interfaces. The phase-change formulation is validated against thermal benchmarks, while the Robin treatment is assessed through literature test cases, exhibiting convergence rates between first and second order. The coupled model is then applied to a local pore-scale segment of a sea ice brine channel in a purely diffusive regime. The simulations recover the expected ideal mushy-layer behaviour under appropriate scale separation. At sea-ice-relevant concentration ratios, thermal perturbations produce relatively large variations in brine salinity, causing freezing rather than melting to reshape the pore geometry in a non-uniform way. The resulting framework provides a pore-scale numerical tool for resolving coupled temperature, solute redistribution, and phase-boundary dynamics in mushy layers.

papers.title: Where Is VLA Inference Time Spent? Bottlenecks and Optimization Interactions Across GPUs
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models map camera observations and language instructions to robot actions. However, their large backbones and repeated action generation can make inference take longer than the robot's real-time requirements for its next action. To reduce the load of VLA computations, researchers have proposed multiple optimization approaches, including quantization and pruning. These optimizations can be combined with other general optimizations such as better kernel compilation or using CUDA graphs instead of the eager mode. However, most of these optimization results are usually reported on a single GPU type, typically for a few VLA models, with no analysis of what the real bottlenecks are for a model on a particular hardware or how these optimizations would generalize beyond the reported results. In this paper, we provide a comprehensive measurement study of seven families of inference optimization methods, from CUDA graphs and compilation to token pruning and quantization, on seven state-of-the-art VLAs evaluated on four GPU families ranging from a datacenter H100 to an embedded Jetson Thor. We analyse how CPU launch overhead, memory bandwidth, and kernel efficiency jointly shape optimization gains, and how applying one method changes the benefit of another. From this analysis, we derive VLA-Triage, guidelines for stacking optimizations under latency budgets. The guidelines identify which stages can provide the required savings and which combinations need testing in the deployed execution mode.

papers.title: BrainBind: Bridging Synchronized EEG and fMRI through Long-Form Naturalistic Video Representations
papers.abstract: Real-world vision is dynamic and scene-rich, while EEG and fMRI resolve it at complementary temporal and spatial scales. Most neural decoding systems, however, align one modality in isolation and mostly against static images or short clips. We study the synchronized case: EEG and fMRI are recorded during the same long-form naturalistic viewing, giving a shared stimulus but also recurring narrative context and many semantically similar candidates. We present BrainBind, a framework that maps synchronized EEG and fMRI into frozen long-form video embedding spaces and treats those spaces as common visual-semantic references, not literal neural codes. On CineBrain, a five-seed Recall@K 2 x 4 matrix across two video anchors and four system configurations shows distinct retrieval profiles. With Omni, fMRI organizes the full candidate list most strongly (MRR = 23.82, nDCG@10 = 25.31), while Joint-Dual gives the highest mean label-aware R@1 (13.52%) with a distinct rank-wide profile. The complementary episode-disjoint evaluation quantifies the contribution of repeated stimulus identity and narrative context to the random split. Across these experiments, proxy choice and system configuration produce distinct top-rank and rank-wide retrieval profiles within the present synchronized dataset. The code is available at https://github.com/Forainest789/Brainbind.

papers.title: GREP: Grounding Generated Room Evaluation in Principles
papers.abstract: Recent LLM-centric advances can generate attractive furnished rooms by selecting and arranging assets. Yet evaluation remains limited to specific perspectives or predefined questions, failing to reflect overall scene quality. To address this pressing need, we introduce GREP. Its core is a focus shift from defining specific questions to establishing a three-tier evaluation philosophy: basic physical validity checks whether a scene obeys physical constraints; visual coherence concerns compatibility in object scale, style, and composition; and, at the highest level, human-use logic requires object arrangements to align with everyday human habits. Guided by these principles, an evaluation agent autonomously and adaptively identifies issues from scene context, gathers evidence, and produces scores and reports. This supports scene-specific issue discovery and reliable judgments. Experiments show that (1) GREP achieves 87% agreement with human majority preferences, substantially outperforming baseline evaluators. (2) GREP reports improve scene quality through refinement, whereas score-only and no-feedback baselines show slight declines. (3) GREP suggests that as planning ability improves, recent models such as GPT-5.6 Sol can move from relying on pipelines and harnesses to challenging their guidance and constraints, but still lack the ability to resolve the resulting conflicts. Stronger models are therefore expected not only to plan well, but also to adapt to external guidance and constraints more flexibly. Project page: https://han-808.github.io/GREP/

papers.title: The integral Chow rings of $\mathcal A_3$ and $\mathcal M_3$
papers.abstract: Over $\mathbb C$, we compute the integral Chow ring of $\mathcal A_3$, the moduli stack of principally polarized abelian threefolds. Along the way, we compute the integral Chow ring of $\mathcal M_3$, the moduli stack of smooth genus-three curves. The ring $\CH(\mathcal A_3)$ is generated by the Chern classes of the Hodge bundle, along with three classes supported on the locus of decomposable abelian varieties, subject to 16 relations. The ring $\CH(\mathcal M_3)$ is generated by the Chern classes of the Hodge bundle, with five relations. In particular, we find that the top Chern class of the Hodge bundle, $\lambda_3$, has order 504 on $\mathcal A_3$ and 252 on $\mathcal M_3$. For $\mathcal A_3$, this removes the factor of 4 from the bound $252\mid\operatorname{ord}(\lambda_3)\mid 1008$ of Ekedahl and van der Geer.

papers.title: Majorana-like Josephson branch structure in one-dimensional transport of cold atoms
papers.abstract: We study phase-controlled transport through a one-dimensional channel of attractively interacting fermions connecting two three-dimensional BCS reservoirs. The competition between channel phase stiffness and pair tunnelling at the two contacts results in the emergence of two $4\pi$-periodic families of stationary states, characterised by symmetric or asymmetric phase drops at the boundaries. Advancing the reservoir phase difference by $2\pi$ exchanges these families so that the equilibrium energy remains $2\pi$ periodic, while the $4\pi $ periodicity might be attained in a diabatic regime. This structure admits a formal description in terms of two boundary Majorana operators, combining into a nonlocal fermion mode. Renormalization-group analysis shows that quantum fluctuations and phase slips are suppressed in the zero-temperature thermodynamic limit, preserving the branch crossings. The predicted branch exchange, metastable currents, and sweep-rate-dependent switching provide experimentally testable signatures of Majorana-like Josephson branch physics in a gapless interacting channel.

papers.title: A Simple Subquadratic Cut Query Protocol for Directed Reachability
papers.abstract:
We study $s$--$t$ reachability in an unweighted directed graph on $n$ vertices, accessed through a directed cut oracle: given $S\subseteq V$, the oracle returns the number of edges directed from $S$ to $V\setminus S$. Directed cut functions are submodular, and reachability asks whether the minimum $s$--$t$ cut has positive value. This connects the problem to the query complexity of submodular function minimisation. Whether or not reachability can be solved in truly subquadratic query complexity has been an outstanding open question for a decade.
  We give a simple algorithmic blueprint with two randomised implementations. The first uses $\widetilde O(n^{9/5})$ outgoing-cut queries; the second improves this bound to $\widetilde O(n^{5/3})$. The common idea is to construct an alternative orientation with the same underlying undirected graph and vertex-wise degree imbalances, thereby preserving reachability. We first approximate the target imbalances using an averaging and rounding procedure, then correct the remaining error with a flow.
  An earlier manuscript, made available in August 2026 in an online AI repository, reports an $\widetilde O(n^{3/2})$ query bound. Our contribution is a simple and comprehensible alternative approach that already achieves a polynomial saving over quadratic query complexity.

papers.title: Reciprocity Can Erase Direction:tructural Boundaries and Controlled Utility of Magnetic Graph Networks
papers.abstract: Magnetic graph networks encode direction through phase, but a learned graph can erase the intended directional mechanism before prediction. We characterize this failure for support-based magnetic Laplacians. Exact identities relate imaginary energy and distance from zero phase to amplitude-weighted reciprocity. Top-$k$ selection forces complete collapse when the observed-node count satisfies $m\leq k+1$, and dense support imposes a lower bound on reciprocal-arc fraction. We then construct paired propagation examples with identical node features and symmetric amplitudes but opposite labels, giving a provable chance-level limit for direction-erasing representations. In 72 fixed neural fits, support phase achieved test AUROC 1.0000 on a unilateral ring but 0.5000 on reciprocal ring and complete supports; continuous score phase and a real directed comparator achieved 1.0000 throughout. All models solved the direction-free control. These are oracle-direction mechanism tests, not evidence of learned clinical direction. In the preserved public DeepDRiD development study, continuous phase was active but its robustness difference from zero phase was only $+0.0036$ (descriptive 95\% interval $-0.0014$ to $+0.0095$) on validation patients used for checkpoint selection. The contribution is a structural and experimental framework for distinguishing erased direction from unestablished task utility. It provides a precise circumstance in which magnetic phase preserves useful information, without asserting universal or clinical superiority.

papers.title: SleuthVLM: Do We Really Need Audio-in-Video for Omni Video Understanding?
papers.abstract: Omni models answer questions about videos by jointly processing sampled frames and audio in one turn, with progress driven largely by scaling model size and omni training data. We ask whether a model needs to hear the audio directly at all, and present SleuthVLM, an agent harness built on a VLM that never hears the audio directly: speech will be transcribed into text, and the VLM will sleuth the video on its own without any predefined workflow. On four omni benchmarks with videos up to 90 minutes, SleuthVLM achieves the best average accuracy: \textbf{75.0%}, 2.6 points above Gemini 3.8 Flash, and it also tops the Video-MME-v2 leaderboard with \textbf{77.8%}; with an open-source 27B VLM, it beats all open-source omni models. We draw three findings: SleuthVLM beats a model that glances; hearing is not the bottleneck, agentic ability is; omni understanding needs better agentic ability, not just more omni data for modality alignment. So we provide a simple but effective starting point for doing omni video understanding. Omni understanding needs better agents, not just bigger models that hear.

papers.title: LIRA: A More Interpretable Dynamic Loss-Informed Rank Allocation for Low-Rank Adaptation
papers.abstract: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) has become a widely used parameter-efficient fine-tuning method for large pretrained models. However, standard LoRA typically assigns a fixed rank profile despite layer- and stage-dependent adaptation needs, while recent adaptive-rank variants often rely on heuristic or first-order signals that provide only an indirect link between rank reallocation and local loss behavior. This leaves the rationale behind each rank reallocation insufficiently interpretable. Motivated by this gap, we propose LIRA (Loss-Informed Rank Allocation), a dynamic-rank LoRA method designed to make online rank reallocation more interpretable. LIRA scores each layer by the estimated magnitude of the local loss perturbation associated with its recent LoRA-factor movements under a second-order approximation, making the basis for each rank change interpretable term by term. By periodically applying DELTA (Displacement-Evaluated Loss-Trajectory Allocation), a displacement-based algorithm for LoRA rank reallocation, LIRA produces discrete effective ranks under matched budgets while remaining compatible with standard (A,B) adapters. On RoBERTa-base GLUE under the La-LoRA/LoRA protocol, LIRA outperforms the uniform-LoRA and adaptive-rank baselines reported under this protocol; Trajectory EMA attains performance competitive with Fixed-point Fisher at lower estimation cost.

papers.title: Autonomous agents for electricity-system planning
papers.abstract: Planning electricity systems requires repeated decisions that connect regional resources, investment, operation and network constraints. Here we present an autonomous planning framework that carries prepared regional scenarios through proposal, numerical evaluation, feedback interpretation, redesign and final plan selection. Agents propose investment bounds, storage operating conditions and feeder interventions, interpret numerical feedback, and decide how to revise designs and when to stop. The framework automatically executes annual investment-and-dispatch optimization and representative-feeder verification, applies fixed acceptance criteria and retains the lowest-cost accepted candidate. We evaluate forty carbon-constrained trajectories across ten system-year scenarios in five electricity systems and four countries, using two model deployments and single- and multi-agent architectures. All forty retain candidates satisfying the implemented physical and fixed annual operational carbon-budget checks. Twenty-eight of forty matched reference designs exceed the new scenario ceilings. A separate archive of ninety-six trajectories under a common 1,000 Mt annual ceiling provides matched references and broader regional coverage. The results demonstrate autonomous planning under explicit emissions constraints using public regional data and published institutional demand outlooks.

authors.name: Yoon Pyo Lee
authors.institution: Hallym University Kangnam Sacred Heart Hospital

papers.title: RAPID: Increasing Efficiency of Internal Distillation via Randomized Methods
papers.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a technique used to transfer the expertise of large teacher models into small, efficient student models. Recent advances have integrated the distillation of internal activations, more directly training students to learn similar representations as the teacher. One of the core challenges of internal distillation is the dimensional incompatibility between the student and teacher internal representations. Existing methods add learnable matrices to project the larger teacher activations into the smaller representation space of the student. This is a notable point of inefficiency, as learning additional parameters for the projectors increases training costs, only for them to be discarded immediately after training. We introduce RAPID (RAndomized Projection for Internal Distillation) a novel distillation methodology which eliminates the wasteful projection learning by leveraging randomized methods. RAPID utilizes an efficient transform construction based on the Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma to compress the teacher representations into the student embedding space with strong theoretical guarantees of structural preservation. RAPID also employs a combination of exponential moving average (EMA) and homoscedastic uncertainty weighting in a novel multi-objective function designed for internal distillation. Our experiments in post-training for reasoning demonstrate that RAPID increases training efficiency by as much as 21.1% while maintaining performance comparable to existing methods.

papers.title: Follow the Features: SAE Feature-Guided Data-Efficient Instruction-Tuning of Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Selecting small, effective instruction-tuning datasets requires identifying which aspects of the original data to retain. We introduce Follow the Features (FtF), a data-selection method that uses sparse autoencoder (SAE) features to characterize training data and guide subset construction. FtF ranks features using dataset-level activation statistics, scores samples by their expression of highly ranked features, and incorporates feature resampling to encourage diversity. The LLM-SAE pair used for selection is independent of the model being fine-tuned, enabling reuse across target models. We evaluate FtF on two model-dataset settings at a training budget of 100 samples with a fixed sequence length of 256 tokens. FtF achieves performance competitive with GRAPE and S2L, with relative rankings varying across settings. On Qwen 3 8B trained on Alpaca, FtF exceeds full-dataset training by 1.59 percentage points in the harmonic mean of an AlpacaEval-based win rate and Open LLM Leaderboard performance, although full-dataset training retains a higher Leaderboard score. These results support SAE feature statistics as a useful signal for data-efficient instruction tuning.

papers.title: LoopKV: Loop-Aware KV Cache Compression for Serving Looped Transformers
papers.abstract: Looped transformers apply a shared block several times per token to improve accuracy without adding parameters. For models such as Ouro that keep a separate key-value (KV) cache per loop, cache memory limits the batch size that amortizes repeated weight reads. Uniform-bit quantization and fixed rules per loop do not allocate precision according to each layer's sensitivity in each loop. Measurements on Ouro show that quantization sensitivity varies across (loop, layer) cells, and the sum of individual cell damages approximates the overall output damage. Sharing damage also varies by cell, with later loops generally tolerating sharing better. Skipping low-attention values to save reads produces errors that compound across loops. LoopKV uses a one-time offline profile to choose 4-bit storage, 2-bit storage or reuse of the final loop's KV for each cell. The planner minimizes reads under budgets for predicted damage and storage. During decoding, each loop reads the high 2 bits of each 4-bit value and fetches the low bits only where its own attention weights require 4-bit precision. A single fused kernel in vLLM executes the plan. Serving Ouro-1.4B on one RTX PRO 6000, the memory-optimized LoopKV-M plan stores 35% less KV than uniform 4-bit quantization (KIVI-4) on the same fused kernel and CUDA graph. It sustains 1.7-2.2x KIVI-4's goodput under a latency service-level objective with a 16K-token maximum length. None of its averages on six public benchmarks falls significantly below BF16's.

papers.title: GRASP: Gradient-Guided Sampling for Contact-Rich Physics-Based Motion Retargeting
papers.abstract: We study physics-based retargeting of human demonstrations for robot learning: finding robot controls that reproduce reference motions under contact dynamics. We propose GRASP (Gradient Recovery from Archived Samples for Proposals), which combines sampling-based exploration with gradient-guided refinement without requiring a differentiable simulator. GRASP-TO extends tempered sequential Monte Carlo by fitting local quadratic cost models to archived rollouts and using their gradients to guide Markov chain Monte Carlo rejuvenation. Metropolis-Hastings correction preserves the target distribution for each fixed proposal kernel, and a population analysis connects the recovered gradients to Gaussian smoothing. GRASP-MPC scales this optimizer to long demonstrations through warm-started receding-horizon planning. Experiments on dexterous hands and humanoids show accurate retargeting with a shared tracking objective and no task-specific contact rewards, including 92.8% success on 1352 bimanual OakInk2 demonstrations. The refined references improve PPO tracking in pen spinning and humanoid-object interaction. We also demonstrate dexterous manipulation and whole-body humanoid motion on real hardware.

papers.title: RouTex: Multi-reference 3D Texture Generation by Reprogramming Rotary Position Encoding
papers.abstract: While single-image 3D texture generation has advanced significantly, conditioning texture synthesis on multi-view reference images remains largely under-explored, despite its necessity for resolving surface ambiguity in unobserved regions. In this paper, we propose RouTex, a novel multi-reference 3D texture generation framework based on in-context Diffusion Transformers (DiT). Our key insight is that native 3D Rotary Position Encoding (RoPE) inherently possesses spatial addressing capabilities. We introduce Positional Routing (PR) to reprogram 3D RoPE along spatial and semantic dimensions, establishing explicit reference-to-view correspondence without introducing additional parameters. To execute this routing efficiently, Dual-Granularity Attention (DGA) combines per-view local attention for fine texture fidelity with global joint attention over deduplicated references for cross-view consistency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RouTex achieves new state-of-the-art performance in multi-reference 3D texture generation.

authors.name: Chengyang Li
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: RDT-3D: Resolution-Decoupled Training for High-Fidelity 3D Geometry Generation
papers.abstract: High-fidelity 3D geometry generation requires maintaining global structural coherence alongside fine-grained surface details. While recent coarse-to-fine frameworks leverage Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE) to condition local queries, we reveal a critical training-inference resolution discrepancy: coordinate guidance and geometric supervision are aligned during training, whereas inference decodes high-resolution geometry from coarse spatial coordinates. This mismatch introduces a severe distribution shift that degrades fine details. To overcome this, we propose Resolution-Decoupled Training (RDT), which anchors RoPE guidance at 512 resolution while supervising geometry at 1536, enabling robust detail extrapolation. Additionally, to eliminate high-resolution data bottlenecks, we present Dual3D-300K, a large-scale paired dataset comprising 300K watertight 3D point clouds explicitly aligned across 512 and 1536 resolutions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RDT substantially improves sharp geometric regions, while Dual3D-300K offers a scalable benchmark for high-resolution 3D generation.
