authors.institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology

authors.name: Daniel H. Slichter
authors.institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology

authors.name: Adam M. Kaufman
authors.institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology

papers.title: Fast Quantum Byzantine Agreement with Nearly Linear Quantum Communication
papers.abstract:
We consider synchronous binary Byzantine agreement among $n$ processes connected by authenticated point-to-point classical and quantum channels. The adversary is computationally unbounded, sees all classical information, adaptively corrupts up to $t\le(1/3-\varepsilon)n$ processes, and may suppress messages sent by a process in the round in which it is corrupted.
  We give a quantum algorithm that solves Byzantine agreement in this model with probability $1$. It uses $O(\log^4 n)$ rounds, $O(n\log^8 n)$ qubits, and $O(n^2\log^8 n)$ classical bits in expectation, with constants depending on $\varepsilon$. This reduces the quantum communication of the protocol of Ben-Or and Hassidim (STOC~2005), which achieves $O(1)$ expected rounds but whose Byzantine coin implementation requires $\Omega(n^4\log n)$ qubits and classical bits.
  We also extend the quadratic message lower bound of Abraham et al.\ (PODC~2019) to quantum channels, obtaining an $\Omega(t^2)$ lower bound on worst-case expected total communication. For $t=\Theta(n)$, the communication and round complexity of our algorithm are therefore optimal up to polylogarithmic factors.

papers.title: On the role of grazing atmospheric particles in hypersonic boundary-layer receptivity
papers.abstract: The role of small atmospheric particulates in the initiation of the laminar-turbulent transition is investigated for the HIFLIER vehicle during Mach 6 ascent condition. High-fidelity simulations are used to examine the disturbance wavepackets generated by particles following either grazing trajectories through the boundary layer or trajectories that lead to impact and rebound at the cone surface. Grazing particles that penetrate less than halfway through the boundary layer are found to generate wavepackets with amplitudes comparable to those produced by wall-impinging particles. To identify the receptivity mechanisms responsible for this behaviour, a multiple-scales asymptotic formulation is developed that accounts for the extended streamwise region over which a particle interacts with the boundary layer. The analysis shows that a grazing particle can generate a strong disturbance response when crossing the critical layer, where the streamwise-momentum component of the adjoint mode is largest and the boundary layer is most receptive. Thus, direct surface impact is not required for atmospheric particulates to excite dynamically significant instability waves. Root-mean-square disturbance estimates for submicron grazing particles predict transition-onset locations close to those measured in flight, suggesting they may have contributed significantly to the onset of transition on HIFLIER at the trajectory condition considered.

papers.title: On the Cameron-Praeger conjecture for Steiner 6-designs
papers.abstract: A long-standing and far-reaching conjecture of Cameron and Praeger (1993) asserts that no non-trivial block-transitive $6$-$(v,k,\lambda)$ designs exist. Huber (2010) reduced the Steiner case ($\lambda=1$) to a single infinite family of possible exceptions, where the automorphism group is $G=\PGaL(2,p^e)$ acting on the points of the projective line, with $p\in\{2,3\}$ and $e$ an odd prime power. In this paper, we resolve this final case. By combining orbit-stabiliser analysis for the action of specific involutions in $\PGaL(2,p^e)$ with the modular arithmetic constraints derived from the design parameters, we prove that no such Steiner 6-designs can exist for any admissible $q$. This completes the proof that the Cameron-Praeger conjecture is true for the important case of non-trivial Steiner 6-designs.

papers.title: Nonuniform Buy-at-Bulk Network Design: Improved Approximation and LP Integrality Gap
papers.abstract:
In nonuniform buy-at-bulk network design, we are given an undirected graph and $h$ terminal pairs with positive demands, and we must route every demand at minimum total cost when each network resource has two independent parameters: a fixed buying price paid once if the resource is used, and a per-unit rental cost (or physical length) paid proportionally to the traffic it carries. Unlike the uniform-cost or single-sink variants, the general multicommodity problem allows unrelated buying and rental metrics across arbitrary source--sink pairs, arbitrary demands, and both edge and node resources.
  We give a deterministic polynomial-time $O(\log^2 h / (\log\log h)^2)$-approximation algorithm for undirected nonuniform buy-at-bulk network design. The guarantee holds for edge costs, node costs, and their combination, and applies to arbitrary positive rational demands with no dependence on the number of vertices or the numerical demand ratio. This improves upon the $O(\log^4 h)$ bound of Chekuri, Hajiaghayi, Kortsarz, and Salavatipour (2010) for unrestricted instances. Our result also establishes the same $O(\log^2 h / (\log\log h)^2)$ upper bound on the integrality gap of the natural affine multicommodity flow LP, bounding integral buying and rental costs separately against their fractional counterparts and preserving zero rental budgets exactly.

papers.title: The Minimal excludant of $\ell$-regular partition
papers.abstract: Andrews and Newman \cite{andrewsnewmanI} introduced and studied ``mex,'' function for an integer partition $\lambda$ of a positive integer $n$. The related function $\sigma^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ was subsequently defined, and its generating function and other properties have been studied by several authors. In this article, for a positive integer $\ell \geq 2$, we define the minimal excludant of an $\ell$-regular partition $\lambda$ of a positive integer $n$. We then define $\sigma_\ell^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$, the sum of the minimal excludants over all $\ell$-regular partitions of $n$, and obtain explicit generating functions for $\sigma_\ell^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ in the cases $\ell = 2$ and $\ell = 3$, expressed as eta-quotients. We prove that the sequence $\sigma_\ell^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ is weakly increasing for every $\ell$, and we obtain Hardy--Ramanujan type asymptotic formulas for $\sigma_2^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ and $\sigma_3^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ as $n \to \infty$. Additionally, we completely determine the parity of $\sigma_2^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$, showing that it is odd precisely at generalized pentagonal numbers, and we use this characterization to compute the density of $n$ for which $\sigma_2^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ is odd versus even. Finally, for $\sigma_3^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$, we prove that it is odd infinitely often, and we establish a quantitative lower bound, showing that the number of such $n$ up to $X$ grows at least like $\log \log X$.

papers.title: Continuity and Stability of the FitzHugh Nagumo System with Respect to the Diffusion
papers.abstract: Spatial heterogeneity in diffusion is a fundamental feature of excitable media, yet its effect on FitzHugh Nagumo dynamics remains mathematically challenging. We establish stability of solutions with respect to perturbations of the diffusion coefficient, providing a rigorous account of how changes in the medium affect the evolution of the system. Specifically, we prove a continuous dependence result ensuring that small perturbations in diffusion produce small variations in the corresponding solutions. The proof adapts the method of contracting rectangles to variable diffusion, yielding a framework for controlling and comparing solutions associated with different diffusion profiles. This result provides a rigorous link between heterogeneous and homogeneous FitzHugh Nagumo systems and justifies constant-diffusion approximations when the diffusion coefficient is close to a constant. Our analysis advances the understanding of FitzHugh Nagumo dynamics in heterogeneous media by establishing robustness with respect to spatial variations in diffusion.

authors.name: Alexander Rodriguez
authors.institution: National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences

papers.title: Phonological Knowledge of Chinese Characters in Language Models
papers.abstract: How much phonological knowledge do language models (LMs) possess about Chinese characters, and how is this knowledge represented and used? We introduce PinyinBench, a controlled benchmark covering homophones, phonological features (initials, finals, and tones), and polyphonic characters. We investigate 17 text-only and multimodal LMs through three complementary approaches: behavioral evaluation, layer-wise probing, and activation steering. Behaviorally, models demonstrate substantial knowledge of initials and finals, with a frontier model (DS-v4-flash) scoring 90%+ in homophone judgment, when two characters share no phonological features. However, its accuracy drops sharply to 72% when two characters differ only in lexical tone. Probing reveals that tone is highly decodable from embeddings and improves modestly across layers, whereas segmental information starts less decodable and improves substantially with depth. Activation steering shows that segmental representations can systematically influence generation, while tone exhibits much weaker effects. Furthermore, audio-bearing training improves phonological decodability, including tone, without corresponding improvements in steering effectiveness. Together, these findings reveal distinct representational and functional profiles for segmental and tonal information, with tonal information much harder to access and manipulate, demonstrating the necessity for combined evaluation, probing, and causal intervention for understanding linguistic knowledge in LMs.

authors.name: Hai Hu
authors.institution: Uniformed Services University of the Health Sciences

papers.title: Identities of Representation of Lie subalgebras of the first Weyl algebra
papers.abstract:
Let $F$ be a field. We study weak polynomial identities for pairs $(A,V)$ where $A$ is the first Weyl algebra over $F$ and $V$ is either a Lie subalgebra (under the usual Lie bracket) of $A$, or simply a vector subspace of $A$. Sometimes the weak identities of $(A,V)$, when $V$ is a Lie algebra, are called identities of representations of Lie algebras. Our starting point is the description of finite dimensional Lie algebras $L$ that can be embedded into the first Weyl algebra; this description was given by Rausch de Traubenberg, Slupinski and Tanas\u{a} in 2006. First we assume that $F$ is algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, and describe a finite basis of the weak identities of the pair $(A,L)$ where $L=\mathfrak{sl}_2$. In order to obtain such a basis we invoke theorems by Razmyslov and by Trishin concerning the identities of infinite dimensional irreducible representations of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$.
  Afterwards we consider $L$ as a filiform Lie algebra together with its concrete realisation inside the first Weyl algebra. We produce a finite basis of weak identities of the pair $(A,L)$, assuming $F$ to be infinite. Finally we study the weakest form of identities for $(A,V)$ where $A$ is the $n$-th Weyl algebra and $V$ is just a vector space - its canonical generating vector subspace. We deduce a basis of the weak identities in this case as well, once again assuming $F$ to be an infinite field, with no restriction on its characteristic. The same result was recently obtained by Dotsenko and Lopatin in characteristic $0$ by different methods. Our methods are combinatorial, we also use the theory developed by Razmyslov, and the representations of the symmetric and the general linear groups and their duality. We employ the characteristic-free description of the invariants of the symplectic group given by De Concini and Procesi.

authors.name: Joao Fernando Schwarz
authors.institution: Southern University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Four Extensions of the Universal Law of Robustness: Log-Concave Covariates, Heterogeneous Mixtures, Vector-Valued Predictors, and Markovian Data
papers.abstract: Bubeck and Sellke's universal law of robustness says that fitting $n$ noisy samples below the noise level with a class of $p$ real parameters forces a Lipschitz constant of order $\sqrt{nd/p}$, when the covariate distribution on $\mathbb{R}^d$ is isoperimetric: smooth interpolation costs a factor $d$ of overparametrization. Its hypotheses are Gaussian-type concentration, a homogeneous covariate law, scalar outputs, and independent samples; we relax each one. Exponential concentration suffices, at the unchanged rate and absolute constant and at the price of a capacity burn-in, some form of which we show is necessary; this gives the law for normalized log-concave covariates, with a $\log d$ loss from the current KLS bound. For heterogeneous mixtures the worst component constant is replaced by the weighted average of the component constants, under a typicality condition on the mixture composition. For vector-valued predictors the bound at the Frobenius Lipschitz scale is free of the output dimension $K$, and the Euclidean bound loses only $K^{-1/2}$, a loss that covariate-independent noise removes. Stationary Markov covariates retain the i.i.d. rate, the pseudo-spectral gap entering only the sample-size conditions. One master theorem carries the shared argument, and constants are explicit throughout.

papers.title: Core Reactivity in Cs-Ba-O ternary system under pressure
papers.abstract: High pressure can activate Cs $5p$ core electrons for covalent bonding. In this study, we investigate the Cs-Ba-O system at 150 and 250 GPa using first-principles structure searches. CsBa$_3$O$_8$ and CsBaO$_4$ both lie on the static-lattice convex hull at 250~GPa and exhibit mild Cs $5p$-O $2p$ bonding while retaining O$_2$ units with intermediate superoxide-peroxide character. Cs$_2$BaO$_3$ shows substantially stronger bonding but remains metastable with respect to CsO and BaO. A 1:1 Cs$_2$O-BaO$_2$ mixture provides a solid starting composition for investigating this chemistry, with core-reactive CsO among the predicted products at 250~GPa. Calculated Cs $L_3$-edge x-ray absorption near-edge spectra and powder diffraction patterns provide electronic and structural signatures to guide identification of the predicted phases in diamond anvil cell experiments.

papers.title: GIST: Gibbs-Targeted Hierarchical Data Selection for Offline RLVR
papers.abstract: Offline reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) trains on a fixed pool of sampled responses and typically supervises every token of every response, although responses and tokens are not equally informative. We study which ones to supervise through the Gibbs-optimal policy of KL-regularized RLVR, which offline training targets, and measure the mismatch between a policy and this target with a bidirectional KL divergence. At the reference policy, this mismatch factorizes exactly and separates the two outcomes: correct responses contribute mainly through the forward term, concentrated on their low-probability tokens, and incorrect responses through the reverse term, concentrated on the responses the policy generates often and on their high-probability tokens. Based on this analysis, we propose GIST (Gibbs-Targeted Hierarchical Data Selection), a two-level selection method that approximates these principles with signals available before training. GIST uses the sampling temperature to select correct responses on-policy and incorrect responses near the policy's mode, and it uses the initial policy's token probabilities to supervise only the tokens where the mismatch lies. Applied to two offline training objectives, GIST raises the average accuracy over GSM8K, MATH-500, and MBPP for all three models under both objectives. In a controlled comparison on Qwen3-0.6B/GSM8K, it outperforms seven selection baselines that choose from the same candidates while supervising 66.6% fewer tokens than training on all candidates of the same prompts.

authors.name: Xuliang Huang
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University

papers.title: Latent Cluster Separation as a Regularizer for Lifelong Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract: Lifelong (continual) anomaly detection systems must learn a sequence of tasks without forgetting how to recognize anomaly types seen earlier -- a property known as backward transfer. A common way to try to improve backward transfer is to reshape a model's internal representation around learnable concept centroids, typically coupled with a new way of scoring anomalies based on distance to those centroids. Because these two design choices are usually introduced together, it is unclear which one is actually responsible for any performance gain. In this paper, we unbundle the two mechanisms within a VAE-based lifelong anomaly detector and study them separately. We find that used purely as a training-time regularizer -- while leaving anomaly scoring unchanged -- latent cluster separation can improve detection quality and backward transfer, though whether it outperforms the alternative scoring approach depends on the dataset's underlying representation. Switching to distance-based scoring is instead where most of the instability commonly associated with this class of method actually originates; we identify and explain the underlying mechanism. This benefit depends on the dataset's underlying representation, and we report this as practical guidance for choosing between the two design choices, rather than as a list of caveats.

papers.title: SaMA: Morpho Adaptation via Asymmetric Expansion of Kronecker Product
papers.abstract: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) has attracted significant attention in the parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) landscape. However, its design suffers from two fundamental limitations. First, its invariance manifold induces flat directions in the loss landscape, creating an optimization bottleneck for adaptive optimizers. Second, its effective rank scales only linearly with the parameter budget. In this paper, we propose Scalable Morpho Adaptation (SaMA), a PEFT method grounded in a principled generalization of the Kronecker product. By relaxing the shared-block constraint in the perfect-shuffle factorization, SaMA spans from low to full rank and achieves a practical rank that scales quadratically with the parameter budget, up to full-rank. Furthermore, we show that its invariance manifold collapses to a diagonal group, making it structurally more optimizer-friendly. Empirically, SaMA consistently outperforms strong PEFT baselines on commonsense and arithmetic reasoning benchmarks while being more parameter-efficient.

papers.title: Analysis of a Two Membrane Thermoelastic Problem
papers.abstract: We formulate and study a mathematical model of a thermoforming process involving two interdependent thermoelastic membranes coupled with equations governing heat transfer. These membranes interact with each other through means of elastic forces and thermal transfer which determines changes in elastic properties and further deform the membranes. The two thermoelastic membranes lead to a pair of implicit obstacle problems which are modeled both as a 2-membrane problem or a pair of quasi-variational inequalities. Mathematically, the primary model couples an elliptic two membrane problem with associated nonlinear elliptic equations describing temperature distribution. We show, under physically relevant conditions, the existence of solutions via a fixed point approach that involves reformulation of the problem to improve regularity of solutions.

papers.title: Understanding the Perception of Transliterated Offensive Social Media Posts Among Banglish and Hinglish Users
papers.abstract: Effective content moderation depends on understanding not just what harmful content looks like, but how users perceive and respond to it. When offensive language is written in transliterated forms such as Banglish or Hinglish (Bangla or Hindi in Latin script), it may be interpreted very differently than in native scripts, with direct consequences for whether users report, ignore, or recognize it as harmful. Yet little is known about how script choice relates to user perception, or how these perceptions vary across demographic groups. To investigate these perceptions, we conducted a user study with $310$ participants ($193$ Hindi, $60$ Bangla, $57$ Bangla-Hindi bilingual speakers) who evaluated offensive posts in native scripts and transliterations. Participants provided offensiveness scores ($4.03$ for Banglish, $3.86$ for Hinglish) to transliterated posts, yet reporting fell from $20.9\%$ (native - Bangla, Hindi) to $18.2\%$ (transliterated - Banglish, Hinglish). Ignoring remained the dominant response (range $25.38\%-44\%$ overall). Women reported at higher probability than men for native-script ($23.6\%$ vs. $17.7\%$) and showed almost identical reporting probability in comparison to men for transliterated posts ($17.5\%$ vs. $17.9\%$), and younger participants ($<40$) rated Banglish content as more offensive than older participants ($\geq 40$), (Overall offensive score: $3.99$ vs. $3.78$). These findings identify transliteration as critical blind spot for moderation, underscoring the need for linguistically sensitive approaches to online safety.

papers.title: MotoVerse: A Benchmark for Predictive Perception of Motorized Two-Wheelers in Dense Unstructured Traffic
papers.abstract: Motorized Two-Wheelers (MTWs) dominate personal transport across much of the Global South, yet remain largely overlooked in predictive perception research for autonomous driving and ADAS. We introduce MotoVerse, a benchmark for predictive perception from an MTW's ego-centric perspective. MotoVerse comprises 949 maneuver clips collected in dense, unstructured traffic and trajectory annotations for over 31,000 surrounding road agents, including over 16,000 MTWs, enabling two complementary tasks: Ego-Rider Maneuver Anticipation (ERMA) and Traffic Agent Trajectory Prediction (TATP). Each clip is further annotated with an MTW-specific challenge taxonomy comprising dynamic ego-motion, weak traffic structure and contextual occlusion, enabling challenge-aware evaluation. We benchmark established conventional prediction models, general-purpose Vision-Language Models (VLMs), driving-specific VLMs and vision-language-action models. Our experiments reveal three key insights: (i) video backbones reach most of their full-observation accuracy from the first fifth of a maneuver, whereas zero-shot VLMs need most of the maneuver to be observed; (ii) zero-shot VLMs, whether general-purpose or driving-specific, largely remain close to simple baselines on both tasks; a preliminary LoRA study shows that adaptation lifts anticipation sharply but leaves trajectory prediction behind conventional models; and (iii) the rider's own motion drives forecasting difficulty: for every model, including a static baseline, errors are highest during left turns and rise under dynamic ego-motion. We believe MotoVerse will serve as a challenging benchmark for safer and more robust predictive AI for intelligent two-wheelers. The dataset and evaluation code are publicly available at https://github.com/VarunIIITH/MotoVerse.

papers.title: Roughness of nets
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we introduce the concepts of ~`\emph{rough weighted ideal-$\tau$-convergence}' and ~`\emph{rough weighted ideal-$\tau$-cluster point}' of a net in locally solid Riesz spaces. We also compare these concepts with key findings from the works of Lahiri $\&$ Das (2007/2008), Das (2012) and Aytar (2008), as follows:
  [(i):] The set of \emph{ideal-cluster points} of a sequence in a topological space is closed, 
[(ii):] The set of \emph{ideal-cluster points} of a net in a topological space is closed, [(iii):] The set of \emph{rough ideal-cluster points} of a sequence in a norm linear space is closed. 
  We demonstrate that, generally, the set of ~`\emph{rough weighted ideal-$\tau$-cluster points}' of a net in a locally solid Riesz space may not satisfy the aforementioned results, which implies that it may not be closed. This suggests that this set exhibits new characteristics, which we will discuss here. Ultimately, our characterization demonstrates that these new concepts can help identify an ideal that is maximal and effectively represent any closed $\tau$-neighborhood of $\theta$ within these spaces.

papers.title: The CNF Encoding Complexity of Boolean Functions
papers.abstract: We study the minimum number of clauses required to encode a boolean function into a CNF formula with auxiliary variables. Our main result is that if a boolean function can be evaluated in nondeterministic time $t$ (in the RAM model) with $m$ bits of advice such that at most $b$ bits of advice are accessed for each input, then it admits a CNF encoding with $\widetilde{O}(t + \sqrt{mb})$ clauses. This constitutes a nonuniform generalization of Robson's (TCS'91) variant of the Cook--Levin theorem, for which a na\"ive generalization would yield $\widetilde{O}(t+m)$ clauses; our applications leverage $b = o(m)$ to obtain significantly better bounds. Since preprocessed data structures can be modeled as computation with advice, our result allows us to translate space- and time-efficient data structures to compact CNF encodings. As an application, we derandomize a data structure of Larsen and Williams (SODA'17) to show that every $k$-CNF function on $n$ inputs can be encoded with $n^k/2^{\Omega_k(\sqrt{\lg n})}$ clauses. Notably, despite encoding a $k$-CNF function, the encoding itself necessarily contains clauses of unbounded width, since an information-theoretic argument shows that the minimum number of bounded-width clauses to encode such functions is $\Omega_k(n^{k}/\lg n)$ in the worst case. In general terms, our results imply that for a wide variety of NP-complete problems, one can reduce to CNF-SAT in a way that results in asymptotically fewer clauses than previously known methods.

papers.title: Low cross-plane thermal conductivity of $\kappa$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ thin films
papers.abstract: The thermal conductivities of (001) $\kappa$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ thin films deposited on $c$-plane sapphire substrates were measured with frequency-domain thermoreflectance (FDTR). The thermal conductivity increases from 1.83 $^{+0.19}_{-0.18}$ W/m$\cdot$K to 2.26 $^{+0.35}_{-0.40}$ W/m$\cdot$K as the thicknesses increase from 159 nm to 689 nm. This weak thickness dependence indicates that the majority of the intrinsic phonon mean free paths are smaller than the range of investigated film thicknesses. First-principles-based calculations that include phonon-phonon and phonon-boundary scattering capture this size-dependent behavior and support our experimental observation. Temperature-dependent measurements of a 689 nm film from 293 to 400 K show a decrease in thermal conductivity with increasing temperature due to enhanced phonon-phonon scattering. A weaker temperature dependence is observed in a 159 nm film where phonon-boundary scattering becomes more prominent. At comparable film thicknesses, our measured $\kappa$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ films exhibit lower values of cross-plane thermal conductivity than the other experimentally measured Ga$_2$O$_3$ polymorphs. Our experimental observations are supported by prior predictions, which suggest that the low thermal conductivity of $\kappa$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ results from its complex crystal structure, which leads to increased anharmonicity and lower phonon group velocities relative to other polymorphs. Thermal management strategies, such as integration with high-thermal-conductivity substrates, may thus be required to mitigate self-heating for $\kappa$-Ga$_2$O$_3$-based electronic devices.

authors.name: Jingyu Tang
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: MKD2World: A Typed Spatial MarkDown World Model For Web Agents
papers.abstract: Graphical user interface (GUI) agents can improve decision-making with world-model foresight, provided that predicted states accurately reflect post-action interfaces. Existing state representations fail to jointly capture interface layout, UI semantics, and explicit locations. We introduce Typed Spatial Markdown (TSM), a Markdown-style textual state representation for desktop web interfaces. TSM serializes block-level and atomic-level UI elements according to their spatial relationships, jointly encoding their types, visual semantics, explicit locations, optional control states, and hierarchical membership. To train a screenshot-to-TSM renderer, we construct AtomBlock-WebUI, a dataset with precise annotations at both granularities. By injecting element-type labels into HTML and directly extracting bounding boxes after rendering, we avoid annotation errors caused by post-hoc inference from webpage structures. Building on TSM, we propose MKD2World, a desktop web world model trained in two stages for current-state description and action-conditioned next-state prediction. During inference, the web agent queries MKD2World as needed and performs a ``digest'' step, in which it interprets each predicted state and extracts task-relevant evidence for selecting the best action. Experiments show that MKD2World-9B achieves an EleF1 score of 26.50 on the out-of-domain test set, outperforming GPT-5.6-Sol(14.98) by 11.52 points. Across Online-Mind2Web tasks, MKD2World-9B improves the success rate of the Qwen3.5-35B web agent from 22.94% to 37.61%, achieving competitive performance among leading open-source GUI world models. Code is available at https://github.com/OmniAI-Lab-CUHKSZ/MKD2World.

papers.title: Visual Token Routing: Learning to keep tokens that matter
papers.abstract: Computer-use agents (CUAs) have recently achieved superhuman performance on several long-horizon benchmarks. However, their computational cost limits their use in long-horizon tasks and real-time domains such as video games. A key bottleneck is representing each screenshot as thousands of visual tokens, which accumulate into long contexts as agents reason over extended interaction histories. We observe that most of these visual tokens are either semantically irrelevant to the agent's next action or temporally redundant across screenshots. Building on this observation, we introduce Visual Token Routing (VTR), a joint training framework for learning sparse visual representations that preserve the information needed for action prediction. In VTR, we train the vision-language model together with a lightweight spatio-temporal router that examines each image region in the current and previous screenshots and decides whether its visual token enters the language model. We optimize the router using an adaptive loss to keep the number of visual tokens as small as possible while minimizing performance degradation. With just 2,000 training steps, VTR matches the performance of the full-resolution model on OSWorld, CUA-World, and video game action prediction, while using 2.5-5.8x fewer visual tokens. These savings reduce inference cost by up to 3.3x and speed up prefill by up to 2.9x. VTR also outperforms lowering the image resolution and other baselines for dropping tokens, by up to 12.8 points on OSWorld. Overall, VTR enables computer-use agents to process only the visual tokens they need, allowing them to be used in long-horizon tasks and real-time domains at a fraction of the computational cost. Code and models are available at https://pranjal2041.github.io/vtr

papers.title: PixelSpline: Continuous Space-Time Video Super-Resolution via Endpoint-Anchored Shared Pixel Trajectories
papers.abstract: Existing continuous space-time video super-resolution methods often infer motion from only two endpoint frames and model the two motion directions independently, making them vulnerable to ambiguous correspondence and inconsistent trajectories. We introduce a continuous STVSR framework that combines long-context encoding, continuous HR feature lifting, and an endpoint-anchored PixelSpline. Long-range observations provide more reliable endpoint representations, while continuous upsampling constructs detailed appearance features directly on the requested HR grid. PixelSpline explicitly models each pixel's motion as a single continuous trajectory shared by both endpoints. Using this trajectory, our method warps endpoint colors into a coarse intermediate frame and aligns the HR features for residual reconstruction. Experiments across spatial and temporal upsampling settings demonstrate that the proposed framework offers a favorable quality--efficiency trade-off.

papers.title: Cibersapiens: Gamifying Cybersecurity Education to Engage Secondary Students
papers.abstract: Cybersecurity education and awareness are often tailored for businesses, leaving general citizens, especially young people, unprepared. Despite the availability of educational resources, cybersecurity training is not provided equally to all individuals, particularly children and teenagers. As digital risks such as sexting, grooming, and cyberbullying, among others, increase, young users remain vulnerable. However, existing awareness efforts fail to engage them effectively and current content lacks the motivation needed to drive meaningful behavioral change. This paper introduces "Cibersapiens: Digital Well-being for a Connected Generation," an interactive, gamified environment designed to teach cybersecurity to secondary school students. The project focuses on developing and implementing gamified educational resources that actively engage students, improve their understanding of cyber risks, and promote best practices in digital security. By leveraging active learning methodologies, this approach transforms cybersecurity education into an engaging and meaningful experience.

papers.title: Ray-Tracing-Based Dynamic Channel Sounding With Autoregressive Wi-Fi CSI Prediction
papers.abstract: Channel sounding in Wi-Fi multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems must balance channel state information (CSI) accuracy against CSI acquisition overhead. Device mobility causes channel aging, while autoregressive CSI prediction introduces errors that accumulate over sounding intervals. However, standardized statistical channel models cannot fully capture the environment-specific channel dynamics encountered in physical artificial intelligence (AI) applications, motivating the use of Sionna-based ray tracing to evaluate CSI prediction under device mobility and evolving propagation geometry. This paper develops a dynamic sounding framework that integrates autoregressive CSI prediction with signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR)-constrained interval selection. A Transformer with rotary position embedding that converts device positions into CSI sequences predicts CSI across multiple subcarriers for beamforming updates between sounding exchanges. We formulate sounding-interval selection as a predicted average-throughput maximization problem under per-stream SINR lower-bound constraints, including CSI acquisition and processing overhead. A prediction-error perturbation analysis provides the SINR bounds, and cumulative-sum enumeration globally solves the finite single-variable problem. Actual SINR feasibility holds whenever the prediction errors satisfy the bounds. Ray-tracing experiments assess channel prediction, trajectory transfer, and autoregressive prediction errors. In single-STA Wi-Fi 7 link-level simulations, predicted-CSI beamforming improves mean goodput by 67.3%, 112.7%, and 119.1% over stale CSI for linear, circular, and cosine trajectories, respectively.

authors.name: Jinke Ren
authors.institution: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

authors.name: Shuguang Cui
authors.institution: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

papers.title: The enhanced polylogarithm conjecture in weight two for imaginary quadratic fields
papers.abstract: Zagier's polylogarithm conjecture predicts that special values of Dedekind zeta functions can be expressed in terms of polylogarithms at algebraic arguments. For imaginary quadratic fields, Zagier and Gangl refined it by lifting both sides to complex values modulo rational multiples of a power of $2\pi i$. In previous work, the author extended their enhanced zeta values from ideal classes to ray classes by means of the Shintani $L$-function of two variables and formulated the enhanced polylogarithm conjecture for ray classes. In this article, we prove this conjecture in weight two. More precisely, we establish a Galois-equivariant equality between the enhanced partial zeta values of ray classes and the enhanced dilogarithms of elements of the rational Bloch groups of the corresponding ray class fields. These elements are constructed explicitly, starting from the Eisenstein class of Doran and Kerr on the square of a CM elliptic curve and contracting it with the graphs of complex multiplication.

papers.title: Where models of minimal height are hard to find: cubic rational maps with a multiple fixed point
papers.abstract: Given a rational point of the moduli space of cubic rational maps, we seek a map in its class with the smallest integer coefficients. A recent algorithm (Shaska, arXiv:2610.33990) combines an exact descent and minimisation of the resultant with a reduction and a local search; it is nearly exact where the minimal height is known. Beyond that range, a certified deeper search shows that the instances in which a smaller model lies beyond its reach are not random: a classifier predicts them from the six invariants of the point, and asking what it relies on leads to an exact algebraic surface, the maps with a triple fixed point. Invariant theory and the stability hypothesis of reduction theory (Hutz and Stoll, 2019) then identify the larger locus that contains it: the hypersurface $\xi_1^3=6\xi_2^2$ of maps with a multiple fixed point, on which the fixed-point quartic is not stable. It holds most of the hard instances. On it the two invariants of the fixed-point quartic are $(\xi_1,\xi_2)=(6m^2,6m^3)$ for an integer $m\ge0$; we parametrise the integer points of the surface, and show that on its generic part the sign of $\xi_5$ is the sign of the cubic coefficient at the parabolic fixed point. A covariant defined on the locus, added to the reduction, resolves only a minority of the hard instances: they appear to be mainly a matter of the search's reach. These findings lead to a certified structured search that never returns a larger model than the original algorithm and finds most of the smaller models within reach, also at heights not used to design it, at a small multiple of its running time.

papers.title: Adaptive Grid-Mode-Aware Hybrid Energy Storage Control for AI Data Center Oscillation Mitigation
papers.abstract: Oscillatory power components in AI data-center demand can produce large frequency deviations when they coincide with vulnerable grid modes. Mode-aware hybrid energy storage systems (HESSs) can selectively suppress these components, but their effectiveness degrades when the grid mode changes while the control target remains fixed. This paper proposes a closed-loop grid-mode-adaptive HESS control framework that integrates measurement-based modal identification with mode-selective control. A sliding-window N4SID estimator identifies the local grid dynamics from grid-side power and frequency measurements, and the resulting natural-frequency estimate is used to retune the modal suppression branch assigned to the supercapacitor. The framework is evaluated under a grid-mode shift from 0.50 to 1.35Hz while maintaining equal physical damping and approximately equal load excitation at both frequencies. Compared with the fixed-target controller, the adaptive method reduces the post-change grid-side modal power component from 8.78 to 2.02MW, corresponding to a 76.94% reduction, and substantially lowers the resulting frequency deviation.

papers.title: ME^2FDiff: Multiscale Expert Enhancing Feature Diffusion in Residual Network for Brain Tumor Segmentation
papers.abstract: Automated segmentation of post-treatment glioma from MRI is essential for accurate diagnosis and treatment planning, yet remains difficult. Surgery and chemoradiotherapy cause structural changes in brain like resection cavities, edema, and fibrosis, that alter imaging appearance and mimic tumor recurrence. Contemporary segmentation architectures attain high accuracy with two limitations. First, the bottleneck originates from the deepest encoder stage, so one representation must serve sub-regions that differ widely in size and appearance. Second, they produce the segmentation in a single forward pass with no mechanism for refinement. We propose ME^2FDiff, a single-model architecture, addressing both. An attention-conditioned spectral diffusion block refines the bottleneck. It uses the image-conditioned latent diffusion process with two processes: a spatial pre-attention gate and a spectral fusion block whose timestep-adaptive bandpass filter selects the informative frequency band at each noise level. A multiscale expert-enhanced feature block fuses the intermediate encoder scales into the bottleneck through expert-selected shared tokens, guaranteeing balanced utilization without an auxiliary loss. On the BraTS 2024 post-treatment glioma dataset, ME^2FDiff achieves the best results on every tumor sub-region among all single-model baselines (91.23% Dice, 84.52% IOU, 2.13 mm HD95 on whole-tumor) and surpasses a three-expert ensemble on both overlap metrics at roughly one-third of its inference cost. Against recent state-of-the-art methods retrained under identical conditions, it maintains the strongest performance with the fewest parameters of any competing model. These findings demonstrate that a single, compact network can absorb the specialization, usually sought through ensembling or larger architectures.

authors.name: Afrida Rahman
authors.institution: Rajshahi University of Engineering and Technology

papers.title: Evaluating Human-LLM Alignment on Visualization Preference
papers.abstract: There are often multiple valid visualizations, spanning different chart types, visual encodings, and aesthetic choices, that can all support a user's goal of analyzing a dataset. Determining which of these candidate visualizations is most appropriate, however, remains challenging. Prior work has leveraged expert-curated taxonomies to guide visualization design and subsequent quality evaluation, a practical evaluation model must also account for human-centric factors. Latest visualization tools integrate Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate and refine visualizations, using LLM-as-a-judge to provide design feedback. Without a deeper understanding of whether, and in what ways, human and LLM perceptions of visualizations align, there is a real risk of deploying low-quality agents that do not reflect human judgment. We study this question through a pilot experiment - we formulate the problem as a preference task over curated chart pairs and compare the judgments of state-of-the-art vision models with those of a panel of human annotators. We establish a cautionary tale: such judges risk filtering out informative, compelling displays. We find that frontier models collapse human subjectivity, a rich signal that reveals contrasting design choices, into near-deterministic verdicts.

papers.title: On the Feature Evolution of Temporal Difference Learning
papers.abstract: Temporal-difference (TD) learning trains neural representations using bootstrapped targets generated by evolving value estimates, yet how predictive features emerge and propagate under incomplete neural updates remains poorly understood. We investigate this problem using finite-width two-layer ReLU critics on a constructed family of smooth stochastic horizon-$H$ MDPs with unknown quadratic structure and $d$-dimensional observations. We first show that an informative TD update acquires the quadratic Bellman signal and yields a representation admitting a bounded predictive readout. The simultaneous hidden-weight and head update achieves a strict finite-sample prediction-risk improvement over matched head-only SGD, with a $2(d+1)$-fold larger population quadratic response. We then establish that an imperfect learned continuation can already provide informative supervision to an earlier zero-reward stage. By tracking coupled neural updates with one SGD step per target copy, without requiring intermediate Bellman regressions to be solved, we obtain a uniform prediction-error transient $\exp[-\Omega(K/(Hd))]$, up to action-independent shifts and explicit sampling and finite-width errors. On the constructed signed-action MDP family whose total reward is bounded by 1, we show that an exploration-then-commit algorithm can achieve $\widetilde{O}(d^3H^{1/3}T^{2/3})$ regret over $T$ episodes, using $K=\widetilde{O}(Hd)$ global updates. Our analysis connects bootstrapped feature acquisition, concurrent neural refinement, and finite-budget policy performance.

papers.title: Say the Same, Act Differently: Diagnosing and Steering Text-Action Divergence in Reasoning VLAs
papers.abstract: Reasoning vision-language-action (VLA) models pair physical control with natural-language rationales that supervisors can read to monitor embodied safety. Prior attacks on VLA reasoning corrupt the rationale itself and leave visible evidence in the text. We show that visual perturbations can instead alter the physical action while keeping the generated rationale word-for-word identical. At the shared text/action interface of Alpamayo for driving and InstructVLA for manipulation, our text-neutral action-subspace (TNAS) diagnostic shows that the locally most action-sensitive direction is nearly orthogonal to the active text-loss gradients, with 1.87% and 5.28% norm overlap. At equal hidden-state perturbation norms across both models, interventions along this text-neutral residual shift actions 4.64x to 47.8x more than text-gradient perturbations, whereas text-gradient perturbations induce 21.2x to 277x more text drift. Steering visual perturbations along this direction reaches the same decoupling from the image. Across 154 obstacle-annotated driving scenes in Alpamayo, TNAS-guided attacks induce a new collision under a word-for-word identical rationale in 52.6% of scenes under full-image perturbations and 35.1% under a localized forward-camera patch, compared with 4.55% for unguided action attacks. Relative to a text-preserving baseline, TNAS guidance raises exact rationale preservation from 83.0% to 89.5% and cuts teacher-forced text drift by 68.4% at a comparable collision rate. In InstructVLA, TNAS guidance cuts text drift by 40.5% and preserves the exact response on 85.0% of examples alongside a 1.73-unit action-chunk shift. An unchanged rationale therefore cannot certify a safe action, so monitors for reasoning VLAs must verify the predicted action channel directly.

papers.title: Mixed-Integer Second-Order Cone Formulations for the Euclidean Bottleneck Steiner Tree Problem in $\mathbb{R}^d$
papers.abstract: Given a set of terminals in $\mathbb{R}^d$ and an integer $k\ge0$, the Euclidean bottleneck Steiner tree problem (EBSTP) asks for a tree spanning the terminals with at most $k$ Steiner points that minimizes its longest edge. Although the planar case has been widely studied, exact optimization methods for arbitrary dimension remain scarce. We develop two exact mixed-integer second-order cone programming (MISOCP) formulations for the EBSTP: a single-commodity flow formulation and a formulation with connectivity cuts. Both formulations share a geometric core based on edge-conditional second-order cone constraints and are strengthened by problem-specific preprocessing, edge-dependent big-$M$ constants, symmetry-breaking constraints, constructive upper bounds, and new global lower bounds on the optimal value. We establish the correctness of the formulations and prove the validity of all strengthening techniques. Computational experiments on 1050 benchmark instances in dimensions $d\in\{2,3,4\}$, with up to $50$ terminals and $9$ Steiner points, show that the single-commodity flow formulation consistently outperforms the formulation with connectivity cuts, with an advantage { in solved instances} that grows with dimension. The proposed global lower bounds substantially strengthen the root relaxation, while the single-commodity flow formulation provides the most robust exact solution method across all test sets. These results establish the single-commodity flow formulation as an effective exact approach for the EBSTP in arbitrary fixed dimension.

authors.name: Nelson Maculan
authors.institution: Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro

authors.name: Renan V. Pinto
authors.institution: Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro

papers.title: Pairing Expert Critique with LLM-Driven Refinement: An Iterative Approach for Curating Quality AI Evaluation Datasets
papers.abstract: Evaluating and improving domain-specific LLM responses requires high-quality reference data and rubrics, yet expert authoring is slow and expensive, and synthetic datasets may fail to capture practitioner preferences unless they are grounded in expert judgment. We present SME-C (Subject Matter Expert Critique), a human-AI workflow that captures expertise through lightweight critiques of candidate responses and complements it with LLM-driven analysis and refinement to iteratively curate response datasets and evaluation rubrics. We validate SME-C in the domain of financial business briefs, collecting 3,853 critiques from 411 finance professionals on 520 queries across two survey rounds. We evaluate two LLM-driven refinement strategies: one guided by the experts' written critiques and one that infers critique solely from their preference votes. In a blind validation survey with 100 additional professionals, we found that both strategies significantly improved quality over the experts' top-ranked baseline responses. The gains were concentrated among weaker original responses, and the two strategies excelled in different ways: critique-based refinement produced more domain-grounded improvements, whereas vote-based refinement was more effective at identifying and removing irrelevant content. The resulting rubrics and refined dataset support reproducible offline evaluation and benchmarking of LLMs, suggesting that structured expert critique is a viable alternative to expert authoring for building high-quality, domain-specific evaluation resources more quickly, at scale, and at lower cost.

papers.title: Frequency-Frame Covariance for Reactive-Power Scalarization
papers.abstract: Measured voltage and current waveforms may be represented in a reference frame whose frequency differs from the physical fundamental frequency. Reactive-power readouts calculated from such frequency-shifted coordinates may change if their readout operators are not transformed consistently. This paper presents a frequency-frame covariance formulation for finite-spectrum, zero-mean periodic waveforms with complete harmonic information over one physical period. A necessary and sufficient covariance condition is derived, requiring the readout operator to transform consistently with the waveform representation. Consequently, frequency-dependent harmonic weights must be evaluated at physical harmonic orders rather than relative frame labels. In particular, the derivative/Iliovici readout equals a relative-derivative contribution plus an explicit reference contribution. The formulation also separates readout-operator errors from errors caused by changes in the physical components retained by waveform projections. Three analytical cases illustrate conditional carrier recovery for a memoryless resistor, physical-frequency weighting at relative zero in an RLC branch, and the possibility that an exact reactive-power scalar can coexist with a substantial waveform error after projection. The scope is deterministic calculation consistency in frequency-shifted coordinates rather than instrument measurement uncertainty.

papers.title: Clips2Story: Training-Free Video Storyboarding and Editing Using Multimodal Retrieval-Embedded Generation
papers.abstract: Video editors often work with large collections of fragmented footage and must select and organize relevant clips into a coherent story. However, many existing video editing and summarization methods assume a temporally ordered source video and aim to preserve its original narrative and temporal structure. In this paper, we introduce Clips2Story, a training-free, LLM-based pipeline that enables users to create keyword-specified short videos from a pool of video clips. Given a pool of clips and a user-specified keyword, we first extract text-based multimodal descriptors for each clip and retrieve the clips most relevant to the keyword. We then provide the textual descriptors of these candidate clips to an LLM, which selects and arranges them into an editable storyboard with connective narrations. Finally, we assemble the selected clips and retrieve accompanying visuals for the narrations to compose the output video. To evaluate the proposed pipeline, we construct a synthetic evaluation dataset from 100 long-form videos across five genres by segmenting each video into short clips using a scene-change detection model and shuffling the resulting clips to remove their temporal order. Through objective evaluation and qualitative examples, we demonstrate that Clips2Story can effectively retrieve keyword-relevant clips and compose coherent storyboards based on user-specified keywords. Human evaluation further shows that Clips2Story outperforms a strong baseline in terms of narrative coherence, keyword alignment, and overall realism.

papers.title: Machine Learning the Complete Active-Space Wavefunction Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials enable multireference-quality reaction dynamics but do not retain the electronic structure underlying the predicted energies and forces. Recovering this information by independently performing complete active space self-consistent field (CASSCF) calculations is both expensive and potentially inconsistent. We introduce the Complete Active-Space Wave Function Reconstruction (CAS-WR) model, which learns the geometry-dependent electronic structure from CASSCF data and reconstructs the CAS wave function without repeated orbital optimization. Combined with uncertainty-based active learning, CAS-WR is demonstrated for the Diels--Alder reaction and \ce{TiC+}-catalyzed C--H activation. The approach enables trajectory-resolved analysis of multiconfigurational electronic structure across reactive ensembles. Preliminary applications to excited-state proton transfer and transition-metal photocatalysis suggest that CAS-WR can provide a general route toward recovering electronic structure along complex ground- and excited-state reactive dynamics.

papers.title: Koszul duality and homotopy algebras for operads over quivers
papers.abstract: For a quiver $Q$, we introduce and study $Q$-operads (or operads over $Q$), defined as a special sort of $\mathbf{fc}$-multicategories or virtual double categories, in which the directions of the arrows of $Q$ encode the permitted input orderings. In this higher operadic framework, we construct the bar--cobar adjunction and develop a theory of Koszul duality and homotopy algebras, together with compatibility results under changes of quiver. We treat dg categories and their left modules, right modules, and bimodules as algebras over quiver-operads. We prove that these operads are Koszul and that their resolutions govern the corresponding $A_\infty$ categories and modules. We also categorify Sagave's notion of derived $A_\infty$ algebras and introduce modules over derived $A_\infty$ algebras and categories. Finally, we explain that restriction along a folding of quivers constructs diagonal $A_\infty$ bimodules, while extension along an inclusion of quivers realizes two-sided bar models of derived tensor products.

papers.title: RATSIFT: Resolution-Adaptive Transformer for Solar Irradiance Forecasting and Temporal Downscaling
papers.abstract: Accurate forecasting and temporal downscaling of solar irradiance is critical for reliable renewable energy integration and grid management. Traditional methods often struggle to capture rapid irradiance variability. In this work, we develop a Transformer-based architecture for simultaneous forecasting and temporal downscaling. The model takes input data at arbitrary resolutions and generates outputs at any resolutions represented within the training data, leveraging both global and local contextual information. To improve training efficiency, a genetic algorithm-based optimization framework is implemented to identify suitable model hyperparameters, while reducing the computational cost of exhaustive grid search. The effectiveness of the proposed model is shown by analyzing real data in Dallas, Texas. The proposed model achieved root mean square error (RMSE) values of 28.785, 29.544, 30.157, 32.132~W/m\(^2\) for 15-, 30-, 60-minute, and irregularly spaced global input and producing forecast at 5-minutes resolution, respectively. Furthermore, this model produced reliable uncertainty estimates, exhibiting wider prediction intervals for high-resolution inputs during volatile solar conditions, whereas coarser-resolution inputs result in narrower intervals and significantly lower training time and computational cost. Our approach provides a scalable and efficient framework for multi-resolution solar irradiance forecasting and temporal downscaling, suitable for practical energy forecasting and grid management applications.

papers.title: Rational Torsion and Ramification Constraints on Odd Superelliptic Jacobians
papers.abstract: Let C: y^d = f(x) be a smooth projective superelliptic curve over Q, where d >= 3 is odd, f(x) in Q[x] is separable of degree n >= 3, and gcd(d,n) = 1. Let J = Jac(C) be its Jacobian. We study the rational torsion subgroup J(Q)_tors through the interaction of ramification geometry, Galois actions, reduction at primes of good reduction, and the geometry of divisors. First, we describe the subgroup R_d contained in J[d] generated by the ramification-point differences and determine its Galois-invariant subgroup explicitly in terms of the sizes of the Galois orbits of the roots of f. This yields a precise description of the rational d-torsion classes arising from ramification, without assuming that they account for all of J(Q)[d]. Second, we establish criteria based on the orders of reduced Jacobians that can prove the vanishing of the full rational torsion subgroup. Finally, we derive geometric constraints on divisor classes represented by effective divisors of degree smaller than the genus, including a restriction arising when distinct effective divisors represent the same class. Explicit examples illustrate how the Galois-theoretic and reduction-theoretic methods can be combined to study rational torsion on odd superelliptic Jacobians.

papers.title: GRIDSHIELD: Verifiable Grid Feasibility and Manipulation Resistance in Privacy-Preserving Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading
papers.abstract: Blockchain-based peer-to-peer (P2P) energy markets let neighbors trade directly, but concentrate unchecked power in the clearing operator. Most prior work addresses only part of this: network-aware clearing respects grid constraints but operates on plaintext allocations, while privacy-preserving designs hide bids yet either drop the network constraint, enforce it only inside an unauditable computation, or recover it at the cost of a per-circuit trusted setup. Neither considers what happens if an adversary captures the operator's clearing privilege to reorder trades for profit or curtail a rival. We present GRIDSHIELD, a P2P energy-trading system that clears sealed bids with an order-independent batch program, removing the welfare a compromised operator can extract by reordering trades, and proves the result grid-feasible via an aggregated congestion-feasibility proof (ACFP). Exploiting the additive homomorphism of Pedersen commitments, ACFP reconstructs each grid constraint directly from per-bus commitments, reducing feeder-wide feasibility verification over any public grid constraints to a single aggregated range proof over the hidden allocation, with a reveal-and-recompute challenge that catches feasible yet unfair clearings. We introduce congestion-responsibility fairness (CRF), a metric scoring curtailment against each party's physical responsibility for congestion rather than consumption. We evaluate GRIDSHIELD against three prior P2P energy-trading designs across four feeders, including a 240-node Midwest feeder with real hourly loads, on a live Hyperledger Fabric network benchmarked with Hyperledger Caliper. GRIDSHIELD proves an entire round feasible with a few-kilobyte proof and no trusted setup, rejects infeasible allocations two of the three compared designs accept, and sustains $\approx$1064 tx/s.

papers.title: Autonomous ETL Pipelines for Salesforce M&A Consolidation: A Reference Framework, Jitterbit Mapping, and Reproducible Simulation Study
papers.abstract: Merging companies that each run Salesforce must consolidate their customer data into a single organization while both source systems remain in use. This requires reconciling different schemas and picklists, resolving duplicate customers across and within organizations, preserving relationships between records, and keeping the target current until cutover. This article proposes a reference framework for an autonomous extract-transform-load pipeline for this task. It combines partitioned bulk extraction, declarative mapping templates, rule-based and statistical quality gates, master data management with deterministic and blocked fuzzy matching, constrained loading with per-record error capture, and change data capture guarded by a data-health circuit breaker. Each stage is mapped to Jitterbit Integration Studio constructs. The framework was implemented as an open reference prototype and evaluated on synthetic two-organization scenarios with known ground truth at three scales, from 32,040 to 383,973 source records, over five random seeds. At a preset threshold, hybrid matching reached pairwise F1 scores of 0.918 for accounts and 0.885 for contacts; calibrating the threshold per object would raise these to 0.938 and 0.963. The quality gates prevented all load failures and all silent loss of unmapped picklist values without wrongly flagging any clean record, whereas removing them produced about 1,000 load failures per run. Over five simulated days of hourly incremental synchronization, replayed events were ignored, an injected upstream fault was contained in the batch in which it occurred, and the target agreed with a full rebuild on more than 99.3 percent of field values. Validation on a production deployment remains future work.

papers.title: On rational curves relative to a divisor
papers.abstract:
Let $X$ be a smooth complex projective variety and $D$ a reduced simple normal crossings divisor. We prove that, given a complete curve of negative $(K_X+D)$-degree, through its general points there is a rational curve whose normalization meets $D$ in at most one point. The proof uses ordinary weighted jets of a smooth family constructed from $(X,D)$, a positive parameter line bundle, and an intersection calculation on a ruled surface. We obtain an explicit degree bound depending on a projective embedding.
  We apply this construction to a cyclic cover compactification associated with a smooth Campana orbifold $(X,\sum_i(1-1/m_i)D_i)$. If its anticanonical divisor is big, we show that there is a covering family of free divisible Campana rational curves with fixed numerical class and contact data. In Picard number one case, the orbifold is Campana rationally connected.

papers.title: Deterministic Oracle Complexity for Goldstein Stationarity in Nonsmooth Nonconvex Optimization with Constraints
papers.abstract: We consider the deterministic oracle complexity of finding a $(\delta,\epsilon)$-Goldstein stationary point of a Lipschitz function under constraints. The problem is posed in $\mathbb{R}^d$, where $d$ denotes the dimension; constraints are specified either by a closed feasible set or by a single explicit inequality. For closed feasible sets that are star-shaped with respect to an interior ball, including all convex bodies, we use a resisting-oracle construction to show that every deterministic algorithm needs $\Omega(\epsilon^{-2})$ objective-oracle calls in the worst case when $d\gtrsim\epsilon^{-2}$ and $\delta\lesssim\epsilon$. For explicit inequalities satisfying uniform Goldstein constraint qualification and strict feasibility, finding Goldstein KKT stationary points requires exponentially many oracle calls in $d$ in the worst case, even at fixed stationarity accuracy. This exponential dependence holds under dimension-independent constraint regularity and strict-feasibility bounds, with a sufficiently small neighborhood radius and complementary slackness error. The result covers common constraints such as ball and box constraints and also allows nonconvex feasible regions. For convex coercive constraints with a Slater point, the resisting-oracle argument also gives an $\Omega(\epsilon^{-2})$ oracle-call bound in the same dimension and radius regime while allowing a larger complementary slackness error. These results hold for all deterministic algorithms using a local oracle, whether or not the returned point was queried. Each constructed objective has a strictly feasible global minimizer; the lower bounds therefore concern the information required to find stationary points, not their existence.

papers.title: Intra-Architecture Source Attribution for Stable Diffusion: A New Task with Benchmark Dataset and Baseline
papers.abstract: Designing systems that attribute a generated image to its source model has lately become a major area of AI research. Most existing datasets and systems related to image source attribution are targeted towards the detection of architectural signatures of the source models. Distinct from this, focusing on stable diffusion, we introduce a novel task, IntrAA-SD, Intra-Architecture source Attribution for Stable Diffusion, where the source models to be differentiated share the same architectural backbone and differ only due to fine-tuning. The proposed task aligns with the emergence of fine-tuned generators having the same architecture, like Juggernaut XL and RealVis XL, which are fine-tuned versions of Stable Diffusion XL (SDXL). We provide a first-of-its-kind $140$K-image benchmark dataset containing images generated from different fine-tunes of SDXL, along with in-domain and out-of-distribution prompts. We also provide a baseline framework for IntrAA-SD, which leverages a style-conditioned Mixture-of-Experts network. It uses a frozen CLIP backbone to capture the image style and gate the MoE, which processes fine-tuned trace features from a high-resolution LoRA-adapted DINOv2 network. The fine-tuned models used, the prompting strategies considered, and the formation details employed in the novel dataset are elaborated. Our baseline intra-architecture source attribution method is evaluated in terms of attribution accuracy on our dataset, and ablation studies are also performed. Code and dataset is available at https://github.com/mallikagarg/IntrAA-SD.

papers.title: Modulating Merging Strengths via Joint Loss Estimation for LoRA-based Continual Learning
papers.abstract: Continual learning (CL) aims to adapt models to new tasks while preserving previously learned knowledge. Recently, Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), a representative Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) method, has gained increasing attention in CL due to its efficiency and scalability. Several LoRA-based merging methods maintain a single inference model by scaling the newly learned LoRA update with one coefficient and merging it into the previous weights after each task. However, they usually control the whole update with a shared scalar factor, although different update elements may affect previous and current tasks in different ways. To address this issue, we propose Merging Strength Modulation via Joint Loss Estimation (M2LE). It consists of Hessian Information-guided Adaptive Merging (HIM) and Task Simulation Perturbation for Merging (TSP). Instead of searching for a global merge coefficient, HIM directly solves for the target merged update under a joint objective over previous and current tasks. Solving this objective gives an analytic solution that naturally takes the form of element-wise modulation over the current task LoRA update. To improve the stability of the learned update under subsequent merging, we introduce TSP which simulates different tasks interference. Experiments on multiple benchmarks show that M2LE consistently outperforms existing PEFT-based continual learning methods. Code is available at https://github.com/bbdeeer/M2LE_NeurIPS2026.

papers.title: Intersection Product Formulas and Integral Dependence
papers.abstract: We prove the intersection product formulas of Gaffney and Gassler for polar multiplicities and Segre numbers over arbitrary Noetherian local rings. For equidimensional and universally catenary rings, we give a geometric refinement of the Principle of Specialization of Integral Dependence, in which the maximal dimension of the images of exceptional components mapping into the hypersurface determines a precise Segre number that strictly increases.

papers.title: The determinantal complexity of the 4*4 permanent is 15
papers.abstract:
The best known lower bound on the determinantal complexity of the 4x4 permanent is 10. In this short note, I prove that this value is exactly 15: the 4x4 permanent is the determinant of a 15x15 matrix of affine linear forms, and cannot be that of any smaller matrix. To do so, I must establish both a lower and upper bound. To establish the upper bound, I use Grenet's construction of size 2^n-1. Hence that construction is optimal at n=4 (and n=3). This now constitutes the first knwon exact value of the determinantal complexity of the permanent at n=4. Only the value at n=3 was exactly known, prior to this note. The general quadratic bound only gives 8 for n=4.
  To establish the lower bound, I work from a normal form at a zero of the permanent. In the first row (and column) of the normal form, the linear forms vanish on a linear space inside the singular locus of the permanent. A hessian inequality bounds the size of the matrix in terms of that space. Then, a matrix of sie 14 foces the space into any of nine corordinate types. The forcing is either up to symmetry, or else into a family that degenerates to one of them. I then rule out every case. All involved computations are exact.
  In respect of the claim, I have made all certificates public.

papers.title: Deep-Learning Algorithm for Indeterminate Thyroid Nodules: Comparison and Combination with Molecular Testing
papers.abstract: Thyroid nodules with indeterminate cytology (Bethesda III) carry an intermediate risk of malignancy, and molecular testing is widely used to decide between surgery and surveillance, but it is costly and not universally available. We investigated whether a convolutional neural network (CNN) applied to routine ultrasound images can stratify Bethesda III nodules, and how it compares and combines with molecular testing. We retrospectively identified 466 nodule records from 418 patients who underwent molecular testing (Afirma or ThyroSeq). A CNN pre-trained on determinate nodules was adapted to indeterminate nodules with soft labels and transfer learning. After removal of duplicate records, 119 nodules with surgical pathology were used for development and 47 were held out for testing. On the test set, the deep learning (DL) model achieved an AUC of 0.73 (95% CI 0.51-0.94), compared with 0.55 (0.38-0.71) for molecular testing (P = 0.15). At a cut-off inherited from the original algorithm, the DL model was more specific than molecular testing (0.95 vs 0.32; P < 0.001), with a higher positive predictive value (0.67 vs 0.21), a lower sensitivity (0.44 vs 0.78; P = 0.25) and a similar negative predictive value (0.88 vs 0.86). All six DL-positive test nodules were molecular-positive, and the DL output split the molecular-positive nodules into a high-risk (4/6 malignant) and a lower-risk group (3/27 malignant; P = 0.01). Surgical verification was strongly driven by the molecular result (99% of positive vs 19% of negative results), and molecular-test accuracy depended on the platform. A logistic regression of the DL output, nodule size and the molecular result dropped the DL term and did not improve on the DL output alone. Ultrasound DL complemented molecular testing for Bethesda III nodules, in particular by identifying molecular-positive nodules at lower risk of malignancy.

authors.name: Jichen Yang
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Prior-data fitted networks for variable selection
papers.abstract: Prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) have become state-of-the-art for tabular prediction but remain underexplored in other areas of statistics. In this work, we present two PFNs for Bayesian variable selection: CD-PFN identifies conditional dependencies, and PC-PFN identifies parents and children in a causal graph. Both networks estimate posterior inclusion probabilities (PIPs) without posterior samples or data-specific modeling. In semi-synthetic and real data experiments, CD-PFN and PC-PFN often outperform existing methods, demonstrating the value of PFNs for variable selection and their potential in statistics more broadly. Open-source software is available.

papers.title: Ab Initio Accuracy Beyond the Cutoff: Distributed Message-Passing Equivariant Attention at Tens-of-Millions-of-Atom Scale
papers.abstract: Molecular dynamics predicts molecular motion from atomic forces and trajectory integration. Density functional theory (DFT) provides first-principles forces, but its $O(N^3)$ cost limits simulations to thousands of atoms; empirical force fields scale to millions but miss bond breaking and charge transfer. Equivariant message-passing Transformers learn the ab initio potential at linear cost. Stacked layers propagate information beyond a single cutoff, giving four layers a receptive field up to 23{\AA}. At this frontier, scale is limited by communication: layers exchange boundary features across devices, force backpropagation repeats the exchange, and moving atoms change neighbor graphs and tensor shapes. We present Tessera, a distributed runtime that fixes workload shapes between rebuilds. It sorts atoms along a space-filling curve into equal-count shards, ensuring identical atom counts and tensor shapes per rank. Peer sets scale as $K^{0.5}$, not $K$. A conservative neighbor skin preserves topology across updates, enabling each rebuild interval to replay as one CUDA Graph. Fused kernels, three-level neighbor search, and overlapped All-to-All complete it. On 512 GPUs, Tessera sustains 30.7M atoms at 89.7% weak-scaling efficiency (77--90% across three per-GPU loads); per-step time rises 1.11--1.29x as machine and problem grow 16x. Graph reuse cuts full-step time $1.87\times$. Across an $8\times$ device increase, neighbor-search cost grows $1.7\times$, versus $3.0\times$ for Morton order. In a live $10.24$M-atom salt solution, NVE energy drift is $0.42\,\mu$eV/atom/ps over $10$ ps, and structure matches a serial reference. A 10.06M-atom Norovirus capsid sustains 100 ps of NVT at $\approx 8$ ps/day on 256 A100 GPUs. Over 200,000 steps, it has no broken bonds or anomalously close pairs and uses three compiled variants, with no graph breaks or eager fallbacks.

authors.name: Ji Zhang
authors.institution: National Institute for Communicable Disease Control and Prevention

papers.title: The Exact Memory-Rate Tradeoff for Three-User Secure Coded Caching
papers.abstract: We determine the exact zero-error memory-rate tradeoff for secure coded caching with three users and any number $N\ge2$ of independent files. Each user recovers its requested file, while its cache and the broadcast jointly reveal no information about the complete tuple of unrequested files. For $N\ge4$, two converse inequalities establish the optimality of the known achievable points and the memory-sharing segments between them. For $N=3$, two additional bounds identify a new corner at $(M,R)=(3/2,2)$, where memory and rate are measured in file units. An explicit linear code over $\mathbb{F}_3$ attains this corner and reduces the rate by one quarter of a file relative to memory sharing between the known points. The converse links the information held by cache pairs and triples to delivery under repeated and distinct requests. Its equality conditions guide the construction: users cancel the keys to recover their requested files, while uniform masking protects the complete tuple of unrequested files.

authors.name: Han Fang
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

authors.name: Wei Kang
authors.institution: City University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen Research Institute

papers.title: Optimization of Joint Beamforming in RIS-aided Multi-carrier and Multi-user MIMO Systems
papers.abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communication is a promising enabler for beyond-fifth-generation wireless networks. However, RIS phase shifters typically rely on a tuning element (for example a variable-length stub), which can be optimally configured for only one carrier frequency at a time. This constraint complicates RIS deployment in multi-carrier systems and often necessitates additional measures, such as using multiple RIS panels or partitioning RIS elements across carriers. In this work, we propose a novel scheme in which all RIS elements simultaneously serve multiple carriers, delivering improved performance over existing approaches. Our method leverages the multiple reflections captured by physically consistent RIS models to realize the desired phase shifts for all carriers using a single stub length setting. We further develop a joint active and passive beamforming optimization framework tailored to multi-carrier, physically consistent RIS-aided systems. Simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed

papers.title: Role-based Effectiveness of an Epistemic Uncertainty Estimate in Training Models for Semantic Segmentation of 3D LiDAR Point Clouds
papers.abstract: Point cloud segmentation is a fundamental task in 3D data analysis, with applications across robotics, augmented and virtual reality, and remote sensing. However, the inherent sparsity, noise, and unordered nature of point clouds introduce significant challenges, particularly in achieving reliable classification. While the state-of-the-art rely on training models for explicit modeling of uncertainty, there is a gap in exploring different roles that estimated uncertainty using generative approaches can play. This work investigates the impact of deterministic uncertainty in point cloud segmentation by explicitly modeling epistemic uncertainty and using it in different roles, namely, as a feature and in loss function.
