We evaluate a baseline artificial neural network (ANN) and two uncertainty-aware variants (uncertainty as an additional input feature and as a per-sample confidence weight in the training loss) on four large-scale LiDAR benchmarks spanning airborne and mobile acquisition, namely ISPRS Vaihingen, AHN3, Paris-Lille-3D, and Toronto-3D, together with PointNet++ and RandLA-Net references and their uncertainty-augmented counterparts under canonical spatially disjoint train and test splits. Under this protocol, uncertainty-aware modeling improves mean Intersection over Union, recovers minority classes that the baseline ANN never predicts at all, and in half of the configurations improves the alignment between prediction error and estimated uncertainty as measured by Patch Accuracy versus Patch Uncertainty. Our findings indicate that uncertainty can play multiple roles in the segmentation pipeline rather than as a device for improving accuracy alone.

authors.name: Jaya Sreevalsan-Nair
authors.institution: International Institute of Information Technology Bangalore

papers.title: Almost All 3-uniform Hypergraphs are Class 1
papers.abstract: The chromatic index $\chi'(H)$ of a hypergraph $H$ is the smallest number of colors needed to color its edges so that no two adjacent edges share the same color. The chromatic index is trivially bounded below by the maximum degree $\Delta(H)$, and when $\chi'(H)= \Delta(H)$, we say that $H$ is Class 1. It is well known that almost every 2-graph is Class 1, and we extend this result to 3-graphs. We show for $n^{-2/3-1/200}\leq p \leq 0.99$ that the $3$-uniform binomial random hypergraph $H\sim H_{n,p}^{(3)}$ is Class 1 with high probability. We also show that this result doesn't hold for uniformities above $3$. For a broad range of $p$, when $k \geq 4$ and $k \nmid n$, the hypergraph $H \sim H_{n,p}^{(k)}$ is with high probability not Class 1.

papers.title: BMV conjecture and positivity of spectral shift for relatively Schatten perturbations
papers.abstract: We establish BMV-type results and prove the positivity-preserving property and uniqueness of support-normalized spectral shift functions of arbitrary order for semibounded operators with relatively Schatten-von Neumann perturbations. We also derive correlation inequalities in the relative Hilbert-Schmidt case. These results build on a new positivity-preserving property for the trace of a higher-order operator derivative along a relatively Schatten direction and are obtained using methods of multilinear operator integration and approximation.

papers.title: Boxicity of Power Graphs of Finite Nilpotent Groups
papers.abstract:
The \textit{boxicity} of an undirected graph $\Gamma$, denoted as $\operatorname{box}(\Gamma)$, is the smallest non-negative integer $d$ such that $\Gamma$ can be represented as the intersection graph of axis-parallel rectangular boxes in $\mathbb{R}^d$. The \emph{power graph} of a group $G$, denoted as $\operatorname{Pow}(G)$, is an undirected graph whose vertex set is the group itself, with two elements being adjacent if one is a power of the other.
  We determine the exact boxicity of power graphs of finite nilpotent groups. For a cyclic group of order $n=\prod_{i=1}^{r}p_i^{e_i}>1$, where the $p_i$ are distinct primes, we prove that its power graph has boxicity $\sum_{i=1}^{r}e_i-\max_i e_i$. For a finite nilpotent group $G$, let the number of noncyclic odd Sylow subgroups be denoted by $t(G)$. If $G$ has odd order or if $G$ has a cyclic Sylow $2$-subgroup, then $\operatorname{box}(\operatorname{Pow}(G))=\operatorname{box}(\operatorname{Pow}(\mathbb{Z}_{\operatorname{exp}(G)}))+t(G)$, where $\operatorname{exp}(G)$ denotes the \emph{exponent} of a group $G$. When the Sylow $2$-subgroup is noncyclic, and the odd part is nontrivial, the boxicity equals this value or one more, and we characterise precisely when each of these values is attained.
  The boxicity of power graphs of arbitrary finite groups and the exact boxicity of the comparability graph of the Boolean lattice were posed as open questions in Discrete Mathematics, 349(7):115017, 2026. As a consequence of our results, we answer the latter question completely and the former question partially, by computing the exact boxicity of the power graphs of nilpotent groups.

authors.name: Jinia Ghosh
authors.institution: Calcutta National Medical College and Hospital

papers.title: High-dimensional Four-Level Structured Functional Principal Component Analysis for Unbalanced Level Data with Application to Concussion Data
papers.abstract: We implement the Structured Functional Principal Component Analysis (SFPCA) framework of Shou et al. (2015) in a four-level nested setting with arbitrarily unbalanced group sizes at every level of the hierarchy. While the SFPCA framework can in principle accommodate deeper hierarchical structures, practical implementations remain challenging when the number of curves is large and the hierarchy is highly unbalanced. Our contributions are twofold. First, we operationalize SFPCA for four hierarchical levels with arbitrary unbalancedness across units. Second, we propose a memory-efficient computational strategy that makes the analysis of large collections of curves feasible on conventional hardware. In particular, we construct the four design-specific matrices required for the Method of Moments (MoM) estimators of the level-specific covariance operators while controlling their memory footprint, which would otherwise grow prohibitively with the number of curves. We illustrate the approach using three subsets of the NCAA-DoD Grand Alliance Concussion Assessment, Research, and Education (CARE) Consortium dataset (2014-2017).

papers.title: Faster Cluster Decomposition with Stronger Bi-Criteria Guarantee
papers.abstract:
Partitioning the vertex set of a graph $G=(V,E)$ into clusters is a classical problem in computer science. As vertices within clusters should be well connected and cuts between clusters sparse, Oveis Gharan and Trevisan (SODA 2014, [OGT14]) proposed to measure the partition quality using inner and outer conductance, i.e., the bi-criteria guarantee. Specifically, when partitioning $V$ into vertex-disjoint subsets $P_1,\ldots, P_k$, every subgraph induced by $P_i$ should have high conductance, while the conductance of $P_i$ in $G$ should be low. They studied the existence of such a partition and designed a polynomial-time algorithm achieving this guarantee. For more than a decade, their algorithm remained the only one achieving this guarantee on its output clusters.
  In this paper, we study faster cluster decomposition algorithms under the same setup as [OGT14] and prove three results:
  1. We make their existential result algorithmic: Our algorithms run in nearly-linear time, and achieve the same bi-criteria guarantee as the one in [OGT14] up to constant factors, including the asymptotically tight dependence on $k$.
  2. We prove that their existential result holds algorithmically under a much weaker condition on the initial disjoint subsets. To achieve this, we develop a general algorithm framework that boosts the approximation guarantee of a solution: given an $\alpha$-approximate solution to the $k$-way conductance problem, if $\rho_G(k+1)/\rho_G(k)=\Omega\left(\alpha/\varepsilon\right)$, then a $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximate solution can be obtained using only $O(k(1+\log\alpha))$ minimum $s$-$t$ cut computations.
  3. We present a nearly-linear time algorithm that finds clusters with the bi-criteria guarantee. Our algorithm has the same guarantee as the one in [OGT14], which, for any unweighted graph of $n$ vertices and $m$ edges, runs in $\widetilde{O}(knm^2)$ time.

papers.title: Poissonian Pair Correlation and Discrepancy Rates
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of a sequence in $[0,1)$ with Poissonian pair correlation (PPC) and optimal-order star discrepancy $D_N^*=O((\log N)/N)$, and further give a deterministic construction by applying a conditional-expectation rule to a nested dyadic random model. We also show that PPC imposes no universal discrepancy decay rate: for every positive sequence $\rho_N\to0$, there exists a PPC sequence with $D_N^*/\rho_N\to\infty$. Under suitable regularity and growth assumptions, we realize prescribed discrepancy asymptotics, including $D_N^*\sim c_\beta N^{-\beta}$ for every $0<\beta<1$, with $c_\beta>0$. We further construct a PPC sequence satisfying $D_N^*\asymp(\log N)/N$ for all sufficiently large $N$.

papers.title: Distinguishing Initial-Condition and Model Error Using Machine-Learning Weather Models
papers.abstract: Gated and ungated optimizations evaluated in GraphCast and Pangu-Weather. The first panel (upper-left) shows the mean over the 36 dates; remaining panels show first-of-month 12 UTC optimization descents from January-November 2017. The y-axis metric is the summed day 1-10 Z500 RMSE verified against ERA5, expressed as percent change from each model's date-matched control. The gated arm optimizes the initial conditions jointly with a LoRA weight correction; its GraphCast curve uses the initial conditions alone (LoRA removed), the same state Pangu receives. Stars and diamonds mark the lowest Pangu errors in the 5- and 10-day windows, respectively. Percentages above each panel show the best Pangu improvement relative to control for gated (green) and ungated (red) optimization. Ungated outperforms gated on half of dates when stopped early. Gating does not guarantee a better Pangu performance, but it does produce more comparable GraphCast and Pangu-Weather improvements on all 36 cases.

papers.title: Lesion Overlap Ranks PET Segmentation Models but Does Not Certify Patient-Level Tumor Burden
papers.abstract: Metabolic tumor volume (MTV) summarizes whole-body PET disease burden for prognostic stratification and treatment assessment. Automated MTV is useful only if its estimate is reliable for the individual patient, yet segmentation models are usually evaluated with overlap metrics such as Dice rather than burden error. We examined whether overlap metrics identify unreliable MTV estimates using 1,014 autoPET FDG PET/CT studies. We evaluated LesionTracer predictions held out from fine-tuning, compared five selected released models on 489 tumor-positive patients, and examined the findings in 597 PSMA studies. Across the five FDG models, ranking by higher mean Dice gave the same order as ranking by lower mean relative MTV error ($\rho=-1.00$, exact $p=0.017$). At the patient level, however, out-of-fold Dice tracked relative MTV error strongly ($\rho=-0.75$), yet 82 of 489 patients (16.8\%) fell on opposite sides of the Dice 0.80 and MTV-error 25\% thresholds. Within the training-exposed released models, correlations ranged from $-0.47$ to $-0.74$ over narrower, high-Dice ranges. Out of fold, opposing false-positive and false-negative volumes cancelled about one third of spatial error in net MTV. In 236 of 489 patients, each of the five models missed at least one lesion, though not necessarily the same lesion. Thus, agreement in average model rankings did not establish the reliability of individual MTV estimates or reveal shared lesion misses. PET segmentation benchmarks should report patient-level MTV error and missed-lesion counts alongside Dice and other overlap metrics.

papers.title: Predictability over Volatility: When simple strategies help households save on fuel
papers.abstract: What reasonable strategies can households use to save on gasoline or diesel purchases under different pricing functions? We assess basic strategies households might employ under a simplified model of a 10-gallon tank, fixed fuel consumption between refill opportunities, and price changes at each opportunity to refill. Purchases always fill the tank, and if the tank is empty, it must be refilled regardless of price. We explore three strategy types: price-independent (filling once the tank is below a specific level), price-dependent (filling when the price is below the last $n$ days or their average), and mixed (filling only below a set level, and then only when the price is below the last $n$ days or their average). We construct price functions from the nearest-in-time US weekly averages of regular gasoline and diesel, filling in higher-frequency values with a smoothing spline, linear interpolation, and random draws from normal and uniform distributions based on national averages. Additional simulations are built using Brownian motion. Together, these pricing models span a wide range of volatilities. We find that price-independent strategies are effective for the spline and linear functions, which have low volatility, while price-dependent strategies are effective for the normal and uniform distributions, which are highly volatile. Brownian motion, despite its mid-range volatility, admits no effective strategy. Our findings suggest that the predictability of price movements, whether prices trend or revert toward a stable level, matters more for household strategies than overall volatility: the random walk is volatile in the middle of our range yet offers households no usable signal. Policymakers can therefore assist households by addressing how prices move from day to day, not only the retail prices they face.

papers.title: CAST-Bench: Tracing Every Sound to Its Source in Multi-Shot Audio-Video Generation
papers.abstract: Existing benchmarks for joint text-to-audio-video (T2AV) generation evaluate perceptual quality and audiovisual alignment, but balanced sound-source sam?pling and separate reporting by shot structure remain limited. This makes it dif?ficult to determine whether a specific sound is missing, attributed to the wrong source, or lost across shot transitions. To address this, we introduce CAST?BENCH, a benchmark designed to trace every generated sound back to its in?tended source in multi-shot audio-video generation. The core idea is to formu?late T2AV correctness as an audiovisual contract in which each requested sound must be emitted by the right source, synchronized with the corresponding visual action, and carry the right semantic content. Concretely, the benchmark orga?nizes 900 prompts into 9 sound-source categories, with 100 prompts per cate?gory, spanning speech, animals, instruments, ambient sounds, and other emitter types. The prompts include 439 single-shot and 461 multi-shot narratives, each derived from a structured specification that links every audio event to its emit?ter, subject, and temporal slot. The benchmark provides an 18-metric evaluation suite covering three dimensions: Visual Performance, Content Consistency, and Audio & Semantic Alignment. We further benchmark 12 representative gen?erators and find that visual quality is nearly saturated across leading systems, yet audio semantic scores still differ markedly. Across the nine shared mod?els, multi-shot prompts receive lower aggregate scores under the subset-specific scoring rules and yield different model rankings. Multi-person speech, con?sistent speaker identity across shots, and cross-shot event retention remain the main unresolved challenges. All prompts and evaluation code are available at https://github.com/yucong-liu/CAST-Bench-public.

authors.name: Weijie Kong
authors.institution: Institute of Optics and Electronics, Chinese Academy of Sciences

papers.title: Shotgun Assembly of the Non-Uniform Labeled Lattice Model
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the graph shotgun assembly problem in the labeled lattice model, as introduced by Mossel and Ross (2019). We start with a $d$-dimensional lattice of length $n$, where the color of each vertex is sampled i.i.d. from a distribution $\pi$. Then, we ask whether it is possible to reconstruct the coloring of the lattice given the coloring of each subgrid of length $k$. While previous work by Ding and Liu (2023) and Demidovich, Panichkin, and Zhukovskii (2023) identified the reconstruction threshold when $\pi$ is uniform, we examine the non-uniform case. This paper establishes a sufficient condition for the impossibility of reconstruction for $d \geq 2$ using information-theoretic arguments. Our negative result matches the known threshold in the uniform case.

authors.name: Andrew Jin
authors.institution: U.S. Army Engineer Research and Development Center

papers.title: Identifying Compact Object Candidates using Gaia DR3 Astrometric Accelerations and Jerks
papers.abstract: Gaia Data Release 3 (DR3) provides astrometric measurements for more than a billion sources, hundreds of thousands of which have non-single-star astrometric solutions that indicate deviations from linear proper motion. Although sources with orbital solutions have been extensively inspected for compact objects via the astrometric mass function, two other solution types--the 7-parameter constant-acceleration solutions characterized by $\dot{\mathbf{\mu}}$, and the 9-parameter variable-acceleration solutions characterized by $\dot{\mathbf{\mu}}$ and $\ddot{\mathbf{\mu}}$--have not been as carefully explored. In this work, we develop a methodology for selecting sources within the Gaia DR3 9-parameter non-single-star astrometric solutions that are most likely to host massive compact companions. We assume that a source is the luminous star in a binary orbit around a dark object and derive analytic expressions for the sky-projected accelerations and jerks for three binary populations with different orbit approximations: inclined eccentric, face-on eccentric, and face-on circular. Using POSYDON, we develop a fourth, more realistic population of binaries, each consisting of a luminous star and a black hole. For each population, we address observational biases using gaiamock and select only the systems it fits with a 9-parameter solution. We find that binaries likely to host massive compact companions can be identified from the characteristic joint astrometric accelerations and jerks exhibited by the luminous stars, despite 9-parameter fits under-constraining full orbits. Finally, to illustrate the utility of our approach, we analyze a historical object of interest, HD 12871, and examine 9-parameter fits of Gaia BH3-like binaries.

papers.title: IC-rigidity and generalizations of a theorem of Mahler
papers.abstract: Mahler showed that for every irrational $\alpha$ and every base ${b\geq 2}$, there is a single positive integer $n$ such that every digit in $\{0, \dots, b-1\}$ occurs infinitely often in the base-$b$ expansion of $n\alpha$. Furstenberg later observed that dynamical methods can be used to give a different proof. Building on this perspective, we give generalizations of Mahler's theorem in two directions: the multipliers are a syndetic subset of certain multiplicative semigroups, and analogous versions hold in higher dimensions. Our main tool is IC-rigidity, a type of rigidity which is a hybrid of topological and measurable constraints.

papers.title: VIPBench: A Human-Aligned Benchmark for Voice Identity Perception in the Age of Voice Cloning
papers.abstract: Speaker-recognition benchmarks test how accurately a model recovers the speaker label of a recording, treating voice identity as a property of the person who produced it. However, these benchmarks do not evaluate how humans perceive voice identity. Whether a listener hears two voices as the same person has consequences for intellectual property rights, cybersecurity, and everyday life. We introduce the Voice Identity Perception benchmark (VIPBench), which contains 124,876 same-or-different judgments from 1,290 listeners on 9,800 recording pairs from 100 public figures. The pairs include real recordings, voice clones generated by a text-to-speech system, and morphs between two speakers' voices. We also define four tasks that evaluate the alignment between speaker-representation models and human identity perception. The first two tasks measure how well a model's similarity score predicts the proportion of listeners who respond "same" and the majority response. The other two measure whether a model and listeners find the same speaker pairs similar, and whether a model's relationship to listener judgments holds equally for real and synthetic recordings. We evaluate eleven publicly available speech models. Listener judgments diverge from speaker labels most often for voice clones: in 41% of responses, listeners judged a clone and a real recording of the same speaker to be different people. No model reaches the noise ceiling; the best model explains 61% of the explainable variance. Models trained with speaker labels align with listeners better than self-supervised models do, yet a model with a 12% error rate on speaker labels aligns with listeners as well as models with error rates below 2%. VIPBench enables the evaluation of speaker models against human perception on real, cloned, and morphed speech, and our results motivate training speaker models directly on listener judgments.

papers.title: Evanescent-Depth-Engineered High-Q topological Cavities for Strong Photon-Exciton Coupling
papers.abstract: Due to the inherent scattering in topological edge states, the topological resonant cavity (TRC) formed by their interference exhibits a relatively low quality factor (Q). To address this issue, we propose the mechanism of engineering the transverse evanescent depth of edge states to achieve high-Q in irregular shaped TRCs, which further enables strong photon-exciton coupling at the single-quantum level. By adjusting the intra- and inter-cell coupling strengths in the pseudo-spin topological photonic crystal, the transverse evanescent depth of edge states is greatly reduced, thereby suppressing the scattering of TRCs. Consequently, the Q of various shaped TRCs with 2 ~ 3 um size is up to 10^5 ~ 10^6 in the visible, so that the strong photon-exciton coupling is achieved. The high-Q topological cavities hold promising application in integrated lasers, sensors, cavity quantum electrodynamics, and quantum photonics.

authors.name: Zihan Mo
authors.institution: Collaborative Innovation Center of Quantum Matter

authors.name: Ying Gu
authors.institution: Second Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University

papers.title: Spatial Differences Analysis of Nodal Frequency Considering Frequency-Voltage Coupling
papers.abstract: The rising penetration of inverter-based resources (IBRs) brings rich control dynamics that can amplify spatial differences in nodal frequency through frequency-voltage (F-V) coupling. Existing analyses often neglect voltage dynamics or only examine the aggregate frequency, leading to overoptimistic evaluation of frequency security. To address these drawbacks, this paper develops a unified model of synchronous generators (SGs), grid-following (GFL)-IBRs, and grid-forming (GFM)-IBRs based on the magnitude and phase dynamics of equivalent internal electromotive force (EMF). Integrating these source models with network equations yields a sparse implicit closed-loop model, which fully captures the device-network F-V coupling without transfer-matrix inversion. Then, the obtained nodal responses are decomposed into common and differential modes. Using this decomposition, coupling indices and pole-residue analysis reveal how F-V coupling can amplify spatial differences in nodal frequency and how source configuration and parameters modify this effect. Finally, case studies on the modified IEEE 39-bus and 118-bus test systems validate the proposed model and demonstrate its computational efficiency.

authors.name: Donghai Zhu
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Jiabing Hu
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: An ambient metric framework for sharp compactness of the constant $Q_{2N}$-curvature problem
papers.abstract:
We develop a geometric method for studying $C^{2N}$-compactness of positive solutions to the constant $Q_{2N}$-curvature equation on closed Riemannian $n$-manifolds, for every integer $N\ge1$ and every dimension $n>2N$.
  Assuming the GJMS operator is invertible, its Green function is positive, and the positive mass condition holds, we establish sharp dimension ranges for the compactness of the set of all positive solutions with prescribed positive constant $Q_{2N}$-curvature. The largest dimension for compactness is $24$ for $N=1$ ([21]), $2N+20$ for $N=2,3$ ([11]), $2N+19$ for $N=4,5$, $2N+18$ for $N=6,7,8$, $2N+17$ for $9\le N\le17$, and $2N+16$ for all $N\ge18$. The constructions in [4,5,33,11] for $N=1,2,3$ and in the companion paper [12] for $N\ge4$ give noncompact examples in every dimension exceeding the corresponding compactness bound. We show that these $L^{\infty}$-unbounded examples can be chosen to satisfy the same operator and mass hypotheses, proving sharpness within this class.
  Our method relates the Pohozaev quadratic forms to the Hessian $D^2\mathscr{F}(g_c)$, where $\mathscr{F}$ is the volume-normalized total $Q_{2N}$-curvature functional and $g_c$ is the standard round metric on $\mathbb{S}^n$. The ambient metric argument of [12] supplies an explicit formula for $D^2\mathscr{F}(g_c)$ on transverse-traceless tensors. The York decomposition projects metric perturbations onto this space. The scalar--vector--tensor decomposition represents the Pohozaev quadratic forms by explicit finite-dimensional matrices. We prove that these matrices are positive definite throughout the stated dimension range, a crucial step in establishing compactness.

papers.title: Chronos: Sequential Identity-Preserving Video Generation by Temporal Anchoring
papers.abstract: Identity-preserving video generation aims to synthesize high-quality and visually realistic videos from textual and visual conditions while faithfully maintaining the subject's identity across diverse motions. Prior methods have extensively introduced reference-guided control signals and identity-aware conditioning to improve facial alignment from reference images. However, improving static identity alignment alone creates a fundamental tension between identity fidelity and temporal controllability, which frequently causes identity drift or motion suppression under large pose variations and multi-segment sequential actions. To address this, we propose Chronos, a framework that unifies single-segment facial identity preservation and multi-segment sequential action generation under a common temporal formulation. Specifically, Chronos integrates Semantic Prompt Anchoring to adaptively refine the user prompt, Visual Frame Anchoring to transform conditions into visually grounded keyframe anchors for visual guidance, and Metric-Guided Candidate Routing to select the highest-quality videos from heterogeneous generators via multi-dimensional evaluation. Extensive evaluations demonstrate the superiority of our approach, which achieved first place in both Track 1 and Track 2 of the ACM MM 2026 Identity-Preserving Video Generation Challenge, demonstrating its effectiveness across both facial identity preservation and sequential action generation settings.

authors.name: Wenchuan Wang
authors.institution: North China University of Water Resources and Electric Power

authors.name: Xiaoxiao Sheng
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Reflection-Robust Stereo Visual-Inertial Odometry via Kalman-Filtered Ground-Height Estimation
papers.abstract: Visual-inertial odometry relies on visual features that correspond to 3D points with consistent projections across sequential frames. In reflective indoor-floor environments, however, specular floor patterns can be detected and triangulated as virtual features below the physical ground plane, producing unreliable feature associations and inconsistent visual residuals. This paper proposes a lightweight reflection-aware front-end for feature-based stereo VIO. Rather than suppressing all floor-region features, the proposed method estimates the ground height in real time and rejects only feature candidates whose inferred 3D positions are below the estimated ground height. A floor-region mask restricts the validation process to reflection-prone regions, while stereo height uncertainty and pose uncertainty are used to construct frame-level ground-height measurements. A scalar Kalman filter with Normalized Innovation Squared (NIS) gating then provides a stable ground-height estimate, and an uncertainty-aware safety margin is used for selective below-ground virtual feature rejection. Experiments on real reflective-floor indoor sequences show that the proposed front-end generally improves trajectory accuracy in reflection-dominant environments while maintaining accurate ground-height estimates and recovering from actual ground-height changes.

papers.title: Hotplug Coded Caching: Embedding the YMA and Interference Elimination Schemes via Reed--Muller Codes
papers.abstract: In the hotplug coded caching model, $K$ users fill their caches of size $M$ as a function of $N$ files, but only an unknown subset of $A<K$ users is active in the delivery phase. We recently showed that (i) under uncoded placement, offline users cause a strict load penalty at intermediate memory sizes, so that coded placement is needed; and (ii) for $AM\leq N$, every classical scheme with row-wise placement, including the scheme of Gomez-Vilardebo (GV), can be embedded in a Reed-Solomon code, which removes the penalty. In this note, we show that every point of the scheme of Yu, Maddah-Ali and Avestimehr (YMA) for a classical system with $A$ users is achievable in the hotplug model for every $K\geq A$. Each user is associated with a hyperplane and each file with a homogeneous polynomial; each user caches the restriction of the polynomial to its hyperplane, and the subfiles seen by the active users are the values of the polynomial at the points where their hyperplanes meet. This is a projective Reed-Muller code, which reduces to the Reed-Solomon code when each subfile is cached by one user. We then show, by an existence argument, that every classical scheme whose cache is a linear compression of the Maddah-Ali-Niesen cache and whose correctness holds for generic coefficients can also be embedded over a sufficiently large field; this includes the interference elimination (IE) schemes of Tian and Chen. These embeddings complement the Reed-Solomon one, which allows any row-wise placement and any delivery. Together with past work, our results show that every point attained by a GV, YMA or IE scheme ($N\leq A$ for IE), and every corner point of the linear tradeoff for $A=N=3$, is achievable in the hotplug model with a load that does not depend on $K$. Whether the optimal hotplug tradeoff depends only on $A$ remains open, but these results support a positive answer.

papers.title: Estimation of Very High Energy Electron (VHEE) beam parameters using an in-air screen
papers.abstract: Very high energy electron (VHEE) beams offer several promising properties for radiotherapy. Accurate beam delivery requires a beam model that accounts for scattering along the beam propagation path. This work develops and validates a beam model incorporating Multiple Coulomb Scattering (MCS) to estimate beam parameters. MCS is incorporated as an additive term to the covariance matrix transformation for a drift space, allowing conventional quadrupole scans to estimate beam parameters in the presence of a downstream scatterer. The scattering correction factor is fitted to Monte Carlo (MC) simulations for a range of materials and thicknesses. The model is then validated by recovering the initial beam parameters from simulated quadrupole scans of a realistic beamline. Finally, the method is applied to in-air screen measurements at the Pulsed Energetic Electrons for Research (PEER) end station of the Australian Synchrotron. After fitting the correction factors, the mean and standard deviation of the estimation errors for the final emittance, diameter, divergence, and mean kinetic energy were $(-0.06 \pm 3.17)\%$, $(0.15 \pm 0.66)\%$, $(0.18 \pm 2.18)\%$, and $(-0.03 \pm 0.06)\%$, respectively. Simulated quadrupole scans successfully recovered the initial beam parameters, with errors of at most $13\%$. PEER measurements yielded emittance estimates ranging from $0.238$ to $1.753~\mathrm{mm\,mrad}$ across scans, which were within the expected range. Following an initial quadrupole scan, the method allows the in-air beam size to be estimated for other quadrupole configurations. Further work is required to improve the consistency and reliability of the experimental estimates.

papers.title: Persona Perspectives: Adopting Viewpoints Reorganizes Representations in LLMs
papers.abstract: Common methods for monitoring features in large language models (LLMs) such as linear probes and sparse autoencoders (SAEs) assume that features maintain a consistent representation across contexts. LLMs, however, can flexibly adopt different perspectives or "personas" that suggest different underlying systems of conceptual relations. In this paper, we examine whether prompting an LLM to adopt a persona alters the representational geometry of the model's latent space. We extract representations of over 9,000 common words and 33 semantic axes from models adopting liberal and conservative political personas and compare these against two neutral baselines. We find that persona conditioning systematically alters both the projections of words onto semantic axes and the alignments among the axes themselves in directions consistent with the specified ideology. We then test the implications of this reorganization for two safety-relevant features: truthfulness and morality. Linear probes, SAE-based classifiers, and classifiers built from manually selected word representations, all trained without a persona, produce divergent results when applied to models conditioned on political personas, producing politically slanted ratings of truth and morality on controversial statements. These findings suggest that internal representations, as they are conventionally extracted, can exhibit different geometric relations when the model adopts personas, potentially undermining monitoring efforts.

papers.title: Existence of a Normalized Mountain Pass Solution for a Coupled Cubic Schr\"odinger System with Partial Confinement
papers.abstract: This paper studies a mass supercritical Schr\"odinger system with partial confinement: $$ \begin{cases} -\Delta u_1+|y|^2u_1 =\lambda_1u_1+\mu_1u_1^3+2\beta u_1u_2^2,\qquad x\in\R^3,\\ -\Delta u_2+|y|^2u_2 =\lambda_2u_2+\mu_2u_2^3+2\beta u_1^2u_2,\qquad x\in\R^3, \end{cases} $$ subject to the mass constraints $ \int_{\R^3}u_1^2\dd x=a_1$, $\int_{\R^3}u_2^2\dd x=a_2,$ where $x=(y,z)\in\R^2\times\R$, the parameters $\mu_1,\mu_2,\beta$ are positive, and $\lambda_1,\lambda_2\in\R$ are unknown Lagrange multipliers. The masses satisfy $(a_1,a_2)=\eps(\rho_1,\rho_2)$ for a fixed vector $\rho=(\rho_1,\rho_2)\in (0,\infty)^2$. For all sufficiently small $\eps>0$, we establish the existence of a positive normalized solution $u_\eps^-$ at a mountain pass level on the full product mass sphere. This level coincides with the infimum of the energy over the negative part of the Pohozaev set. The main difficulty arises from the lack of compactness due to partial confinement. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a compactness argument that preserves the two independent mass constraints and show that every minimizing sequence for this infimum admits a strongly convergent subsequence after suitable common translations along the unconfined axial direction. We further establish the asymptotic relation $\eps E(u_\eps^-)\to m_0(\rho)$ as $\varepsilon\to0$, where $m_0(\rho)>0$ denotes the infimum of the free energy under the corresponding Pohozaev constraint. In addition, we derive the asymptotic behavior of the kinetic and potential energies. The solution obtained here is distinct from the normalized ground states constructed by Jia et al. [Discrete Contin. Dyn. Syst., 40(2020), 2739-2766] through local minimization for sufficiently small masses.

papers.title: A sharp Bernstein theorem for affine maximal type surfaces
papers.abstract: We investigate Bernstein theorem for the affine maximal type equation \begin{equation*} \sum_{i,j=1}^nf^{ij}(D^a)_{ij}=0,\qquad D=\det(f_{ij}),\qquad a\neq0, \end{equation*} under completeness of the Calabi metric. In dimension two, we prove that every smooth strictly convex solution on a convex domain is a quadratic polynomial whenever $a\notin[-\tfrac23,-\tfrac13]$, resolving a conjecture of Sun and Xu [25]. For every $n\geq2$, we also construct explicit non-quadratic Calabi complete solutions on convex domains for all $a\in[-\tfrac n{n+1},-\tfrac1{n+1}]$. These examples show that the rigidity range is sharp in dimension two.

authors.name: Ruiwei Xu
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Learning Object-Centric Motion Priors from Human for Robotic Dexterous Manipulation
papers.abstract: Manipulating diverse objects with multi-fingered dexterous hands is challenging due to the high dimensionality and complex dynamics. Human-Object Interaction (HOI) datasets provide rich knowledge about task information and embodied interactions. Instead of solely imitating the human demonstrations, our method learns to holistically predict future hand-object states by leveraging these datasets. The predicted future states of the object can serve as a general-purpose reward term for reinforcement learning, reducing reliance on task-specific reward engineering and enhancing generalization across tasks. We conduct extensive experiments on three manipulation tasks in simulation and the real world. Our approach outperforms existing SOTA methods in both success rate and generalizability on novel objects. Furthermore, we validate the cross-embodiment compatibility of our methods by successfully deploying the skills on different robot hands.

authors.name: Zhengdong Hong
authors.institution: Second Affiliated Hospital of Nanchang University

papers.title: ReactWorld: Structuring Interaction Responses for Embodied Video Generation
papers.abstract: Embodied video world models predict scene changes caused by robot actions, yet generated object responses may remain inconsistent with task intent and contact dynamics. Critical responses in embodied scenes often concentrate in local regions and specific time intervals. Inspired by chain-of-thought reasoning, we introduce ReactWorld, an embodied video generation model guided by structured interaction anticipation. In the generation backbone's feature space, an interaction response field predictor anticipates how the interaction will unfold, explicitly describing participant roles, future motion response intensity, and local motion changes. A response feedback adapter forms increments to object features from the difference between the object branch's outputs with predicted and zeroed local dynamics inputs. It also converts predicted displacements into positional biases for temporal attention. These two mechanisms guide object feature updates and information retrieval across frames, respectively. Through interaction anticipation and generative feedback, ReactWorld achieves an average score of 77.51 on RBench, outperforming PhysisForcing by 3.29 points with improvements in all nine categories. On EZS-Bench, it achieves a Domain score of 86.98 and an average score of 81.87.

papers.title: Fluctuations in Environmental Resource Availability Alter the Oscillatory Tragedy of the Commons
papers.abstract: Environmental noise in real-world complex systems--including fluctuations in temperature, humidity, and related environmental conditions--inevitably modulates individual metabolic capacity and, consequently, the efficiency of public-resource utilization. Yet conventional evolutionary game models incorporating environmental feedback treat resource dynamics deterministically. Here, we incorporate stochastic fluctuations into a noise-corrected replicator-dynamics framework. Theoretical analysis and stochastic birth-death simulations yield a counterintuitive result: moderate environmental noise stabilizes, rather than destabilizes, the interior fixed point across diverse payoff landscapes, while suppressing or eliminating catastrophic oscillations. These findings reframe environmental variability not merely as a perturbation but as a mechanism that fosters strategy coexistence and sustainable resource use in complex social and ecological systems.

authors.name: Yi-Duo Chen
authors.institution: Zhejiang University Medical College Affiliated Stomatological Hospital

papers.title: BiCG-Net: Target-Specific Image Quality Assessment via Observation Modeling and In-Image Differencing
papers.abstract:
We estimate the quality of a specific target region (e.g., a train body) in an image, rather than the whole image. This differs fundamentally from whole-image No-Reference Image Quality Assessment (NR-IQA): when the target occupies a small fraction of the frame, the whole-image score is dominated by background, and no public benchmark provides target-level human Mean Opinion Score (MOS). We estimate target quality via nested sampling - a sequence of patches expanding outward from the target box - and infer quality from the relative structure of this sequence.
  This motivates BiCG-Net, a student network that distills an 11-teacher ensemble through a linear observation model and an in-image differencing mechanism, which provably cancels the target term and teacher-specific bias. We train and test the student independently on each dataset, and evaluate zero-shot transfer across benchmarks. On CSIQ and LIVEC, the student reaches PLCCs of 0.9009 and 0.9133 against human MOS, exceeding the best single teacher and the teacher consensus. On a self-built MOS-free railway dataset, the student reaches a PLCC of 0.9855 against a weak label.
  The student exceeds its teachers because it learns a new mapping from the relative structure of teacher readings to the ground-truth label, rather than mimicking them. Residual analysis on CSIQ and LIVEC shows the prediction residual is significantly correlated with background contamination, teacher dispersion, and label extremity, demonstrating the student extracts information the consensus does not contain. Under CSIQ-to-LIVEC transfer, the frozen student reaches a PLCC of 0.8416, exceeding the consensus by 0.1947. We position BiCG-Net as an offline target-level quality auditing and label-generation engine; its 39,482-parameter student is compact by design, acting as a unifying layer mapping heterogeneous teacher readings onto a common quality scale.

authors.name: Siyuan Liu
authors.institution: Qingdao University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Cycles in Regular Multipartite Tournaments
papers.abstract: We study balanced cycles in regular multipartite tournaments. A cycle in a $c$-partite tournament is $k$-balanced if it contains exactly $k$ vertices from each partite class. We prove that there exists an absolute integer $r_0$ such that every regular $c$-partite tournament with each partite class size of $r\ge r_0$ contains a $k$-balanced cycle for every $1\le k\le r$ when $c=3$ or $c\ge5$, and for every $2\le k\le r$ when $c=4$. In particular, our result confirms three conjectures of Volkmann and Winzen for large regular multipartite tournaments. We also confirm Yeo's conjecture on the existence of $(p,q)$-cycle factors for large regular $c$-partite tournaments $G$ with $c\ge4$, where a $(p,q)$-cycle factor is a pair of vertex-disjoint cycles of lengths $p$ and $q$ spanning $G$.

papers.title: A weak Galerkin finite element method for the coupled Stokess-Biot problem
papers.abstract: In this paper,we consider a stable numerical method for the Stokes-Biot model. We adopt the standard formulation of the Stokes equations coupled with the mixed formulation of the Biot system involving the additional total pressure variable. We construct the semi-discrete scheme on polygonal meshes by employing weak Galerkin finite element methods for spatial discretization. It is convenient to incorporate the interface conditions into the semi-discrete scheme via the edge-based degrees of freedom. Furthermore, we give a fully discrete scheme based on the backward Euler method. We establish the well-posedness of these two schemes and provide a rigorous error analysis. Finally, we present some numerical examples to verify the convergence and stability of our algorithm under a wide range of some physical parameters.

papers.title: Stability of energy gap of macroscopic quantum matter
papers.abstract: In quantum many-body physics and quantum field theory, it is often assumed that gapped systems remain gapped under sufficiently weak local perturbations. However, to what extent this assumption holds is elusive, except for some special systems. In this work, we examine the stability of energy gap of macroscopic quantum matter that is only subject to two physically natural conditions, locality and translation invariance. We first show that in any spatial dimension, there are gapped local Hamiltonians with a unique ground state and an unstable gap, i.e., they become gapless under certain arbitrarily weak local perturbation in the thermodynamic limit. We then prove that for both spin and fermionic systems in one dimension, such Hamiltonians with an unstable gap must not only break translation invariance but also be fine-tuned. We further show that in any dimension greater than one, there are fine-tuned local translation invariant Hamiltonians with a unique ground state and an unstable gap. These results greatly sharpen our understanding of the fundamental problem of the stability of quantum phases of matter. We also discuss implications of our results on, for example, anyon superconductivity and higher-form symmetries.

papers.title: Improved approximation algorithms for capacitated cluster editing
papers.abstract: We study the minimum-disagreement cluster editing problem that, from a complete edge-signed graph, where a positive edge represents two vertices agreeing to each other while a negative represents a disagreement, constructs disjoint cliques of upper bounded size such that the total number of negative edges inside cliques and positive edges outside cliques is minimized. When the sizes of the candidate cliques are unbounded, the problem is NP-hard and APX-hard, and many approximation algorithms with improving ratios have been proposed in the literature and the state-of-the-art approximation ratio of $\alpha = 1.3865 + \epsilon$. The capacitated variant, in which the candidate cliques have sizes no greater than a given $k$, is less studied and the best approximation ratio is $5.37$. In this paper, we study the latter problem. We first present a downsizing procedure that achieves an approximation ratio of $\alpha_k = 2 \alpha + 1$, based on any $\alpha$-approximation algorithm for the uncapacitated problem. Secondly, we propose a hybrid of cluster-LP sampling and pivoting and show that for every fractional capacitated cluster-LP solution of cost $L$, the hybrid using ordinary pivoting has an expected cost at most $\frac 95 L + \frac 1{10} \OPT_k$, and the hybrid using conditional pivoting has an expected cost at most $\frac {306}{203} L + \frac {50}{203} \OPT_k$. A cardinality-constrained adaptation of the approximate dual-separation framework of Garc\'ia-Soriano and Schohn supplies the required fractional solution and yields a randomized $(1.9 + \epsilon)$-approximation algorithm and a randomized $(1.7537 + \epsilon)$-approximation algorithm, respectively.

authors.name: Guangting Chen
authors.institution: Zhejiang University of Water Resource and Electric Power

authors.name: Jiaxuan Ma
authors.institution: Shenyang National Laboratory for Materials Science

papers.title: Whose Values Are Generated? Measuring Visual Value Leakage in Multilingual Text-to-Image Generation
papers.abstract: Text-to-image (T2I) systems serve users across languages and cultural contexts. However, evaluations of cultural representation focus mainly on recognizable elements such as landmarks, clothing, and activities, overlooking the cultural values that generated images convey. To bridge this gap, we introduce VisionValueBench, a multilingual benchmark that operationalizes six of Hofstede's cultural value dimensions (e.g., individualism versus collectivism) to investigate how T2I systems frame neutral social situations through a particular cultural orientation. We find that value-neutral prompts, which admit diverse cultural interpretations, nonetheless yield images that favor particular value orientations, a phenomenon we call visual value leakage. We evaluate prompts varying in language and geographic cues across 960 social scenarios and six T2I configurations. Generated images consistently favor the same value orientations across all six dimensions, for example, equality over hierarchy (low power distance), individual autonomy over group obligation (individualism), and enjoyment over restraint (indulgence). Prompt language has limited influence on these orientations, whereas geographic cues shift some dimensions toward the associated cultural values while largely preserving the prevailing orientations. These findings reveal substantial homogeneity in the cultural values conveyed by T2I systems worldwide.

authors.name: Zucan Lyu
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Binwei Yao
authors.institution: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs

papers.title: Efficient Gaussian Process Modeling for Large Replicated and Censored Data in Industrial Research
papers.abstract: Gaussian process regression is widely used for modeling responses in both physical and computer experiments. In practice, data from physical experiments may include replications and be subject to censoring due to equipment limitations or contextual constraints, and such datasets can be large, posing a scalability challenge for standard Gaussian process inference. Motivated by a real-world industrial research study, we develop a Gaussian process modeling framework that efficiently analyzes large replicated and censored data. Our approach integrates a Vecchia approximation for computational scalability with a likelihood-based formulation that fully exploits replication and rigorously incorporates information from censored observations, analogous to exact simulation from truncated distributions. Through experiments on synthetic data and a real case study from industrial research, we demonstrate that the proposed method yields improved predictive accuracy and reliable uncertainty quantification compared to existing approaches, making it well suited for large-scale applications with structured replication and incomplete data.

authors.name: Shuo Li
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Graph-Mediated Large Language Model Systems in the Agentic Era: Reasoning, Knowledge, Retrieval, Execution, and Coordination
papers.abstract: Graphs play an increasingly important role in large language model (LLM) systems, supporting structural reasoning, knowledge grounding, retrieval, and memory. As these systems evolve toward the agentic era, graphs also organize execution dependencies and multi-agent communication, linking intermediate observations and retained information to subsequent decisions. However, understanding their contribution requires distinguishing the function of each graph operation, the component responsible for its computation, and the subsequent use of its output. This survey introduces an operation-level role--locus taxonomy for reasoning, knowledge and evidence, retrieval and memory, execution, and coordination. We compare how graph observations and external computations guide decisions, how memory representations and updates support later tasks, and how dependencies constrain execution and information delivery. These comparisons distinguish improvements in local metrics from downstream task performance while retaining the conditions under which results were reported. We then organize benchmarks, comparison designs, process diagnostics, and system costs into an evaluation framework. Finally, we identify open challenges in adaptive computation and stopping, memory maintenance, and dependency-aware recovery. The survey provides a basis for assessing when graph mechanisms are useful and for evaluating their effects across components and stages.

authors.name: Haihui Liu
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Advanced Separation Membrane Materials

papers.title: HLA-Net: A Physics-Guided Skeleton-Based Framework for Automatic Gravitational Arc Detection in Astronomical Images
papers.abstract: Gravitational arcs produced by strong gravitational lensing provide a unique approach for investigating dark matter distribution, galaxy cluster mass reconstruction and the structure of the Universe. Automated detection remains challenging because gravitational arcs are rare, often faint and morphologically similar to elongated galaxies.In this paper, we propose \textbf{HLA-Net (Hybrid Lens Arc Network)}, an interpretable multi-stage framework for automatic gravitational arc detection that explicitly exploits both the geometric morphology and physical characteristics of gravitational lensing without requiring manually annotated training datasets.The proposed framework was evaluated on astronomical FITS images containing complex galaxy cluster structures. Starting from 169 initial arc candidates extracted from ordered skeleton representations, the multi-stage verification pipeline reduced the search space to 83 geometrically consistent candidates, while robust circle fitting successfully modelled 113 candidate arc structures. The results demonstrate that HLA-Net effectively suppresses false-positive detections while preserving physically reasonable lens candidates through an interpretable and modular verification strategy.

papers.title: FedCSGA: Evolutionary Client Selection with Joint Statistical and System Heterogeneity in Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative training of machine learning models across distributed clients while preserving data privacy. In practical deployments, FL relies on selecting a client subset in each communication round to reduce communication cost, mitigate stragglers, and improve training efficiency under heterogeneous data and system conditions. In heterogeneous edge computing environments, both statistical heterogeneity and system heterogeneity significantly affect convergence efficiency and model performance. However, existing client selection methods often address these factors independently, overlooking their coupled and dynamic impact across communication rounds. To address this limitation, we propose FedCSGA, a Client Selection method for Federated learning based on Genetic Algorithm. FedCSGA encodes client subsets as chromosomes and evaluates these subsets through a non-linear fitness function that jointly integrates resource-aware metrics and history-aware participation weighting. This design captures subset-level interactions, mitigates persistent selection bias, and balances statistical utility with system efficiency. Extensive experiments on FMNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny-ImageNet demonstrate that FedCSGA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across diverse heterogeneity settings, achieving accuracy improvements of up to 7.0% and faster convergence with fewer communication rounds. These results validate the effectiveness of jointly modeling statistical and system factors to achieve robust and efficient learning in heterogeneous federated environments.

papers.title: De Rham cohomological architectures for PINNs and PDEs with topological holes
papers.abstract: We attempt to alleviate failure modes of classical physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) in scenarios of topological pathologies corresponding to punctures, holes, poles, and voids by introducing de Rham cohomological augmentations, or Hodge-de Rham PINNs. Vanilla PINNs often encounter pitfalls in hole-based settings due to discontinuous interfaces, nonzero closed path integration, path dependence, correspondence to exact forms via the exterior derivative, etc., therefore we absolve traditional failures via parameterizing a 1-form by the Hodge-Morrey-Friedrichs (HMF) decomposition for manifolds with boundary, drawing a connection to de Rham cohomology such as through the HMF isomorphism theorem. 1-forms can act as representations of scalar-valued PDE solutions through integral operator mappings. We propose performing a PINN-based loss on the parameterized 1-form through an associated PDE, which subsequently solves the potential-based PINN problem and moreover remedies the failures of vanilla PINNs via the Sobolev-regular operator under a Fr\'echet differentiation interconnection. The operator relationship often has a nontrivial closed-form and often requires integration or a case-by-case analysis, which we address thoroughly in our experiments. When an integrability condition is not met on our losses, we can equip exhaustion functions to train the networks. We demonstrate our methods on the Aharonov-Bohm effect, which, to our understanding, is largely nonexistent in PINN literature. We develop theoretical guarantees of our methods and demonstrate our pathological safeguards on a broad selection of topologically-adverse problems, including scenarios of inexact forms, and those of nontrivial harmonics and coexact terms.

papers.title: Tight Lower Bounds under Matched High-Order H\"older Smoothness and Uniform Convexity
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we provide tight lower bounds for minimizing high-order H"older-smooth and uniformly convex functions when their orders match. Specifically, we consider functions whose $p^{th}$-order derivatives are H"older continuous with degree $
u$ and parameter $H$, and that are uniformly convex with degree $q$ and parameter $\sigma$. When these orders match, namely, $q = p + 
u$, we show that any deterministic algorithm with access to derivatives up to order $p$ requires $\Omega\left(\left( rac{H}{\sigma}ight)^{ rac{2}{3(p+
u)-2}}\log rac{\Delta_0}{\epsilon}ight)$ oracle calls to reduce an initial optimality gap of $\Delta_0$ to $\epsilon$. This matches the corresponding upper bound and establishes a higher-order uniformly convex counterpart to Nesterov's classical first-order lower bound for strongly convex functions. Rather than directly generalizing Nesterov's classical quadratic-chain construction, we develop a multiscale phase-wise construction that preserves previous oracle responses while maintaining global H"older smoothness and uniform convexity. Our result resolves the matched case left open by existing lower bounds for the two asymmetric regimes.

papers.title: Shock-driven Jetting at HMX Crystal Surface Asperities
papers.abstract: Shock-induced jetting and recompression are plausible mechanisms for hot spot formation in energetic materials, but remain poorly understood. To this end, we apply all-atom nonreactive molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of a shock-loaded sinusoidal surface asperity in the crystalline explosive HMX (octahydro-1,3,5,7-tetranitro-1,3,5,7-tetrazocine) to quantify the roles of shock strength, asperity geometry, system size, and crystallographic orientation in determining the jetting response. Our simulations span a shock pressure interval of $\approx$4-47 GPa, which captures responses in both detonation initiation and steady-state detonation regimes. We find that shock strength and asperity curvature exert strong influence on jet velocity, temperature, and morphology, while feature size and crystallographic orientation play more modest roles. Jet morphology correlates strongly with the HMX ambient-pressure phase diagram and the narrow temperature range associated with its liquid phase. Coherent jets form when focusing and dissipation are sufficient to drive local temperatures above the melting point, while formation of molecular plumes is seemingly connected to jet temperatures exceeding the liquid-vapor transition temperature. Formation of plumes is unlike the jetting responses seen in metals, which typically exhibit liquid phases that are stable over wider temperature intervals. This work proposes a simple hypothesis for the connection between jet morphology and ambient-pressure phase diagrams that can be readily tested in other explosives and metals. It also provides a foundation for ongoing nonreactive and reactive MD simulations of jet impact and recompression to quantify the role played by jets in forming hot spots in HMX-based explosives.

papers.title: When Does Better Confidence Improve a Knowledge-Graph Audit?
papers.abstract: Confidence estimates guide human review in LLM-built knowledge graphs, but better error prediction can yield little improvement in an audit. We study this gap through repairability, selection headroom and label validity. Modelling non-adaptive auditing as budgeted covering, we characterise the minimal decision-relevant error statistics and bound the regret of scalar-preserving first-order planning by a structural mass $\Delta^{\mathrm{cl}}$. We simulate ideal repair against benchmark-aligned labels for five extraction configurations and two cross-document graphs on Re-DocRED, followed by frozen confirmation on test and replication on 500 hash-selected training documents. On the held-out cross-document graphs, an error-rate $\times$ fan-out queue leaves 3.98-4.74 percentage points more errors than a joint model with the same actions. By comparison, opening shared actions for that joint planner reduces residual errors by 0.89-1.43 points relative to its own fact-only plans, in point estimates. Equivalence between joint and independent-block models remains inconclusive. Generic LLM verification improves three of four model-budget configurations on each held-out set. LLM adjudication identifies possible benchmark omissions.

authors.name: Kai Chen
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Chunyu Li
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: InterSim: Innovative Intersection Digital Twins for Human-in-the-Loop Driving Simulation
papers.abstract: Innovative intersection designs can improve roadway safety and operational efficiency, but their uncommon geometries may create challenges for driver comprehension during early deployment. Evaluating these designs through full-scale field implementation can also be costly. This paper presents InterSim, a Unity game engine-based human-in-the-loop (HITL) driving simulator that constructs digital twins of site-specific innovative intersections in a virtual environment. InterSim links the real world and the simulation world through two closed cycles: a digital twin cycle that builds each intersection twin from agency design and traffic data and returns evidence from simulation to the agency, and an HITL cycle in which human drivers or automated driving algorithms operate the ego vehicle under identical scenario conditions. The research capabilities of InterSim are demonstrated through two case studies: a surrogate safety study compares post-encroachment time distributions between a Reduced Conflict Intersection and a standard intersection under different traffic volumes; an eco-driving study compares human drivers with a rule-based agent using vehicle-to-infrastructure information and reveals differences in emission and driving behavior. These studies demonstrate that InterSim provides a reusable digital twin platform for investigating innovative intersection designs from diverse perspectives. Demo video and open-source code can be accessed at https://purduedigitaltwin.github.io/InterSim/

authors.name: Yaguang Li
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Sekai: Incremental Event Memory for Generalized Reasoning Video Segmentation
papers.abstract: Online reasoning video segmentation (Online RVS) requires a model to segment query-referred objects as a video streams in, using only the frames observed so far. Existing formulations largely assume a fixed target set throughout the video, overlooking a fundamental property of streaming reasoning: as new events occur, the objects that satisfy a query may change over time. To address this, we propose a new task, Generalized Reasoning Video Segmentation (GRVS), where the target set depends on query-relevant events accumulated over the observed video history. As new evidence accumulates, the target set can evolve from empty to one or multiple objects, requiring a model to continuously maintain target validity while localizing the valid objects currently in view. To evaluate GRVS, we build Isekai, a diagnostic benchmark of 60 videos and 197 queries across 11 temporal query families, with 12,569 scoring points whose target sets are causally annotated over time. We further propose Sekai, an online framework with two complementary components: an Event Memory Reasoner (EMR) that maintains query-relevant events and evolving target states in structured memory, and a Memory-Grounded Decoder (MGD) that identifies valid targets from this memory and localizes them in the current frame. Experiments show that Sekai significantly outperforms existing online RVS methods, achieving 50.33 J&F and improving over the strongest baseline by 3.2 points. Code, example annotations, and evaluation scripts are available at https://github.com/zenastangbi/Sekai.

authors.name: Zhengtao Liu
authors.institution: Chinese Research Academy of Environmental Sciences

authors.name: Huixin Sun
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Yicong Li
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Joint Association and Beamforming Design for Cooperative ISAC Systems
papers.abstract: Cooperation among multiple base stations (BSs) improves both communication and sensing in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) networks. However, it requires deciding which BSs serve each communication user (CU) and each target, and how each BS beamforms. In this work, we consider joint BS-CU and BS-target association, and beamforming for a general cooperative ISAC system, overcoming prior simplifications such as single-user or target setups, fixed BS roles, coherent radar or separate waveforms. We maximize a joint communication rate and position Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) based tradeoff utility while guaranteeing a minimum service per-CU using a data queue model. We develop a successive convex approximation (SCA)-based beamforming with closed-form updates. The discrete association problem is solved as an overarching layer using a low-complexity algorithm. Numerical results validate the effectiveness of the algorithm and unveil benefits of cooperative communication and sensing.

authors.name: Mehdi Karbalayghareh
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Dallas

authors.name: Xiaoyan Ma
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Architecture and Technology

papers.title: A topological Mundici representation theorem
papers.abstract: We lift Mundici's equivalence between MV-algebras and abelian $\ell$-groups with a strong unit to the topological setting. To this end, we prove that, for every topological MV-algebra, the associated Mundici group can be endowed with a topology that extends the topology of the MV-algebra and makes it into an abelian topological $\ell$-group. Among such topologies there is a finest one; we identify this topology as the topological-group reflection of the bounded-stage final topology, and construct an explicit zero-neighbourhood base in terms of the original MV-algebra topology. Using this topology, we establish a topological Mundici adjunction that restricts to an equivalence between topological MV-algebras and Mundici-fine abelian topological $\ell$-groups with a strong unit. Here, Mundici-fine means that the group topology is the finest $\ell$-group extension of its unit-interval topology. We also identify extremal $\ell$-group extensions under additional hypotheses, and establish a quasitopological correspondence clarifying the distinction between separate and joint continuity.

papers.title: Sure Enough to Share? Overconfidence in GenAI Video Discernment is Associated with Sharing Intentions
papers.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is blurring the line between synthesized and recorded videos, but less is known about people's awareness of their discernment abilities and the consequences of miscalibration. This study examines three forms of overconfidence in GenAI video discernment (i.e., overestimation, overplacement, and overprecision) and their associations with source judgments and sharing intentions in an online study (N = 973). Participants evaluated videos depicting everyday scenes and achieved 62.5% accuracy. Three forms of overconfidence showed distinct patterns: participants overplaced themselves by 12.8 percentile points, but overprecision showed consistent positive associations with sharing intentions and the tendency to classify videos as human-made. Age, GenAI usage, and AI literacy showed consistent positive associations with all three forms of overconfidence. These findings highlight the importance of distinguishing the three forms of overconfidence to better understand GenAI engagement and incorporating metacognition into interventions to support informed media consumption.

authors.name: Sijia Qian
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Charlotte

papers.title: Electron Kinetics in the Sheath of Atmospheric Pressure Plasmas in Helium and Helium:H$_2$O Vapor
papers.abstract: The electron energy distribution function (EEDF) plays a central role in determining the rates of electron-induced reactions in the bulk plasma, the sheath, and at the plasma-surface interface. However, the electron kinetics within the sheath and near the surface are generally not well described by conventional Boltzmann solvers, which neglect the sheath electric field and electron losses to the surface. In this study, we investigate electron kinetics in atmospheric pressure plasmas in pure helium and helium-water vapor mixtures using a hybrid model that combines a fluid description of the collisional sheath with a particle kinetic Monte Carlo model for electrons. The floating wall potential is determined taking into account electron diffusion through the sheath and the non-Maxwellian EEDF. Our results demonstrate that electron kinetics within the sheath can exhibit both local and nonlocal behavior, even at atmospheric pressure. The transition between these regimes is governed primarily by the ratio of the electron energy relaxation length to the sheath thickness. At high plasma densities, where the sheath thickness becomes smaller than the electron energy relaxation length, the EEDFs approach the nonlocal limit, exhibiting significant changes in electron kinetic energy toward the wall. The addition of water vapor reduces the energy relaxation length and shifts the electron kinetics toward the local regime. In the nonlocal regime, the electron mean kinetic energy decreases substantially toward the wall, accompanied by reductions of more than an order of magnitude in electron-impact excitation and ionization rate coefficients. These findings demonstrate that modeling of electron-induced processes in the sheath and at plasma-surface interfaces requires accounting for nonlocal electron kinetics and electron losses to the surface, even at atmospheric pressure.

papers.title: Maximal Unipotent Monodromy and $p$-adic Eigenvalue Formulas
papers.abstract: We establish p-adic formulas for the eigenvalues of Frobenius in the case of the family of hyperkloosterman sums. The deformation equation in this case has maximal unipotent monodromy, and the interplay of Frobenius and the differential equation plays an important role in establishing p-adic analytic formulas for the eigenvalues.

papers.title: Flux-Matched Poisson Iteration for Generated Jacobian Equations: Local Convergence and Spectral Galerkin Approximation
papers.abstract: We develop a flux-matched Poisson iteration for solving generated Jacobian equations with second boundary conditions. In each step, it solves a fixed shifted Poisson problem with a Neumann-type boundary condition. Near a smooth regular solution with positive $C^{1,1}$ densities, we prove that the iteration has local geometric convergence in $C^{2,\alpha}$ on smooth connected Riemannian domains. The iteration is then discretized using a spectral Galerkin method, with local convergence proved for the Fourier-Jacobi scheme on spherical caps. Optical numerical experiments support these estimates and demonstrate useful imaging performance beyond the local convergence theory.

authors.name: Yixuan Zhang
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: The Harmonic Online $k$-Server Algorithm Is Poly(k)-Competitive
papers.abstract: The online $k$-server problem is one of the most fundamental problems in online algorithms. In this problem, $k$ servers are located in a metric space and serve a sequence of requests at points in the metric space by moving a server there. The Harmonic algorithm is a very natural algorithm: it chooses a server with probability inversely proportional to its distance from the request. It is also highly efficient, being memoryless and answering each request in $O(k)$ time. However, its competitive ratio has remained unsettled between the $O(2^k \log k)$ upper bound (Bartal and Grove, JACM 2000) and the $k(k+1)/2$ lower bound (Raghavan and Snir, 1994, IBM J. Res. Dev.). We prove that Harmonic is $2k^4$-competitive on every metric space against adaptive online adversaries. Our analysis uses a potential combining corrected electrical energy with the distances of online servers to their assigned adversary locations.

papers.title: Floquet-Volkov spin polarization in spin-degenerate Antiferromagnets
papers.abstract: Periodic driving enables ultrafast control of electronic structures in solids through the formation of photon-dressed Floquet-Bloch states. However, the measured photoemission spectra are influenced not only by these states but also by their interference with Volkov-dressed outgoing photoelectrons. Here, we demonstrate that Floquet-Volkov interference can generate spin-polarized photoemission in a collinear antiferromagnetic Dirac model without spin-orbit coupling (SOC). An in-plane linearly polarized pump preserves $\mathcal{PT}$ symmetry, leaving the Floquet quasienergies spin degenerate. Under near-resonant driving, photon-dressed conduction and valence bands hybridize, producing spin-dependent relative phases that are converted into unequal spin-resolved photoemission intensities through interference between pathways reaching the same Volkov-dressed final state. We analytically identify this interference mechanism and verify it using nonequilibrium Green-function calculations under periodic driving and finite pump-probe pulses. We further demonstrate that rotating the probe polarization can suppress or reverse the spin polarization without modifying the Floquet bands. Our findings establish Floquet-Volkov interference as a route to spin-selective photoemission in driven antiferromagnets without Floquet spin splitting or SOC.

authors.name: Tongshuai Zhu
authors.institution: China University of Petroleum, East China

papers.title: Route First, See Later: Enabling Vision Agents to Reason Scientifically by Separating Routing Policy from Action Spaces
papers.abstract:
Scientific image-analysis workflows require agents to select among diverse capabilities like description, detection, counting, and segmentation. Current multi-tool architectures conflate intent interpretation with visual execution, masking whether a failure arises from flawed reasoning (misrouting) or failed perception (invalid tool execution). This lack of auditability renders agents unreliable for high-stakes scientific automation. We introduce ZETA, an extensible architecture that operationalizes the decoupling of routing policy from action execution. ZETA resolves scientific intent before invoking specialized visual tools, treating measurement as a deterministic operation grounded in explicit geometry rather than generative output. This architecture exposes the "black box" of agent decision-making, allowing routing correctness and downstream execution to be evaluated as independent failure modes.
  To our knowledge, we provide the first controlled study in scientific vision-agent routing that isolates explicit routing-policy specification while holding the legal action interface fixed. Evaluation on a zero-shot benchmark of 51 scientific-intent queries shows that explicit routing semantics can substantially improve routing accuracy, particularly at semantically adjacent action boundaries, although improvements vary across models. For Qwen 3.8, explicit routing-policy specification improves segmentation routing accuracy from 6.2% to 75.0% and detection routing accuracy from 60.0% to 100%. ZETA's execution traces make routing decisions and downstream artifacts separately observable, providing a basis for distinguishing intent-selection errors from visual execution failures. ZETA establishes the necessary infrastructure to isolate execution errors from interpretive ones, a critical requirement for deploying reliable scientific vision agents.

papers.title: Homology and Topology of Partially Ordered Fields
papers.abstract: We develop a unified homology theory for directed partial orders (DPOs) and lattice-ordered positive cones on fields of characteristic zero. With the underlying field and its operations fixed, we define order?carrying spaces independently by topological conditions, establish a bijection with DPO positive cones, and characterize lattice orders by intersections of minimal open neighborhoods. A unified comparison theorem identifies graded Ext for region ideals with sheaf cohomology and multiplicative Tor with the reduced singular homology of truncated regions, giving a topological interpretation of the existence and preservation of reduced decompositions. We obtain canonical cohomological obstructions to lattice ordering, prove that a coefficient module for positive multiplication is flat if and only if the multiplier has a positive inverse, and show that every strict extension of positive cones on the same field produces a nonzero first Tor obstruction. Finally, we place the concrete lattice recently constructed by Bao-Zhang within this framework.

papers.title: Augmentation with Reinforcement Transformation for Low-textured Scientific Sketch Image Retrieval
papers.abstract: Low-textured sketch images are widely used in scientific applications, including wildlife conservation, archaeological illustration, and forensic composites. Learning from and retrieving such images is challenging because they lack detailed surface textures and visual variations commonly exploited by modern deep learning models. This paper proposes Augmentation with Reinforcement Transformation (ART) to fine-tune pretrained models to learn effective representations for accurate sketch image retrieval. Our key observation is that sketches are particularly sensitive to image transformations, such as rotation, flipping, zooming, and stretching.
