In simulation and on hardware, Ctrl-F completes loco-manipulation that demands large, sustained interaction force and adjusts its command online as the load changes, both out of reach of a force-blind tracker. On hardware, Ctrl-F demonstrates hand-based dragging, pushing, and lifting, as well as foot-based kicking, successfully manipulating boxes weighing up to 20kg in pushing and kicking tasks where the force-blind baseline fails, while adapting online to additional loads introduced mid-task.

authors.name: Jiakang Chen
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Guangzhou Medical University

authors.name: Masayoshi Tomizuka
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

papers.title: Bypass Transition via the Non-Hermitian Skin Effect
papers.abstract: Non-Hermitian skin lattices can directionally amplify propagating signals. Here we show that this amplification and nonlinear feedback together drive a bypass transition to self-sustained motion, familiar from shear flows. A finite local excitation can trigger sustained periodic or chaotic motion while the resting state remains linearly stable. We develop a return-map theory that predicts the triggering threshold, its scaling with directional gain, and the instability governing near-critical dynamics. The threshold decreases exponentially with chain length. Weak noise triggers sustained motion as well, with a characteristic ignition length that grows logarithmically as noise weakens at fixed observation time. Our work establishes a skin-effect route to bypass transitions, opening a new avenue for predicting and controlling nonlinear wave dynamics.

authors.name: Konghao Sun
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: How fast is the fastest-rotating O-type star in the Galaxy?
papers.abstract: {Rapid rotation distorts massive stars, making parameters from spherical models inclination-dependent. We studied these effects in the extreme Galactic O-type runaway LAMOST J040643.69+542347.8.} {We re-determined its stellar and rotational parameters with an oblate, gravity-darkened photospheric model and tabulated Stark profiles for selected \ion{He}{ii} lines.} {We fitted continuum-normalised spectra over 4000--4600\,\AA\ with \texttt{ZPEKTR}, using TLUSTY/SYNSPEC emergent fluxes, limb darkening to weight their angular contribution over the visible Roche surface, Espinosa-Lara \& Rieutord gravity darkening, and Sch\"oning--Butler Stark profiles. Interstellar and wind- or circumstellar-dominated features were masked.} {The model reproduces \ion{He}{ii}~$\lambda4200$, \ion{He}{i}~$\lambda4471$, and \ion{He}{ii}~$\lambda4542$. We obtained parent non-rotating counterpart (PNRC) parameters $T_{\rm eff}^{\rm PNRC}=38\,716\pm1041$~K, $\log g^{\rm PNRC}=4.12\pm0.12$, and $v_{\rm e}\sin i=587\pm73$~\kps. The central grid solution gives $\Omega/\Omega_{\rm c}=0.93$, $v_{\rm e}/v_{\rm c}=0.77$, $i=65^\circ$, $R_{\rm e}/R_{\rm p}=1.25$, and an equatorial centrifugal-to-gravitational acceleration ratio $\eta_{\rm e}=0.50$. Roche critical rotation requires $\eta_{\rm e}=1$ and $R_{\rm e}/R_{\rm p}=1.5$: despite the high angular rate, the central solution is not critical in equatorial force balance. The projected velocity exceeds, but is statistically consistent with, the previous spherical-fit value.} {\object{LAMOST J040643.69+542347.8} has a markedly oblate, gravity-darkened photosphere. Its proximity to critical rotation should be assessed using $\Omega/\Omega_{\rm c}$, $v_{\rm e}/v_{\rm c}$, and $\eta_{\rm e}$ together. A controlled spherical fit with the same atmosphere grid is needed to isolate the bias from neglecting deformation and gravity darkening.}

papers.title: Near linear mixing of random-cluster Glauber dynamics on random regular graphs
papers.abstract:
We study the random-cluster model on locally treelike graphs at low temperatures. This is a model of dependent percolation parametrized by an edge probability $p \in (0,1)$ and a clustering weight $q \in [1,\infty)$, generalizing independent Bernoulli percolation ($q=1$) and closely related to the classical ferromagnetic Ising and Potts spin systems at integer $q$. For $q>2$, at parameter $p$ below the tree uniqueness threshold $p_{\mathsf u}(q,d)$, it is expected that sampling is easy and local Markov chains mix rapidly on all graphs with degree bounded by $d$. On typical graphs, the same is predicted at $p>p_{\mathsf s}(q,d)$, where $p_{\mathsf s}(q,d)$ is a second uniqueness transition point on the $d$-regular wired tree. Our result confirms this prediction for random regular graphs, showing that the random-cluster Glauber dynamics mix in time $O(n^{1+o(1)})$ on a random $d$-regular graph for all fixed $q>2$ and $p>p_{\mathsf s}$.
  For comparison, the best prior sampling results for these models that held for all $p>p_{\mathsf s}$ required $q\gtrsim \log d$ \cite{BGPZ26}. The key difficulty is that simply utilizing the contraction of cavity messages on $d$-regular trees does not suffice to cover the entire regime $q>2$. To address this issue, motivated by \cite{LS26}, we develop a careful bootstrap argument to show the shrinkage of disagreement under grand coupling. The core ideas of the proof were generated using GPT-6 and the Pharos system; the proof was then refined and simplified by the author.

papers.title: Near-Optimal Complexity of Finding Approximate Local Minima of Nonconvex Finite Sums
papers.abstract: We study the component-oracle complexity of finding approximate local minima of nonconvex finite sums under mean-squared averaged smoothness with parameter $L$ and a $\rho$-Lipschitz average Hessian. Each query returns the value, gradient, and one Hessian-vector product of a component. We show that the complexity in the high-accuracy regime $\varepsilon\le c_0L^2/(n\rho)$ is $\tilde\Theta(n^{3/4}L^{1/2}\rho^{1/4}\Delta\varepsilon^{-7/4})$ for a sufficiently large initial gap $\Delta$. We attain the upper bound by adapting the inverse solver and eigenvector routine of FastCubic to averaged smoothness. Our lower bound assigns the bridge edges of a nested chain to random components; a replicated spectral construction gives the same bound for unrestricted randomized algorithms. Under individual smoothness, a factor of $n^{1/4}$ remains for $\varepsilon\le cL^2/(n^2\rho)$, up to logarithmic factors. In the complementary low-accuracy regime, we propose PathVR, which uses $\tilde O(n+\sqrt{n}L\Delta\varepsilon^{-2})$ queries and matches a lower bound from dense weak hiding.

papers.title: Interplay between Spin Stripes and Pairing Crossover in the Bilayer Hubbard Model
papers.abstract: Whether $d$-wave or $s_\pm$-wave pairing prevails in the bilayer nickelate \ce{La3Ni2O7} remains unresolved, and how its observed spin order and magnetic excitations relate to the pairing mechanism is unclear. Here, we use finite-temperature determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations of a minimal bilayer Hubbard model to investigate pairing competition at strong interlayer coupling, where intralayer and interlayer antiferromagnetic correlations have comparable strengths. We find that spin stripes develop spontaneously with increasing hole doping, accompanied by a crossover of the dominant pairing symmetry from $d$-wave to $s_\pm$-wave. The crossover tracks the changing relative strengths of the spin correlations, with the interlayer correlations overtaking their intralayer counterparts in magnitude. Concomitantly, the dynamical spin structure factor exhibits a momentum-dependent reorganization of the magnetic excitations, consistent with fluctuating spin stripes. Our results identify the structure of spin fluctuations as a key link between spin stripes and pairing competition, offering a minimal-model perspective for understanding \ce{La3Ni2O7}.

papers.title: Generative AI for urban planning: synthesizing land-use maps with satellite imagery via DualControlNet
papers.abstract: Various land-use models characterize land-use patterns and facilitate scenario planning. However, existing models are largely predictive, forecasting transitions based on numeric data without synthesizing new land-use maps from simple text prompts. Meanwhile, generative AI in urban systems remains unimodal, weakly controllable, and evaluated mostly by generic image quality rather than domain-specific metrics. To address these gaps, we introduce DualControlNet, a generative land-use model that jointly synthesizes high-resolution land-use maps and satellite imagery, addressing multimodality, controllability, and verification challenges. Trained on over 40,000 paired tiles from Orlando and Chicago, DualControlNet is evaluated using land-use, spatial consistency, and image quality metrics. Relative to unimodal baselines, DualControlNet improves land-use diversity consistency by 62.8% and building coverage ratio consistency by 16.3%, more than doubles cross-modal spatial consistency, and triples visual quality. Scenario-based experiments demonstrate that DualControlNet supports sustainable development through multidimensional controls, increasing density and diversity, and responding to text prompts like "high-density development." Overall, this work advances land-use modeling via a multimodal, controllable, and verifiable generative framework, lowering technical barriers and enabling intuitive exploration of urban futures.

authors.name: Lingqian Hu
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: A Complete Characterization of $q$-Ary $2$-Designs in Doubly-Extended Reed-Solomon Codes
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}_k$ be the doubly-extended Reed--Solomon code with parameters $[q+1, k, q-k+2]_q$. We give a complete characterization of when its codewords of a fixed weight form $q$-ary 2-designs. The main ingredient is an exact criterion showing that the number of $r$-subsets of $\mathbb{F}_q^*$ with a prescribed product is independent of that product if and only if $\gcd(r, q-1)=1$. Applying this criterion to the minimum-weight codewords of $\mathcal{C}_k$, we prove that they form a $q$-ary 2-design if and only if $\gcd(k-1, q-1)=1$. We further establish a propagation result for MDS codes showing that the $q$-ary 2-design property at minimum weight implies the same property at every nonzero weight. Consequently, $\mathcal{C}_k$ holds $q$-ary 2-designs at all nonzero weights if and only if $\gcd(k-1, q-1)=1$.

papers.title: Feature Puzzles: Single-Image Supervision for Multi-View 3D-Aware Segmentation
papers.abstract: Humans can easily recognize the same objects across different viewpoints of a 3D scene, whereas teaching models such multi-view-consistent perception typically requires videos or calibrated multi-view captures, which are considerably more expensive and less diverse than large-scale monocular data.~In this paper, we introduce Feature Puzzles, a novel framework for learning multi-view-consistent segmentation using only single-image semantic segmentation supervision. Specifically, we propose a simple yet effective pipeline that constructs multi-view-consistent segmentation pseudo-labels through image cropping and geometric transformations. We further introduce a lightweight, plug-and-play network that leverages the multi-view-consistent image features learned by existing pretrained 3D foundation models and the generated pseudo-labels to perform multi-view-consistent segmentation. Importantly, our flexible framework supports various types of prompts provided from one or multiple views and can be readily extended to open-vocabulary 3D segmentation. Under this single-image supervision, our feed-forward model achieves the best mIoU on NVOS, remains competitive on SPIn-NeRF and ScanNet++ against baselines using per-scene optimization or in-domain multi-view training, and demonstrates zero-shot transfer to open-vocabulary 3D segmentation. Visual comparisons are available on our project page: https://featurepuzzles.github.io/

authors.name: Qiang Zhang
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: CellCanon: An Agentic Cellular World Model for Prediction, Explanation, and Observation-Driven Updating
papers.abstract: Biological discovery requires using molecular knowledge and new measurements to infer responses beyond the conditions already observed. We introduce CellCanon, the first agentic cellular world model to unify single-cell expression prediction, evidence-grounded explanation, and observation-driven updating. Its predictive core reuses condition-level biological evidence across gene-specific numerical readouts to guide single-cell expression generation. A shared world state links predictions, acquired measurements, and source-linked claims, supporting explanation and revision. On 339 held-out SciPlex3 conditions across three cell lines, CellCanon improves differential-expression AUPRC and Macro-F1 over the best baseline for each metric by 63.3% and 17.3%, respectively, and direction Macro-F1 by 7.2%. Relative to gene-wise reasoning on matched drug-cell cohorts, measured language-model token use falls by 99.77% for Predict and 98.41% for Explain. On the source-grounded benchmark, Explain correctly answers all answerable questions with supporting proofs and identifies all insufficient-evidence cases. In simulated experimental feedback, Update uses one measured source context per drug to exceed the best fine-tuned baselines in differential-expression AUPRC and Macro-F1 without changing model weights. Together, these capabilities support a cumulative account of cellular responses, with predictions and biological judgments that can be revised as evidence accumulates.

papers.title: CHARM+: Cross-Hardware Attention with Re-Merge Multistream Mechanism
papers.abstract: As sequence lengths continue to grow, distributed attention based on sequence parallel (e.g., Ring-Attention) has become a mainstream solution for large language models (LLMs). Nevertheless, inherent communication dependencies limit computation-communication overlap, reducing GPU utilization. Moreover, in cross-hardware (NUMA or node) architectures, due to imbalanced communication bandwidth, frequent communication synchronization will limit overall performance. Based on these insights, we propose CHARM+, Cross-Hardware Attention with Re-Merge Multistream Mechanism. We reorganize sequential communications into several levels and achieve intra-level parallelism and computation overlap. Furthermore, we decouple cross-hardware communication from intra-hardware communication, eliminating synchronization overhead caused by bandwidth imbalance. Forward and backward algorithms were evaluated on multiple hardware architectures and consistently outperformed state-of-the-art methods. Compared to Ring-Attention, our forward and backward algorithms achieve average speedups of 1.3x and 1.7x on a dual-NUMA PCIe architecture, and 2.8x and 2.9x on a dual-node NVLink architecture, respectively.

authors.name: Boning Zhang
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Beijing

papers.title: Parabolic Extrapolation of Compactness with Applications to Characterizations of the Parabolic CMO Space via Parabolic Fractional Commutators
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove two compactness parabolic extrapolation theorems for linear operators and their commutators on parabolic weighted Lebesgue spaces. As applications, we show that $b\in\mathrm{PCMO}$ (parabolic CMO space) if and only if $b\in L_\mathrm{loc}^1$ and the commutator $[b,I_\alpha^{\gamma+}]_k$ is compact from $L^r(\omega^r)$ to $L^q(\omega^q)$ for any $k\in\mathbb{N}$, $1<r<q<\infty$ with $\frac{1}{r}-\frac{1}{q}=\alpha\in(0,1)$, and $\omega\in A_{r,q}^+(\gamma)$ (parabolic Muckenhoupt class), where $I_\alpha^{\gamma+}$ is the parabolic fractional integral. Several other equivalent characterizations of the space $\mathrm{PCMO}$ are also given. Our approach combines the unweighted compactness for mixed commutators, a local lower estimate for $[b,I_\alpha^{\gamma+}]_k$, and both a quantitative Uchiyama-type description and the equivalence with $\inf_T\{\|[\cdot,I_\alpha^{\gamma+}]_k-T\|_{L^r\to L^q}^\frac{1}{k}\}$ of $\mathrm{dist}_{\mathrm{PBMO}}(\cdot,\mathrm{PCMO})$, where the infimum is taken over all compact operators $T:L^r\to L^q$. Finally, we establish two parabolic weighted Fr\'echet--Kolmogorov compactness criteria, which further induce a parabolic interpolation theorem of compactness.

papers.title: Community Search under Member-Specific Tolerances
papers.abstract: We study community search when each vertex has its own tolerance for differences in position. For positions such as opinions or homes, a latitude-consistent community (LCC) contains the query vertex, is connected, has minimum degree at least k, and bounds its diameter by the smallest member tolerance. Motivated by social judgment theory, the bound exactly characterizes persistent acceptance of every interaction in a closed group under bounded-confidence dynamics with arbitrary positive weights. It also prevents rejection under social-judgment dynamics, whereas natural relaxations preserve neither guarantee. Finding a maximum LCC is NP-hard even in the plane, and with unbounded dimension, deciding whether an LCC exists is NP-complete for every fixed k >= 2. LatSweep turns the coupled bound into a sweep over the smallest tolerance, yielding two feasible heuristics, a (1,2)-bicriteria approximation and an exact branch-and-bound algorithm. Across eight graphs with up to 1.8 billion edges, the exact algorithm proves optimality on all but 9 of 3,700 efficiency queries and usually certifies absence within microseconds when no LCC exists. Its branch-and-bound solver proves more queries than a reimplemented maximum-(k,r)-core algorithm, a mixed-integer program and CP-SAT. In simulations, uneven influence disrupts initially accepted interactions in pairwise groups. Outside ties invalidate the guarantee for many real groups. On two location-based networks, tolerance-agnostic groups often place another member's home beyond a member's estimated travel radius; comparisons with spatial communities of the same size detect no co-visit loss from enforcing every member's tolerance.

papers.title: Scaling Limits and Fractal Dimensions of $\omega$-Substitution Graph Systems
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a class of non-homogeneous self-similar constructions, called $\omega $-substitution graph system, in which the interface vertices are determined by an infinite sequence $\omega .$ The associated graph sequences naturally form compact metric measure spaces, and under suitable assumptions on $\omega$, we establish their convergence in the Gromov-Hausdorff-Prokhorov sense. We determine the Hausdorff and box-counting dimensions of the limiting space. We further prove that the discrete Hausdorff dimension of the graph sequence coincides with the Hausdorff dimension of its scaling limit. As a direct application of the scaling limit, asymptotic formulas are derived for a class of generalized Wiener indices, which include the classical Wiener index and Kirchhoff index as special cases. Finally, closed-form expressions for these indices are also obtained.

authors.name: Yumei Xue
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Cheng Zeng
authors.institution: National Center for Nanoscience and Technology

papers.title: Linear adaptive variable time step schemes for the anisotropic phase field dendritic crystal growth model
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a class of efficient, linear and decoupled adaptive variable time step schemes for the anisotropic phase field dendritic crystal growth model. The main difficulty is twofold: the gradient dependent anisotropic coefficient and the strongly nonlinear terms make unconditional energy stability difficult to achieve, and on nonuniform meshes the discrete energy dissipation law, which is straightforward to establish on uniform meshes, has to be reestablished under varying step sizes. To overcome these difficulties, two linear stabilizers and a time dependent auxiliary variable with relaxation are introduced and incorporated into a second-order generalized BDF-type operator, with the spatial derivatives discretized by the Fourier spectral method. The proposed schemes are energy stable for arbitrary positive adjacent step ratios, so that no restriction on the step ratio is imposed, and only two linear equations together with a few algebraic equations, which are solved independently in Fourier space, need to be solved at each time step. Moreover, the schemes are naturally compatible with energy based time adaptive strategies. The associated adaptive strategy reduces the number of time steps by $24.6\%$--$86.6\%$ in comparison with uniform time stepping, and numerical experiments on fourfold and sixfold dendritic growth in two dimensions and on three-dimensional growth confirm the accuracy, efficiency and stability of the proposed schemes.

authors.name: Ziqi Ma
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Heavy Oil

papers.title: Single-Variable Connectivity in Random $k$-SAT
papers.abstract:
We resolve longstanding questions about connectivity, reconstruction,and looseness in random $k$-SAT, for sufficiently large fixed $k$ as the number $n$ of variables tends to infinity.
  $\textbf{Single-variable connectivity up to reconstruction.}$ At clause densities up to \[\frac{2^k}{k}\bigl(\ln k+\ln\ln k+\gamma_*-o_k(1)\bigr),\] a polynomial-time algorithm joins a typical pair of satisfying assignments with high probability, using $O_k(n)$ single-variable flips that preserve satisfiability. Here $\gamma_*\approx0.871$ arises from a refined tree-reconstruction analysis.
  $\textbf{Settling the reconstruction threshold.}$ Building on the tools developed for connectivity, we determine the clustering threshold defined by the reconstruction criterion to be \[\frac{2^k}{k}\bigl(\ln k+\ln\ln k+\gamma_*+o_k(1)\bigr),\] below the classical cavity prediction with constant term $1+O(\ln\ln k/\ln k)$.
  $\textbf{Shattering before rigidity.}$ We locate the looseness--rigidity transition at a higher density, matching the classical cavity prediction for clustering: \[\frac{2^k}{k} \left(\ln k+\ln\ln k+1+\Theta\left(\frac{\ln\ln k}{\ln k}\right)\right).\] Below the transition, we establish a stronger form of looseness: any variable of a typical solution can be reversed by logarithmically many single-variable flips that preserve satisfiability. Above it, reversing most variables of a typical solution requires changing linearly many variables (rigidity). Yet throughout an interval between reconstruction and rigidity, the solution space already splits into groups of exponentially small relative size separated by linear Hamming distance and linear energy barriers (shattering), while logarithmic looseness persists.

authors.name: Yiyao Zhang
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Time-Varying Tails: Estimation, Inference, and Risk Measurement
papers.abstract: Motivated by evidence that the tails of economic and financial time series need not be stable over time, we develop a framework for studying time-varying tails. We model the extreme value index as a smooth function of time in the locally stationary framework of Zhou and Wu (2009). We estimate it by a ratio-form kernel Hill estimator in which a single intermediate quantile thresholds the whole local window. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality, and we construct uniform confi- dence bands. We also propose a consistent test of tail stability under extremal clustering. Combined with the Weissman extrapolation method, the estimator of the extreme value index yields time- varying extreme Value-at-Risk and Expected Shortfall. In an empirical application, we find the tail of daily loss of S&P 500 is compatible with a constant shape, whereas that of volatility-filtered loss varies significantly.

authors.name: Shuo Li
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Spectroscopy-informed Deep Learning Searches for Photometric Little Red Dots in JWST Surveys
papers.abstract: Little Red Dots (LRDs) are a population of compact, red sources discovered at high redshift with JWST that exhibit distinctive V-shaped spectral energy distributions (SEDs). Existing LRD samples are typically identified using a variety of color-based selection criteria, which can lead to differences in the populations recovered by different studies. We develop a cross-modal machine-learning framework that combines matched NIRCam imaging and NIRSpec/PRISM spectroscopy to transfer spectroscopic information into imaging-based representations, enabling LRD identification from JWST/NIRCam imaging alone. Applied to spectroscopically observed high-redshift galaxies previously classified as non-LRDs, our model identifies 35 new LRD candidates. The majority satisfy at least one independent LRD color selection criterion, and among the 13 candidates with medium- or high-resolution NIRSpec grating spectra, 10 exhibit broad H$\alpha$ emission - a hallmark of LRDs. We further apply the classifier to public NIRCam imaging from the Dawn JWST Archive and two independent JWST surveys, yielding 357 and 23 additional LRD candidates, respectively. The candidates recovered by our method span a broader range of observed SED properties than those in existing samples, suggesting that current color-selected samples may not fully capture the diversity of LRD-like systems present in JWST surveys. Our findings highlight the value of spectroscopy-informed photometric classification as a powerful strategy for systematically mining large-area JWST imaging datasets and provide a practical framework for future studies of this emerging population.

authors.name: Huanian Zhang
authors.institution: North China University of Water Resources and Electric Power

papers.title: Softmax Attention with Any Temperature in Fixed Dimension: Matching the Best Known Maximum-Inner-Product Bounds
papers.abstract:
Attention is central to modern AI models for language, vision, and scientific modeling. However, direct evaluation compares every query with every key, requiring quadratic time in the context length, which limits its scalability to long contexts. Consequently, characterizing the complexity bounds of attention is of fundamental importance.
  For every fixed dimension $d$, we give an algorithm for $m$ queries, $n$ key-value pairs, and additive error $\varepsilon$, with expected time $ \widetilde{\mathrm{O}}\bigl((mn)^{k/(k+1)}+m+n\bigr),\qquad k=\lfloor d/2\rfloor. $
  For fixed dimension and a fixed number of value channels, soft-O hides factors of the form $\operatorname{poly}_d\bigl(b,\log(m+n),\log B,\log(1/\varepsilon)\bigr),$ where $b$ bounds input encoding lengths and $B$ bounds coordinate and value magnitudes. In particular, the dependence on $B$ and $1/\varepsilon$ is polylogarithmic, which allows arbitrary positive temperature. When $m=n$ and $d\ge2$, the bound is $\widetilde{\mathrm{O}}(n^{2-2/(\lfloor d/2\rfloor+1)})$: near-linear in dimensions two and three, with exponent $4/3$ in dimensions four and five and $3/2$ in dimensions six and seven. It improves the previous $\widetilde{\mathrm{O}}(n^{2-1/d})$ upper bound and matches the best known batch maximum-inner-product bound in each fixed dimension. Additionally, we reduce integer batch maximum inner product computation to one attention call with the same dimension and input sizes $m,n$.

papers.title: Breaking the One-Player Extension Barrier: History-Aware Repair for Multiplayer Approximate Nash Equilibria
papers.abstract: Computation of Nash equilibria is a central problem in algorithmic game theory, yet exact equilibrium computation is $\mathsf{PPAD}$-complete even for two-player games. This hardness motivates the study of polynomial-time algorithms for approximate Nash equilibria. While substantial progress has been made for two-player and three-player games, existing algorithms for general $m$-player games have largely relied on repeatedly applying one-player extension starting from improved fixed-player algorithms. Such improvements can at best strengthen the classical $1-1/m$ guarantee to $1-1/(m-c)$, for some constant $c$ independent of $m$. We break this long-standing barrier by developing an iterative algorithm that directly tackles general $m$-player games and achieves a $(1-(\sigma_{\star}-\epsilon)/m)$-approximation for fixed $\epsilon > 0$ and sufficiently large $m$, where $\sigma_\star\approx1.5867$ is the unique root in $(1,2)$ of $\sigma_\star^3-19\sigma_\star^2+27\sigma_\star+1=0$. Our approach rests on a novel iterative descent-and-repair framework that allows multiple rounds of repair. At the heart of our analysis is a new potential function inspired by continuous-time dynamics, which certifies progress across iterations and ensures polynomial-time termination. Our results highlight the power of history-aware, iterative repair in breaking approximation barriers for multiplayer games.

papers.title: SWEOps-Bench: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Resolution of Software-Induced Cloud Incidents
papers.abstract:
As autonomous agents advance, the traditional boundary between software development and cloud operations gradually blurs, increasing the need for integrated incident detection, localization, and remediation. Existing benchmarks evaluate isolated diagnostic queries or repository-level program repair, failing to test continuous incident resolution across operational clusters and source repositories. We introduce SWEOps-Bench, an interactive benchmark comprising 55 reproducible incident tasks derived from confirmed historical defects across 16 Kubernetes operator projects. Each task preserves the original software repository and initializes in a healthy cluster before a controlled workload triggers the historical fault. Agents investigate runtime evidence and submit source or configuration repairs through a terminal interface, while the harness builds and deploys the changes within a shared time budget.
  Evaluation covers stage-wise accuracy, verified recovery, penalized lifecycle latency, and token consumption. Across six agent-model configurations, faulty-state detection ranges from 72.7% to 90.9%, whereas overall recovery ranges from only 14.5% to 52.7%, exposing a substantial gap between recognizing incidents and resolving them end to end. Trajectory analysis further shows that reported diagnosis and final recovery only partially coincide: some tasks achieve verified recovery despite an incorrect reported RCA, while runtime symptom clearance can still fail fix-specific functional verification. SWEOps-Bench establishes a rigorous foundation for evaluating autonomous agents in integrated development and operational environments.

papers.title: When Predictive Fit Misleads: Selecting Marketing Mix Models Using Experimental RoAS Benchmarks
papers.abstract: Marketing Mix Models (MMMs) are used to estimate channel-level Return on Ad Spend (RoAS) and guide marketing investment, yet competing specifications are usually compared on predictive-fit metrics such as out-of-sample R-squared, MAPE, or RMSE. We show that predictive fit can diverge from recovery of the causal quantities that drive marketing decisions. In simulations with known RoAS, the best-fitting specification is often not the one that recovers RoAS most accurately; replicated studies show that this disagreement is systematic and persists under media-spend collinearity, noise, and a misspecified carryover shape. Selecting specifications against experimental RoAS benchmarks, even imprecise ones, improves RoAS recovery relative to fit-based selection, and a real-world application with experimental benchmarks shows the same pattern. We propose an applied workflow: calibrate MMM specifications against estimand-aligned experimental benchmarks when they exist, and otherwise report RoAS sensitivity across plausible specifications rather than relying on a single best-fitting model.

papers.title: Multi-Period Bilevel Coordination of Primary and Secondary Frequency Regulation for Grid-Forming Battery Energy Storage
papers.abstract: We study the coordination of primary and secondary frequency regulation by grid-forming battery energy storage systems in islanded microgrids. We formulate the coordination as a multi-period bilevel program, in which the upper level schedules secondary regulation setpoints and each lower level computes primary regulation decisions. Using the lower-level Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions, we obtain an exact single-level reformulation with complementarity constraints. To address the numerical difficulties introduced by these constraints, we develop a continuation method that couples the complementarity relaxation parameter with the interior-point barrier parameter and warm-starts successive stages. Under the stated boundedness assumptions and with vanishing subproblem residuals, we prove that every accumulation point is feasible and satisfies a first-order stationarity condition for the reformulated problem (C-stationarity). Numerical results for an islanded microgrid show that the proposed method reduces solution time by 89.3% and peak frequency deviation by 0.53% relative to conventional Scholtes relaxation.

papers.title: Spin swapping mediated by spin-orbital textures in centrosymmetric multiorbital materials
papers.abstract: Spin swapping converts a primary spin current into a secondary one by interchanging its flow and spin-polarization directions, attributed to spin-orbit scattering or spin-band splitting. Here we uncover a fundamentally distinct route to spin swapping arising from the orbital degree of freedom in the spin pumping to centrosymmetric multiorbital materials \textit{without spin-band splitting}. When the dynamical proximity ferromagnet injects a longitudinal spin current flowing normal to the interface, spin-orbit-entangled orbital textures redirect the injected spins into longitudinal and transverse orbital currents. Their subsequent conversion back to the spin sector generates transverse spin currents with propagation and polarization directions swapped relative to the primary spin current. The swapping efficiency achieves $50\%$ for Ge and Si. Governed by a fourth-rank tensor constrained by crystalline symmetry and without requiring spin-orbit scattering or inversion symmetry breaking, our finding reveals spin-orbital textures as hidden intermediate channels of spin swapping with unexplored material choices and functionalities.

authors.name: Chengyuan Cai
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Hanchen Wang
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Reasoning-Aware Cross-Modal Association Unlearning in Multimodal Large Reasoning Models
papers.abstract: Multimodal large reasoning models (MLRMs) integrate visual inputs with textual and parametric knowledge, allowing sensitive information to be accessed through cross-modal associations during reasoning. This raises privacy concerns when a visual input should no longer provide access to such information. Machine unlearning can remove this influence without retraining the model from scratch. However, multimodal unlearning methods mainly target samples, concepts, or knowledge content, without separating the knowledge from the cross-modal association through which it is accessed. In reasoning models, target information may disappear from the final answer while remaining in intermediate reasoning, or be replaced by incorrect substitute knowledge. We therefore study cross-modal association unlearning, where the forget target is a designated visual-to-knowledge association: the model should suppress target-bearing behavior under the designated visual context while preserving access to the same knowledge in permitted contexts. We propose Visual-Keyed Counterfactual Rebinding (VKCR), a parameter-efficient framework for cross-modal association editing. VKCR first localizes the edit to a compact association-conditioned parameter subspace. It then reduces support for the designated target at task outputs and counterfactually rebinds the affected reasoning behavior by discouraging target-bearing or unsupported continuations while favoring valid non-sensitive alternatives. We further introduce CLEAR-R and MLLMU-R to evaluate target leakage, hallucinated reassociation, reasoning preservation, and modality-specific utility. Experiments show that VKCR substantially reduces image-conditioned target leakage and hallucinated reassociation, including across heterogeneous task formulations, while preserving non-sensitive visual reasoning and permitted text-only knowledge.

papers.title: Hamiltonicity and cycle factors in k-quasi-transitive digraphs of large diameter
papers.abstract: A digraph is $k$-quasi-transitive if the endpoints of every directed path of length $k$ are adjacent. In this paper, we prove that every strong non-bipartite $k$-quasi-transitive digraph of diameter at least $k+2$ is Hamiltonian when $k\ge7$ is odd. Moreover, combined with the known even case, for $k\ge6$, we also prove that a strong bipartite $k$-quasi-transitive digraph of diameter at least $k+2$ is Hamiltonian if and only if it has a cycle factor. These answer two problems posed by Alva-Samos and Hern\'andez-Cruz affirmatively [Journal of Graph Theory \textbf{96} (2021) 310--325].

papers.title: EnzymeRSI: A dual-loop recursive self-improvement system for enzyme design
papers.abstract: Improvement in enzyme engineering is usually pursued by optimising which candidates to assay within a fixed model and workflow; when the bottleneck arises from a mismatched method or a failing workflow, that route is difficult to escape. We present EnzymeRSI, a dual-loop system for recursive self-improvement (RSI). The outer loop evolves harness assets without changing model weights, the inner loop develops prediction and selection algorithms under controlled conditions, and a cloud laboratory system is specified to close the physical loop with quality-controlled feedback. By updating its prediction strategy through iterative comparison, the outer loop raised the mean development-set Spearman correlation on ProteinGym by 0.044 across five assays, reaching 0.335 on CD19 and 0.683 on OPSD (rhodopsin); of the two first places, only CD19 was produced by the outer loop itself. In the self-improvement of the ThermoMPNN algorithm the inner loop reached a PCC of 0.849, and on TadA-Bench it reached a Spearman correlation of 0.307 in 1.13 h. In three prospective wet-lab tests of the system's experimental decision-making, 10 of the 32 candidates that had not been pre-specified for the luciferase RLuc showed at least twice the wild-type activity; a recommended variant of the cytidine deaminase A3A raised 5mC conversion to 90.2%; and path selection in evolution raised the catalytic efficiency of the DNA polymerase KOD-E on a modified substrate to 31.1 times that of the parent. By treating the organisation of the research workflow and the development of algorithms as a single falsifiable dry-to-wet loop, this work offers an evolutionary paradigm for moving beyond the blind spots of a fixed method and for autonomous enzyme engineering.

authors.name: Yisi Liu
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: On the (in)finiteness of fixed characters in genus $3$
papers.abstract: We construct a counterexample to the Putman--Wieland conjecture in genus $3$ and discuss some of its consequences.

papers.title: On the proof of multi-variable $n/d$-conjecture for hyperplane arrangements
papers.abstract: In this article, we use Wu's method to prove Budur's multi-variable $n/d$-conjecture for completeness.

papers.title: The optimal barrier parameter of the three-dimensional power cone
papers.abstract: We determine the optimal logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier parameter for the three-dimensional power cone. Although several self-concordant barriers for this cone have been constructed, its optimal barrier parameter had remained unknown. For a power cone with exponent $c\in(0,1)$, we prove that the optimal parameter is $\frac{3}{1+\min\{c,1-c\}}$. Except at $c=1/2$, this value is strictly smaller than the parameter $3-2\min\{c,1-c\}$ of Chares' conjectured barrier. At $c=1/2$, the optimal parameter equals $2$, in agreement with the optimal barrier parameter of the second-order cone. The proof combines a sharp lower bound for arbitrary logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barriers with an explicit barrier attaining the bound.

authors.name: Rui-Jin Zhang
authors.institution: Academy of Mathematics and Systems Science

papers.title: Measuring the collaboration, not the agent
papers.abstract: Benchmarks for visualization agents score the agent alone; the human only supplies reference answers. For high-dimensional data this misses what matters: the knowledge of which variables count is held by on-site experts, not by the model, so the useful question is how well an analyst and an agent do together. We study one specific form of collaboration, the agent proposes a view, the analyst accepts, rejects, or modifies it, and those judgments are kept for later sessions, and propose five measures for it: complementarity, intervention efficiency, appropriate reliance, knowledge retention, and agency. The first four are computed from interaction logs alone. We test the measures, not people: in a testbed for parallel-coordinates design on public manufacturing data (UCI SECOM), with a simulated analyst whose behavior we control, all four are computable and respond to the controlled differences. Whether they reveal anything about real analysts is the next step; we release the testbed for it.

papers.title: Tools Need Not Speak in Text: Latent Context Compression for Agents
papers.abstract:
Large language model (LLM) agents typically append raw tool outputs to their context. Over multi-step interactions, long and noisy observations incur substantial context overhead and dilute the agent's attention to task-relevant information. Existing token pruning and summarization methods remain constrained by discrete text representations, limiting the achievable compression ratios.
  In this work, we challenge the prevailing assumption that agents must consume tool observations as explicit text tokens. To this end, we propose Coca-Cola, a continuous latent context compression model for LLM agents. Coca-Cola compresses tool observations into latent tokens and embeds them into the input embedding space of the agent. We further introduce Action-Preserving Training, which aligns the agent's next-action distributions under full and compressed observations. This trains the compression model to learn action-sufficient latent tokens that retain decision-critical information. Experiments with web-search agents on four QA benchmarks and two model families show that Coca-Cola reduces the agent's token consumption by 70.01%-89.24% and end-to-end runtime by 24.45%-55.97%, while consistently improving task performance. These results suggest that Coca-Cola offers a promising approach for context compression in agents. Our code is available at https://github.com/THU-Agent/Coca-cola.

authors.name: Yitong Zhang
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Haorui Chen
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Jia Li
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Property F and weak integrality of braided fusion categories
papers.abstract: We prove that a braided fusion category with property F is weakly integral, provided it admits a pivotal structure whose left categorical dimensions are positive on the intersection of its M\"uger center and its adjoint subcategory. In particular, the converse implication in the property F conjecture holds for modular fusion categories and pseudounitary braided fusion categories. We also show that the positivity condition holds for every pivotal braided fusion category if and only if every braided fusion category over $\mathbb C$ admits a pivotal structure.

papers.title: Small inertia limit of the distribution-dependent stochastic Cucker--Smale equation
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the small inertia limit of the distribution-dependent stochastic Cucker--Smale equation with the full velocity alignment source term, which serves as the mean-field equation for the stochastic Cucker--Smale model. Inspired by the idea of Hottovy et al. \cite{Hottovy2015} to rearrange SDEs via integration by parts, we repeatedly perform integration by parts on independent copies of our equation. Then we define a global position correction and a quadratic remainder, both with uniformly bounded tails. Applying the Aldous criterion, we obtain tightness of the position correction, which in turn yields tightness of the position process. Subsequently, using the averaging method on the fast time scale, the quadratic functional can be decomposed into the equilibrium average, local quadratic fluctuations, and exponential transients. Then, the Poisson--Lyapunov equation is employed to prove the convergence of the time integral. Finally, under various suitable assumptions, we obtain the weak convergence of the laws of the approximating processes to the law of the solution of the small-inertia limit equation, along with the identification of the limiting process, and also the convergence rate of strong $L^1$-convergence. The extra noise-induced drift term can be expressed as the solution of a contraction-type Fredholm equation. This paper is complementary to the deterministic particle limit work of \cite{Carrillo2021,Choi2021} .

authors.name: Jizhao Huang
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Yan Lv
authors.institution: Anhui University of Finance and Economics

papers.title: Using Experience Twice: Dynamic Process Rubrics for Privileged Token-Level Credit Assignment
papers.abstract: Agent trajectories often contain both successful decisions and failed attempts, yet optimization with sparse trajectory-level rewards struggles to identify which critical decisions should be reinforced or suppressed. We observe that meaningful distinctions among on-policy trajectories can be distilled into natural-language process rubrics and used as process supervision signals. Based on this insight, we propose Online Rubric Self-Distillation (ORSD), which leverages self-derived process rubrics for dense token-level supervision, thereby augmenting outcome-centric reinforcement learning. Specifically, the current policy independently generates multiple rubric bundles at each step according to the same group of trajectories, extracting candidate process rubrics from cross-trajectory behavioral differences. A frozen verifier then evaluates all rubric items against each trajectory in the group, and selects one candidate bundle based on bundle-level alignment between rubric satisfaction and task success. ORSD treats the selected rubric bundle as privileged information during training, then compares the log-likelihoods of the original tokens with and without the rubric. The resulting likelihood gap provides token-specific process credit, which is added to the original trajectory-level GRPO advantage through additive advantage shaping. ORSD thus bridges trajectory-level outcome supervision and fine-grained process supervision, enabling token-level credit assignment using process signals. Extensive experiments on ALFWorld and WebShop show that ORSD accelerates policy improvement and boosts final task performance for both Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-4B under the same environment-interaction budget. Our code is available at https://github.com/AnnaXChun/ORSD.

authors.name: Shumao Wu
authors.institution: Collaborative Innovation Center of Advanced Microstructures

authors.name: Jianqiang Huang
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Dual Banach spaces with AP but without BAP
papers.abstract: We give negative answers to the AP-to-BAP and BAP-to-MAP questions for dual Banach spaces. More precisely, there is a separable Banach space $V$ with the metric approximation property (MAP) such that $V^*$ has the approximation property (AP) but no bounded approximation property (BAP). There is also a separable MAP space $X$, isomorphic to $\ell_1$, whose dual has BAP but no MAP. This resolves a longstanding open question explicitly stated in \cite{Oja2010}. The constructions rely on a finitely generated group without Property A and a quantitative estimate for optimal bounded approximation constants of projective tensor products.

papers.title: Weak Atomic Continuity and Subgame Perfection
papers.abstract: Subgame-perfect equilibrium need not exist in continuous games with perfect information when Nature moves. Under standard regularity assumptions, we prove that weak atomic continuity of Nature's transition probabilities yields a measurable pure-strategy subgame-perfect equilibrium for finite and infinite horizons. The condition, originating in the population genetics literature, is necessary for the existence of subgame-perfect equilibrium uniformly over the remaining primitives: whenever this condition is violated, one can construct a dynamic game with no subgame-perfect equilibrium, even in behavioral strategies. The proof preserves compactness and upper hemicontinuity of continuation payoff correspondences under integration without requiring convexity.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Driven Efficient Communication for UAV-Based Collaborative Perception
papers.abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based collaborative perception enables multiple agents to share complementary perceptual information, overcoming limitations such as occlusion and limited sensing range. Communication efficiency is a critical bottleneck, as UAVs operate under stringent bandwidth and computational constraints. However, existing spatial selection methods focus predominantly on foreground regions to reduce missed detections, neglecting perceptually ambiguous regions and leaving false detections unresolved. We propose UCP, an uncertainty-driven framework that characterizes collaborative value through observational uncertainty, identifying sensor-limited regions, and discriminative uncertainty, capturing model-level ambiguity near the decision boundary. These estimates drive spatial request and supply maps for efficient inter-agent communication, and the received messages are aggregated via U-Fusion, an uncertainty-guided cross-attention module. Experiments on three benchmarks across 3D object detection and trajectory prediction demonstrate a superior performance-bandwidth trade-off with high interpretability and strong generalizability.

authors.name: Jiuwu Hao

papers.title: Universal Nonexistence of Monotone Equilibrium in Multiunit Auctions with Risk Aversion
papers.abstract: We establish universal nonexistence results for monotone pure-strategy equilibrium in multiunit auctions with risk-averse bidders. Fix any number of bidders greater than one and any profile of strictly increasing concave utilities, with at least one strictly risk-averse bidder. Under uniform pricing, for every supply of at least three units, we construct independent, full-support type distributions under which neither lowest-winning-bid nor highest-losing-bid pricing admits an admissible monotone equilibrium. Under discriminatory pricing, we construct a finite supply and independent, full-support type distributions that preclude monotone pure-strategy equilibrium. We extend these results to all-pay auctions and finite bid grids.

papers.title: Anomalous thermal transport in isotope-enriched germanium carbide
papers.abstract: Advances in modern electronics demand the dissipation of heat fluxes approaching 1000 W cm$^{-2}$, which drives an urgent need for materials with thermal conductivity ($\kappa$) exceeding 1000 W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$. Here, by solving the Boltzmann transport equation considering both three- and four-phonon interactions, we observe that isotopically pure cubic germanium carbide (GeC) exhibits a remarkable $\kappa$ of 1018 W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ at room temperature, which is further corroborated by state-of-the-art machine-learning molecular dynamics simulations. Two unique mechanisms underlie this anomalously high $\kappa$: a remarkably strong isotopic enhancement effect (289%) and a surprisingly modest suppression due to four-phonon scattering (22%)-despite the presence of a wide acoustic-optical phonon gap. Moreover, we find that GeC defies the conventional Leibfried-Schlomann formula and exhibits a non-monotonic variation of $\kappa$ with external hydrostatic pressure at elevated temperatures. Our findings establish isotope-enriched GeC as a material of ultrahigh $\kappa$ and an ideal platform for exploring exotic phonon physics.

papers.title: Which Physical Tactile Cues Matter for Contact-Rich Imitation Learning? A Controlled Real-Robot Study
papers.abstract: Vision-based tactile sensors capture multiple aspects of physical interaction within a single image stream, including contact appearance, geometry, indentation depth, and tangential deformation. However, existing visuo-tactile policies often directly process tactile observations as images, making it difficult to determine which physical cues contribute to policy learning. This paper presents a controlled real-robot study that compares physically interpretable tactile signals using the LeRobot platform, enhanced with our visuo-tactile perception system. From the same tactile stream, we derive tactile RGB images, normal/depth maps, and marker-flow fields, representing contact appearance, geometry, and tangential deformation, respectively. Using identical task demonstrations and the same policy backbone, we evaluate the individual and combined contributions of these tactile cues. We further compare tactile encoders and visuo-tactile fusion strategies. Evaluation across 720 real-robot trials yields four key findings: (1) tactile perception substantially improves the overall success rate from 57.8% to 78.9%, although its contribution varies across task stages; (2) marker flow is the most effective individual cue, achieving a success rate of 74.4% and playing a particularly important role in regulating established contact; (3) cue-factorized encoding consistently improves performance, highlighting that different physical cues require tailored processing techniques; and (4) although the effectiveness of tactile fusion is task-dependent, cross-attention offers a lightweight solution with performance comparable to that of pretrained tactile encoders.

papers.title: Concavity of Normalized Generalized Br\'ezin--Gross--Witten Correlators and Its Applications
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the generalized Br\'ezin--Gross--Witten model using its BKP integrability. By virtue of the formula for connected $n$-point functions of tau-functions of the BKP hierarchy obtained by Wang and the first-named author, we prove that the normalized generalized BGW correlators are strictly concave for fixed genus and fixed total degree. As applications, we establish the strict Schur-concavity and derive upper and lower bounds for these correlators. We also prove the strict monotonicity of normalized ordinary BGW correlators, which resolves a conjecture by Guo--Norbury--Yang--Zagier.

papers.title: Finite-Time Blowup for Navier-Stokes with Smooth Forcing, Part II: Residual Correction via Oscillatory Pulses
papers.abstract: This paper is a companion to Part I: Construction of Self-Similar Solutions with Admissible Stress and Flat Remainder (arXiv:2609.35406). Part I constructs approximately self-similar flow profiles with a singular stress in divergence form. The associated velocity becomes unbounded as $t\uparrow 1$. Here, localized oscillatory pulses cancel this stress contribution through their averaged quadratic momentum flux. Successive corrections preserve the velocity growth and leave a smooth external force $f\in C^\infty$. This gives a local solution of the three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with forcing $f$. Its velocity satisfies $\limsup_{t\uparrow 1}\|u(t)\|_{L^\infty}=\infty$. Together, the two papers present a readable and accessible account of OpenAI's Finite Time Blowup for Navier-Stokes. We claim no original mathematical contribution.

authors.name: Xiao Ren
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Industrial Control Technology

papers.title: SpecCompact: Accelerating LLM Agent Context Compaction with Slot-Parallel Semantic Speculative Verification
papers.abstract: LLM agents use context compaction to manage growing interaction histories, but summarizing long histories with large models can introduce substantial delays. Compaction therefore requires balancing information retention against latency. We observe that structured summary slots can retain information when generated independently. Based on this observation, we present SpecCompact, a framework that accelerates compaction through slot-parallel semantic speculation. SpecCompact fine-tunes a small drafter and generates slots in parallel. The target model verifies each proposed line and repairs rejected content, while subsequent drafting uses the updated slot prefix. System optimizations further reduce repeated context processing and model calls. Across AppWorld and $\tau^3$ benchmarks with two target models, SpecCompact achieves $2.04$--$5.63\times$ compaction speedups over Hermes-style summarization. Separate downstream evaluations reveal model- and task-dependent performance trade-offs. A user study within Hermes further shows an $8.68\times$ median compaction speedup.

authors.name: Yulu An
authors.institution: The University of Texas at San Antonio Health Science Center

papers.title: Lifts of Brauer characters and vertex pairs for odd primes
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $G$ be a finite $p$-solvable group, and let $\varphi\in\IBr_p(G)$ have vertex $Q$. We prove that $\varphi$ has at most $|Q:Q'|$ lifts to ordinary irreducible characters, establishing Cossey's conjecture for odd primes.

papers.title: PointNDF: Cascaded Neural Displacement Fields for Point Cloud Denoising
papers.abstract: Point cloud denoising aims to recover clean geometry from noisy 3D observations while preserving both fine surface details and the underlying spatial distribution of the points. Many learning-based methods adopt a two-stage pipeline that first extracts point-wise features from the noisy input and subsequently predicts point-wise displacements via simple regressions. However, these approaches often lack robust feature guidance and distribution-aware geometric refinement, causing them to fail at maintaining optimal point uniformity and geometric quality. To address these limitations, we propose PointNDF, a denoising framework that combines patch-level geometric context with local displacement prediction. Specifically, a Point Transformer V3 (PTv3) encoder aggregates multiscale geometric information into a global patch descriptor. Rather than directly regressing an unconstrained displacement vector, a Neural Displacement Field (NDF) fuses this global patch descriptor with per-point neighborhood features. It then predicts each displacement through bounded-vector and scale factor branches, thereby achieving a superior, more uniform point distribution. Three cascaded NDF stages propagate local features and progressively refine the point positions. Experiments on PU-Net and ModelNet10 demonstrate competitive denoising accuracy and favorable inference efficiency. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/peridous/PointNDF.

authors.name: Pingping Cai
authors.institution: Chinese Center For Disease Control and Prevention

papers.title: LegalEvolver: Agentic Legal Judgment Prediction via Rubric-Guided Self-Evolution
papers.abstract: As LLM-based agents develop, they have been increasingly applied in the legal domain. Legal Judgment Prediction~(LJP) requires models to conduct multi-step reasoning and external legal evidence retrieval. Existing legal search agents' performance is often constrained by the quality of retrieval queries. They often formulate queries directly from the initial user request, overlooking latent legal issues and legally salient details. To address this issue, we propose \emph{LegalEvolver}, a query optimization framework specifically designed to generate legally informative queries for LJP-oriented retrieval. Sampling high-quality optimized queries and their corresponding search trajectories is challenging, as relying solely on unguided high-temperature rollouts is both inefficient and constrained by the model's initial capabilities. We therefore heuristically optimize queries as seeds, improving the efficiency of trajectory generation. Furthermore, we summarize rollout experience into rubrics and use them to guide multi-round iterative self-evolution. Iteratively performing rubric optimization and rubric-guided RL enables the model to surpass its initial performance ceiling. End-to-end performance on extensive benchmarks demonstrates the effectiveness of query optimization on LJP. Comparisons with direct SFT followed by RL demonstrate the effectiveness of rubric guidance. Evolving rubrics further outperform fixed rubrics, confirming the benefits of self-evolution.

papers.title: Real alternative Daugavet property without Daugavet property in a separable complex Banach space
papers.abstract: We construct a separable complex Banach space whose underlying real space has the alternative Daugavet property, although the complex space fails the Daugavet property, thereby answering an open question posed by Kadets, Martin, and Paya in 2006.

papers.title: Bug2Scenario: Root-Cause-Preserving Test Scenario Amplification for Autonomous Driving Software
papers.abstract: Simulation-based fuzzing exposes autonomous driving system (ADS) failures by repeatedly mutating and executing scenarios, but converting one failure into reusable regression scenarios remains difficult. Such variants test whether the mechanism persists after software changes, for example by varying weather or actor placement while retaining a collision's actor-route conflict. We present Bug2Scenario, a root-cause-guided post-fuzzing framework. From scenario data, traces, and oracle evidence, it extracts a root-cause pattern. An LLM proposes semantic variations over actors, missions, routes, and weather. Deterministic rules construct DriveFuzz-compatible scenarios. Execution evidence and manual review assess preservation. Separating these responsibilities prevents fluency, syntax, or recurring labels from masquerading as causal evidence. Under matched seeds, six LLM backbones, candidate budget, and execution pipeline, Bug2Scenario improves strict preservation by 6.7 percentage points (p=0.104; not significant) and boundary-inclusive preservation by 10.6 points (p=0.011). Feedback helps some initially unsuccessful seeds yield a strictly preserved candidate. Seed-level stopping then avoids further API calls and simulator runs. Remaining failures reflect actor-placement constraints, simulator instability, and incomplete or conflicting causal evidence. Bug2Scenario thus produces reliable ADS regression assets. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/YgcCoder/Bug2Sce.

authors.name: Jingyu Zhang
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Liaoning

papers.title: Floer theory on based loops and fundamental groups of Lagrangians in $\mathbb{C}^n$
papers.abstract: We obtain new constraints on the topology of Lagrangian submanifolds in the standard symplectic vector space $\mathbb{C}^n$ using Floer theory on the based loop space, generalizing a theorem of Fukaya-Irie. In particular, we show that non-trivial connected sums of closed, spin, aspherical manifolds of even dimensions do not admit Lagrangian embeddings into $\mathbb{C}^n$. A feature of the proof is that the obstructedness of the Floer theory is used to constrain the fundamental group of the Lagrangian.

papers.title: Growing One's AI Tools: A Paradigm of Practice-Grown Tools
papers.abstract: Professionals have long used software built for them by others. This article reports the growth of a professional computer-assisted interpreting (CAI) tool built by its own user, a conference interpreter without programming training. Drawing on an eight-week version-controlled record with telemetry from 133 logged sessions and over 20,000 recognized utterances, the article traces how real conference work drove the tool through 62 commits and six versions. The record shows capabilities deployed on the day their need appeared and one strategy change that cut median end-to-end delay by over a third within one afternoon. The article then proposes the paradigm of practice-grown tools, defined by the shift from using to growing, the co-evolution of tool and practice through breakdown and repair, bounded local computation, and an assessment corollary, and it formulates three propositions toward tool-inclusive assessment of practitioners, from tool-making literacy to a compute-standardized format for certifying what they and their tools achieve together.

authors.name: Zeming Zhao
authors.institution: Second Hospital of Hebei Medical University

papers.title: Barrier-State-Based Safe Navigation in Complex Environments Using Look-Ahead Safety Corridors
papers.abstract: Safe navigation in cluttered environments requires a safety representation that captures the available motion space along the planned path. A single local safe region may restrict progress through narrow passages and continuous turns. This paper presents a planning-guided look-ahead safety corridor framework for barrier-state-based navigation. Local safe convex polytopes are constructed around collision-free seeds along the forward reference path. Their facet constraints are combined using softmin, and the local functions are fused using softmax with entropy-based adaptive compensation. The resulting safe set remains within the union of the local polytopes while reducing the shrinkage caused by fixed compensation. A Poisson boundary-value problem then defines a differentiable interior safety field while preserving the prescribed corridor boundary. This field is embedded into the robot dynamics through one geometric barrier state. We establish sufficient conditions for corridor invariance based on barrier-state boundedness and active-corridor validity. Navigation simulations cover cluttered layouts, narrow passages, and moving obstacles. A differential-drive ground vehicle further demonstrates navigation through narrow passages and among obstacles absent from the prior map.

authors.name: Yunlin Wei
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Fangfei Li
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Betti Sequences of Four-Generated Non-Almost-Symmetric Nearly Gorenstein Numerical Semigroup Rings
papers.abstract: Let $S$ be a minimally four-generated numerical semigroup that is nearly Gorenstein but not almost symmetric, and let $R=k[S]$ over an arbitrary field $k$. We prove that the defining ideal of $R$ has four or five minimal generators when $R$ has Cohen--Macaulay type two, and exactly six when it has type three. Thus the total Betti sequence over the four-variable polynomial presentation ring is one of $$(1,4,5,2),\quad (1,5,6,2),\quad (1,6,8,3),$$ and all three possibilities occur. The type-three argument uses a canonical-ideal exact sequence, a chain-level comparison on $\operatorname{Tor}$, and a codimension-three Gorenstein reduction. The resulting classification gives an affirmative answer, over every field, to Moscariello and Strazzanti's Question 4.3 on four-generated nearly Gorenstein numerical semigroups that are not almost symmetric.

papers.title: Accessibility of collapsed Anosov flow
papers.abstract: We prove that every $C^1$ collapsed Anosov flow on a closed three-manifold with non-virtually-solvable fundamental group is accessible. No transitivity or nonwandering assumption is required, and the collapsing map need not satisfy the strong-collapse conditions. We also prove that every three-dimensional collapsed Anosov flow for which no positive iterate is a discretized Anosov flow is accessible.

papers.title: ProcessPrefBench: Evaluating Cross-Task Transfer of Individual Process Preferences from Naturalistic Human-AI Interaction
papers.abstract: In natural human-AI dialogue, users' corrections, requests, and self-descriptions carry reusable signals about how they want work to be done. These signals reveal individual process preferences, user-specific standards for evidence, depth, analytical focus, procedure, and delivery. We ask whether a preference revealed in one dialogue can shape an assistant's later answer when the task does not restate it. ProcessPrefBench uses three months of natural dialogues from two knowledge workers to build 66 source-target cases separately judged for source evidence and target applicability. Sources are preselected, so the benchmark tests application rather than retrieval. We test three models with target-only, full-history, and distilled-preference prompts. Target-specific 0-2 rubrics score preference realization, and a task gate flags severe failures. Compared with target-only prompting, full-history and imperative distilled-preference prompting raise preference realization by 0.204 and 0.244 points on the 0-2 scale, respectively, with no reliable advantage from distillation. Fabricated-evidence failures rise from 5.8% under target-only prompting to 10.1% under full-history and 10.4% under imperative prompting. ProcessPrefBench highlights a tension in learning from dialogue, where drawing on prior interactions can improve preference realization yet also invite fabricated evidence. We hope it helps build assistants that honor a user's process preferences without sacrificing factual reliability.

papers.title: Observability and stabilizability for Grushin-Type parabolic equations in the whole space
papers.abstract:
We study observability and stabilization for the whole-space Grushin heat equation $$ \partial_t u-\Delta_\gamma u=0,\qquad \Delta_\gamma:=\Delta_x+|x|^{2\gamma}\Delta_y,\qquad (t,x,y)\in(0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m,\quad \gamma>0. $$ For product sets $E=E_1\times E_2$, we identify three observability regimes in which thickness, distance from the degeneracy set $\{x=0\}$, and local density near that set play different roles.
  (i) In the subcritical regime $0<\gamma<1$, the observability inequality holds for every $T>0$ if and only if both $E_1$ and $E_2$ are thick; hence $T_{\min}(E)=0$.
  (ii) At the critical exponent $\gamma=1$, if $E_2=\mathbb{R}^m$ and $E_1\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is thick, we determine the exact minimal observable time: $$ T_{\min}(E)=\frac{a_{\mathrm{ess}}(E_1)^2}{2n},\qquad a_{\mathrm{ess}}(E_1):=\operatorname*{ess\,inf}_{x\in E_1}|x|. $$ Thus, the threshold depends on the essential distance of $E_1$ from the degeneracy set.
  (iii) In the supercritical regime $\gamma>1$, we consider $n=1$, $E_2=\mathbb{R}^m$ and thick sets $E_1\subset\mathbb{R}$. If $a_{\mathrm{ess}}(E_1)>0$, observability fails for every $T>0$, so that $T_{\min}(E)=+\infty$. If $a_{\mathrm{ess}}(E_1)=0$, observability depends on the density of $E_1$ near $0$, measured by $$ D_{E_1}(r):=\log\!\left(\frac{2r}{|E_1\cap(-r,r)|}\right),\qquad L_{E_1}:=\limsup_{r\downarrow0}r^2D_{E_1}(r). $$ If $L_{E_1}=0$, then $T_{\min}(E)=0$; if $0<L_{E_1}<\infty$, a finite sufficient observation time exists. Moreover, observability at time $T$ requires $$ \limsup_{r\downarrow0}r^{2(1+\gamma)/(\gamma-1)}D_{E_1}(r)\le C_{T,\gamma}. $$
  In contrast, for every $\gamma>0$, exponential and complete stabilizability hold if and only if both $E_1$ and $E_2$ are thick. The stabilization criterion is therefore independent of $\gamma$.

papers.title: Data Center Agglomeration and Power Infrastructure Capacity in the United States
papers.abstract: The continuous expansion of digital infrastructure, especially data centers, has imposed unprecedented, geographically concentrated stress on existing power grids. However, rigorous causal evidence quantifying how these facilities reshape local power-infrastructure supply remains limited. This study builds a comprehensive county-level US panel dataset spanning 2010-2024, uniquely integrating individual data center building footprints and power-plant additions. To mitigate endogeneity and high-dimensional confounding, this study deploys Double Machine Learning with five-fold cross-fitting, conditioning on county and year fixed effects alongside regional socioeconomic covariates. Baseline estimation identifies a significant positive causal effect robust across multiple rigorous specifications. The result holds following 1%-99% winsorization that downweights mega-clusters including Loudoun County: growth in data-center floor area drives meaningful increases in nearby power-generation capacity (ATE=1.982, P=0.000, CI: [1.25, 2.72]). Outcomes remain statistically significant using a one-year lagged treatment to address reverse causality, and are stable under state-level fixed-effect alternatives. An event-study framework augmented with historical agglomeration controls validates clear parallel trends and detects a sharp causal spike at t = 3, matching typical utility-scale grid-construction lead times. A placebo test further verifies these causal estimates cannot emerge from random chance. Substantial regional heterogeneity emerges: strong positive impacts concentrate in the West, while significant negative displacement-related effects appear within resource-constrained Northeastern counties. These results deliver timely insights for urban planners and energy regulators, stressing the importance of forward-looking grid-capacity investment to support ongoing digital transformation.

papers.title: TandemBench: Benchmarking Decision Models for Multi-Agent Collaboration
papers.abstract: Decision models choose among predefined options in tasks such as routing and action selection. In multi-agent collaboration, a decision determines how members divide work, exchange resources, and act in parallel. We introduce TandemBench, a benchmark of 1,200 questions in multi-agent cooking scenarios where coordination choices affect goal completion. Models receive complete global information and candidate team plans, with reference answers established through execution and exact search. Models select an optimal team plan and, in paired variants that retain or remove it, judge whether better arrangements exist beyond the supplied options. We evaluate 40 native decision models and compare them with 10 general-purpose language models. The best native decision model achieves 62.50% decision accuracy. Native decision models remain close to chance in optimality verification. Paired tests reveal that some report better alternatives regardless of whether an optimal plan is already present. These findings show that team-plan decision accuracy alone can conceal systematic errors in judging whether the supplied options contain an optimal arrangement. The dataset and evaluation code are publicly available at https://github.com/lililibaohang/TandemBench.

papers.title: Critical one-arm probabilities for metric-graph loop soups in dimensions $d\ge3$
papers.abstract:
We study the critical Brownian loop soup on the metric graph $\widetilde{\mathbb Z}^d$. Using a new unified approach, we determine the one-arm probability up to multiplicative constants in all dimensions $d\ge3$. In particular, at the upper critical dimension $d_c=6$, we show that the one-arm probability is comparable to $r^{-2}(\log r)^{\frac12}$, and moreover, with high probability a box of radius $r$ contains on the order of $\log r$ macroscopic clusters, each with volume of order $r^4(\log r)^{-\frac12}$.
  For $d\ne6$, we recover the one-arm estimates of Cai and Ding, $r^{-(d-2)/2}$ for $d=3,4,5$ and $r^{-2}$ for $d>6$ (arXiv:2406.02397; Probab. Theory Relat. Fields, 2025), and the three-dimensional estimate of Drewitz, Pr\'evost and Rodriguez (Probab. Theory Relat. Fields, 2026). Our proof adapts the entropy method of Dewan and Muirhead (Probab. Theory Relat. Fields, 2023) to the loop-soup setting. This yields a renormalization inequality for the one-arm probability, from which we derive the upper bounds.
  Independently, Rodriguez, Shi, and Zhang (arXiv:2611.05357) have recently used a closely related entropy approach to recover the one-arm estimates for $d>6$ and improve the upper bound for $d=6$. They also announce the same sharp one-arm estimate for $d=6$ in forthcoming work.

authors.name: Yifan Gao
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: OSD-JSCC: Neural Joint Source-Channel Coding with One-Step Diffusion
papers.abstract: Neural joint source-channel coding (JSCC) enables efficient image transmission over noisy channels, yet distortion-optimized approaches often produce blurry reconstructions. While diffusion priors can enhance visual fidelity, their iterative sampling incurs substantial decoding latency. To address this limitation, we propose OSD-JSCC, an SNR-adaptive JSCC framework with a single diffusion step. Specifically, OSD-JSCC transmits pretrained variational autoencoder (VAE) latents through an SNR-conditioned JSCC codec and incorporates two key designs. First, we introduce a stochastic diffusion-state interface that enables the JSCC decoder to predict a Gaussian diffusion state rather than a clean latent, while extracting image-specific semantic tokens. The sampled diffusion state preserves spatial structure and provides a good initialization for one-step refinement, whereas the semantic tokens, together with an SNR token, guide the reconstruction process. Second, we develop SNR-conditioned feature modulation and adaptive timestep selection to jointly adapt latent transmission and diffusion refinement to varying channel conditions. Furthermore, we adopt a three-stage training strategy with low-rank adaptation (LoRA) to efficiently adapt the pretrained diffusion prior to the JSCC task. Extensive experiments on Kodak and CLIC2020 demonstrate that OSD-JSCC achieves superior perceptual quality and decoding efficiency. Compared with existing diffusion-based JSCC baselines, OSD-JSCC reduces LPIPS by approximately 43% on Kodak and 53% on CLIC2020, while achieving up to a 50.6$\times$ reduction in decoding latency.

papers.title: Uniform localization and boundary corrections for two-node quiver Coulomb branches
papers.abstract: We construct simple coherent classes and compute their normalized difference operators for the two-node quiver Coulomb branch with gauge group $GL_1\times GL_2$ and $m-1$ framing columns at the second node. The first magnetic charge is fixed at zero. For every $m\geq1$, every support $(n,-1)$ with $n\geq1$, and every integral electric twist, we prove that termwise saturation of the matter Koszul complex gives the simple intermediate extension. A graded normalization formula expresses its localization on every stratum as a finite binomial shuffle sum.
